    • main: block force pushes and deletion, require a linear history. With a single maintainer pushing to it; with more, require a pull request and the status checks of CI (Lint and type check, Unit and integration tests (3.11) … (3.14), End-to-end, Package, Audit dependencies, Docs) too.
    • Tags v*: block updates and deletion (a published version must never move), and only the repository's admins create them (a second ruleset, so that their bypass is for creating only).
  • Environments:
    • testpypi: deployment tags v*, required reviewer: you (nothing is published, not even to TestPyPI, until you say so).
    • pypi: deployment tags v*, required reviewer: you (the approval before PyPI).
    • github-pages: created when Pages is enabled; deployment branch main, from which the Docs workflow deploys every version.
  • Pages: source "GitHub Actions". The Docs workflow keeps a site per version in the gh-pages branch, which its first run creates: dev for main, X.Y for each release.
  • Security: Dependabot alerts and security updates, secret scanning with push protection, private vulnerability reporting (SECURITY.md points there), code scanning (CodeQL and Scorecard upload their results).

docs.title: 3. Trusted publishers
docs.text:
Before the first release the project doesn't exist on the indexes: add a pending publisher on TestPyPI and on PyPI:

Field TestPyPI PyPI PyPI project name fastapi-alcazaba fastapi-alcazaba Owner nonodev96 nonodev96 Repository fastapi-alcazaba fastapi-alcazaba Workflow release.yml release.yml Environment testpypi pypi

No API token is created or stored anywhere: the workflow proves its identity with OIDC.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
1. Move the Unreleased notes of CHANGELOG.md under ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD and merge to main; wait for CI.

  2. Tag the merge commit on main and push the tag:

    git switch main && git pull
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z

  3. The Release workflow:

    1. checks that the tag is a version on main and runs every suite;
    2. builds the sdist and the wheel (the version comes from the tag, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit);
    3. generates the CycloneDX SBOM and validates it;
    4. signs: GitHub attestations of build provenance (SLSA) and of the SBOM, plus a Sigstore bundle per file;
    5. waits for your approval in the testpypi environment, publishes to TestPyPI and installs that version in a clean environment (smoke test);
    6. waits for your approval in the pypi environment, then publishes to PyPI with PEP 740 attestations;
    7. creates the GitHub release with the distributions, the SBOM, the provenance, the Sigstore bundles and the notes of that version from the changelog;
    8. runs the Docs workflow, which publishes the documentation of the release as X.Y, with the latest alias that the root of the site leads to.

Pre-releases (vX.Y.ZrcN, aN, bN) stop after TestPyPI and become GitHub pre-releases, with no documentation of their own. They take the changelog section of the version they lead to (v0.1.0rc1 → ## [0.1.0]), which can still say Unreleased: a first rc tries the whole pipeline without spending the version.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
• Nothing reaches PyPI until you approve it: reject the deployment and fix.
  • A version can't be uploaded twice. Published something broken? Yank it on PyPI (it stays installable only when pinned exactly) and release X.Y.Z+1.
  • Don't move or reuse a tag that was released.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: Only the latest release of fastapi-alcazaba gets security fixes.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text:
Please don't open a public issue. Report it privately through GitHub's security advisories for this repository, with:

  • the affected version and backend,
  • how to reproduce it (a minimal app is ideal),
  • the impact you expect.

You'll get an answer within a week. Once a fix is released, the advisory is published with credit to you, unless you prefer otherwise.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In scope: anything that lets a request read another user's cached data, write or poison entries, run code, or exhaust the server through the cache; and anything that lets a client get past a rate limiter, or use up someone else's budget, other than by having several IPv4 addresses, IPv6 /64 networks or identities. The same goes for the other tools: getting another client's response through an idempotency key or a request run twice, a lock held by two processes while their renewals work, a revoked token accepted or a one-time code guessed beyond its attempts, a header injected or a body over the limit accepted by the middlewares, errors leaked by the health checks, an exclusive scheduled job run twice for one tick while the backend works, and a call let through an open circuit breaker.

Out of scope: problems that need write access to the backend when no signing_key or encryption_key is configured, reading the backend when no encryption_key is configured (the README explains when each key is needed), and denial of service of the backend itself.

docs.title: Supply chain
docs.text: Releases are built and published from GitHub Actions with PyPI trusted publishing (no API tokens) and carry PyPI attestations. The workflows pin every action to a commit and are checked with zizmor.

docs.title: Verifying a release
docs.text:
Every release is signed with Sigstore by the GitHub Actions workflow that built it: there's no key to trust, only the identity of the workflow (nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba, .github/workflows/release.yml, the tag). Replace X.Y.Z below with the version. The tools, in a virtual environment of their own:

python3 -m venv verify && verify/bin/pip install pypi-attestations sigstore

docs.title: What PyPI serves
docs.text:
PyPI keeps the PEP 740 attestations published with each file:

verify/bin/pypi-attestations verify pypi \
  --repository https://github.com/nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba \
  pypi:fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: GitHub attestations
docs.text:
Build provenance (SLSA v1) and SBOM attestations, for any copy of the files:

gh attestation verify fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl --repo nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba
gh attestation verify fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl --repo nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba \
  --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom

The release carries the provenance too, fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.intoto.jsonl (the Sigstore bundle of the attestation, one JSON line): with it, gh attestation verify doesn't ask GitHub for it, and checks the repository's name as the certificate recorded it when the release was built.

gh attestation verify fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl --repo nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba \
  --bundle fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.intoto.jsonl

docs.title: Sigstore bundles of the GitHub release
docs.text:
Each file of the release but the provenance has a .sigstore.json bundle next to it:

verify/bin/sigstore verify github fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl \
  --bundle fastapi_alcazaba-X.Y.Z-py3-none-any.whl.sigstore.json \
  --repository nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba --ref refs/tags/vX.Y.Z --trigger push

docs.title: The SBOM
docs.text:
fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.5) lists every runtime dependency, with every extra, at the versions installing it resolved to when it was released, with their licences and the hashes of their files. Scan it for known vulnerabilities:

osv-scanner scan --sbom fastapi-alcazaba-X.Y.Z.cdx.json

docs.title: About
docs.text: About Alcazaba: what guides its design, its license, and where its name comes from.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Secure defaults: anything that could serve one user's data to another, trust data read from the backend, or let a client get around a protection is opt-in, and documented.
  • One package, a folder per tool: each tool in fastapi_alcazaba.<tool>, its main class importable from fastapi_alcazaba. The tools share a backend, a circuit breaker, the metrics and the error format, instead of each bringing its own.
  • Optional dependencies: FastAPI, Pydantic and typing-extensions are all Alcazaba requires. Each backend or integration is an extra, and the code that needs it imports it only when it's used.
  • Every change tested: a bug fix comes with a test that fails without it, and the documentation's examples are apps that the tests run.
  • A careful supply chain: new dependencies only when they're worth it, and never a release younger than three days.

docs.title: License and credits
docs.text:
Apache License 2.0: see LICENSE and NOTICE.

An alcazaba is the walled citadel of an Andalusian city, like those of Almería, Málaga or the Alhambra: walls around what matters, and gates that only let the right things in. The logo is one of its walls, crowned with pointed merlons, whose horseshoe arch opens on a bolt: safe, and fast.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Each example is a small, complete FastAPI app in the repository's examples/ folder, written the way the tools are meant to be used in production, and tested with the library on every change. They keep their state in memory so that they run without any server; in production, Redis or Valkey lets every process share it. Only the background work needs one.

  • A browser app

    Server-side sessions, CSRF protection and security headers for a cookie-based app.

  • API keys, tokens and codes

    Keys stored as digests with scopes, one-time login codes and revoked tokens.

  • Passkeys

    A site without passwords: sign-ups and logins by passkey, and the devices each user is logged in on.

  • Second factor

    An authenticator app after the password, recovery codes, and a recent code to delete the account.

  • Accounting

    Searches and tokens metered per tenant, held to its plan, each charge a record for billing.

  • Audit trail

    Who changed or deleted which account, refusals included, signed and chained.

  • Authentication strategies

    An app per strategy: JWTs, logins with GitHub, sessions, bearer tokens, SAML single sign-on and API keys; and three of them on one app.

  • Authorization

    A newsroom whose Casbin policy says who reads, writes, publishes and grants roles, a team's documents whose Cedar policies decide by their attributes, and a shop whose refunds Open Policy Agent decides, asked over the network.

  • Background work

    Scheduled jobs, a leader among processes and a task queue on Redis streams.

  • Checking uploads

    The real type of a file from its bytes, size and pixel limits, and safe names.

  • Errors and observability

    Problem details, request IDs in logs and responses, deadlines and health checks.

  • Idempotency keys

    A retried payment gets the first response instead of charging twice.

  • Operations

    Maintenance mode, feature flags and circuit breakers, switched at runtime.

  • Pagination

    An app per strategy, from page numbers to scrolls and streams; and a catalogue cached three ways.

  • Rate and concurrency limits

    Requests per client and per user, shared budgets, and at most N expensive calls at a time.

  • Response cache

    Shared entries for public pages, private ones per user, invalidation by tag and get_or_set.

  • Webhooks in and out

    Signed webhooks received without replays, and sent to user URLs without SSRF.

docs.title: Running them
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository, each one starts with uvicorn:

git clone https://github.com/nonodev96/fastapi-alcazaba.git
cd fastapi-alcazaba
make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.cache.main:app

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs to try its endpoints from the browser. The keys and secrets they need come from environment variables, with a throwaway value for trying them out: set real ones in production.

docs.title: Accounting
docs.text:
Accounting Tenant to Your app: acme: GET /search. Your app to Counters: +1 search, if under 3. Counters to Your app: 3 of 3. Your app to Tenant: 200, a record for billing. Tenant to Your app: acme: GET /search. Your app to Counters: +1 search, if under 3. Counters to Your app: no: 3 of 3. Your app to Tenant: 429, at midnight. Each tenant held to its plan, every charge recorded. Tenant Your app Counters acme: GET /search +1 search, if under 3 3 of 3 200, a record for billing acme: GET /search +1 search, if under 3 no: 3 of 3 429, at midnight Each tenant held to its plan, every charge recorded What it's for: what each tenant uses per period, held to its plan's quotas, with a record of every charge for billing.

An API that meters what each tenant uses, holds it to its plan, and records every charge for billing. FastAPIAccounting charges each search before it runs, and the tokens of each summary when it answers; GET /usage tells the tenant what it has left.

Each tenant has an API key and a plan: acme-key (Acme, the free plan: 3 searches a day and 50 tokens a month) and globex-key (Globex, the pro plan: searches without a limit and 10,000 tokens a month).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.accounting.main:app

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Acme searches three times today; the responses say what's left, and the fourth gets a 429 until midnight, UTC:

$ curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search?q=ore" -H "X-API-Key: acme-key"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
ratelimit: "searches";r=0;t=43491
ratelimit-policy: "searches";q=3;w=86400

["Oregano"]

$ curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search?q=oli" -H "X-API-Key: acme-key"
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
ratelimit: "searches";r=0;t=43491
ratelimit-policy: "searches";q=3;w=86400
retry-after: 43491
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Quota exceeded"}

Globex, on the pro plan, has no limit, and no RateLimit headers:

$ curl "http://127.0.0.1:8000/search?q=oli" -H "X-API-Key: globex-key"
["Olive oil","Olives"]

A summary takes the tokens it used, known only when it answers. Acme's second one starts with 18 tokens left and uses 32, which it's charged: the quota is checked when a request starts. The next one gets a 402, a plan to upgrade:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/summaries -H "X-API-Key: acme-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text": "Olive oil is pressed from olives, the fruit of the olive tree, and keeps for two years in the dark."}'
{"summary":"Olive oil is pressed from olives, the fruit of the olive tree,","tokens":32}

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/summaries -H "X-API-Key: acme-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text": "Olives."}'
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
ratelimit: "tokens";r=0;t=2549091
ratelimit-policy: "tokens";q=50
retry-after: 2549091
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Quota exceeded"}

What Acme has used, and when each meter starts again:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/usage -H "X-API-Key: acme-key"
{"searches":{"used":3,"limit":3,"remaining":0,"period":"2026-11-01","resets":"2026-11-02T00:00:00+00:00"},"tokens":{"used":64,"limit":50,"remaining":0,"period":"2026-11","resets":"2026-12-01T00:00:00+00:00"}}

Every charge is a line of JSON on the server's output, for billing to add up:

{"id":"165fc663b5ff4376a6cb76959df5df3a","time":"2026-11-01T11:55:09.237011+00:00","subject":"acme","meter":"tokens","amount":32,"period":"2026-11","request_id":null,"trace_id":null,"method":"POST","route":"/summaries"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The plan decides: each quota's limit is a function of the tenant (searches_of, tokens_of), which reads its plan; None from it is no limit.
  • Charged before, or as it goes: a search is charged before it runs, checked and counted at once, so concurrent searches never go past the quota. The tokens are added by the endpoint (usage.add(...)) and charged when it answers.
  • 429 or 402: over the searches of the day, try again tomorrow; over the tokens of the month, a plan to upgrade (status=402).
  • Counters and records: the counters, in the backend, hold the quotas; the records, one per charge with an id to count it once, are what billing adds up, and they're written even when the backend is down.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/accounting/main.py
"""An API that meters what each tenant uses, holds it to its plan, and records every charge for
billing.

    uvicorn examples.accounting.main:app

Each tenant has an API key and a plan. The free plan gets 3 searches a day and 50 tokens of
summaries a month; the pro plan, searches without a limit and 10,000 tokens a month.

- `GET /search` takes one search of the day; over the plan, a 429 until the day ends.
- `POST /summaries` takes the tokens it used (a word, a token here), counted when it answers;
  over the plan, a 402: a plan to upgrade.
- `GET /usage` tells the tenant what it has used and has left this period.

Every charge is a usage record, logged as a line of JSON by `fastapi_alcazaba.accounting.usage`:
what billing adds up. The counters live in the cache's backend: InMemoryBackend here, so that
it runs without a server. Production uses Redis or Valkey, so that every process shares them.
"""

import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, Security
from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from fastapi_alcazaba import Cache
from fastapi_alcazaba.accounting import FastAPIAccounting, Metering, Quota
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend

Plan = Literal["free", "pro"]
# Stands in for your tenants and their API keys (a database, with the keys stored as digests).
TENANTS: dict[str, tuple[str, Plan]] = {
    "acme-key": ("acme", "free"),
    "globex-key": ("globex", "pro"),
}
PLAN_OF = dict(TENANTS.values())
#: What each plan allows: None for no limit.
SEARCHES: dict[Plan, int | None] = {"free": 3, "pro": None}
TOKENS: dict[Plan, int] = {"free": 50, "pro": 10_000}


class Summary(BaseModel):
    summary: str
    tokens: int


class Text(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(max_length=10_000)


class Meter(BaseModel):
    used: int
    limit: int | None
    remaining: int | None
    period: str
    resets: str


api_key = APIKeyHeader(name="X-API-Key", auto_error=False)


async def current_tenant(key: Annotated[str | None, Security(api_key)]) -> str | None:
    """The tenant of the request's API key; None without one (a 401)."""
    if key is None:
        return None
    if key not in TENANTS:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid API key")
    return TENANTS[key][0]


def searches_of(tenant: str) -> int | None:
    return SEARCHES[PLAN_OF[tenant]]


async def tokens_of(tenant: str) -> int:
    # A coroutine function: where the plan comes from your database.
    return TOKENS[PLAN_OF[tenant]]


accounting = FastAPIAccounting(
    subject=current_tenant,
    quotas=[
        Quota("searches", limit=searches_of, period="day"),
        Quota("tokens", limit=tokens_of, status=402),  # a month
    ],
    challenge="ApiKey",
)


# The usage records, to the console: a log pipeline would keep them for billing.
records = logging.getLogger("fastapi_alcazaba.accounting.usage")
records.setLevel(logging.INFO)
if not records.handlers:
    records.addHandler(logging.StreamHandler())


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    Cache(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="accounting").install(application)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/search", dependencies=[Depends(accounting.meter("searches"))])
async def search(q: str) -> list[str]:
    """One search of the day, charged before it runs."""
    return [name for name in ("Olive oil", "Olives", "Oregano") if q.lower() in name.lower()]


@app.post("/summaries")
async def summarize(
    text: Text,
    usage: Annotated[Metering, Depends(accounting.meter("tokens", amount=None))],
) -> Summary:
    """The tokens it uses are charged when it answers: only then are they known."""
    words = text.text.split()
    summary = " ".join(words[:12])
    usage.add(len(words) + len(summary.split()))  # what it read and what it wrote
    return Summary(summary=summary, tokens=usage.total)


@app.get("/usage")
async def read_usage(
    request: Request,
    tenant: Annotated[str | None, Depends(current_tenant)],
) -> dict[str, Meter]:
    """What the tenant has used of each meter this period, and what its plan leaves."""
    if tenant is None:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Not authenticated", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "ApiKey"})
    meters = {}
    for meter in ("searches", "tokens"):
        report = await accounting.usage(tenant, meter, request=request)  # the app's cache
        meters[meter] = Meter(
            used=report.used,
            limit=report.limit,
            remaining=report.remaining,
            period=report.period,
            resets=report.resets.isoformat(),
        )
    return meters


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Audit trail
docs.text:
Audit trail Admin to Your app: PUT /accounts/u3/role. Your app to Audit trail: account.role.change ✓. Your app to Admin: 200. Admin to Your app: DELETE /accounts/u3, sam. Your app to Audit trail: account.delete, denied. Your app to Admin: 403 Forbidden. Admin to Your app: GET /audit/verify. Your app to Admin: no event altered. Who did what, when and from where: signed and chained. Admin Your app Audit trail PUT /accounts/u3/role account.role.change ✓ 200 DELETE /accounts/u3, sam account.delete, denied 403 Forbidden GET /audit/verify no event altered Who did what, when and from where: signed and chained What it's for: a record of who did what to which resource, allowed or not, that nobody can alter without it showing.

An admin API whose sensitive actions leave an audit trail: who changed which account's role or deleted it, whether they were allowed to, and the request it came from. FastAPIAudit writes each event when the endpoint ends, as a line of JSON on standard output, signed and chained to the previous one, and verify_audit_trail checks that none was altered or removed.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.audit.main:app

The events are signed: set AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, and keep it from the people whose actions are recorded. The example has three accounts: u1 (Ada, an admin, token ada-token), u2 (Sam, support, token sam-token) and u3 (Vic, a viewer).

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Ada makes Vic support:

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/u3/role -H "Authorization: Bearer ada-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"role": "support"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: 2b78a9c373054722779a26e2904a6b0a

{"id":"u3","email":"vic@example.com","role":"support"}

and the server's standard output gets the event, the request's ID included:

{"id":"eec01d5969ce42deb8787aae473acfa1","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.175075+00:00","action":"account.role.change","outcome":"success","actor":"u1","resource":"account:u3","reason":null,"status":null,"request_id":"2b78a9c373054722779a26e2904a6b0a","trace_id":null,"method":"PUT","route":"/accounts/{account_id}/role","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{"from":"viewer","to":"support"},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":1,"previous":null,"signature":"13c0da20bf320784d6a1a4698cd91574b2b97b8c8e818668ef104aa9cc65fb34"}

Sam, who isn't an admin, tries to delete Vic's account; then someone without a token does:

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/u3 -H "Authorization: Bearer sam-token"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Only admins can do this"}

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/accounts/u3
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Both are recorded as denied: Sam's with who he is and why, the anonymous one with the account it was after. Each event carries the signature of the one before:

{"id":"2221174595b04a82b269e441227a0933","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.178638+00:00","action":"account.delete","outcome":"denied","actor":"u2","resource":"account:u3","reason":"support, not admin","status":403,"request_id":"14500c6bd67ff72fd772d584cdb9fee5","trace_id":null,"method":"DELETE","route":"/accounts/{account_id}","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":2,"previous":"13c0da20bf320784d6a1a4698cd91574b2b97b8c8e818668ef104aa9cc65fb34","signature":"41ea75d99c58cd8618d1f3e5bad140e52f270929beb26cc811a53c9bee452aa6"}
{"id":"41a26fffb4bd41df9d8c370da2d9cc7d","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.182414+00:00","action":"account.delete","outcome":"denied","actor":null,"resource":"account:u3","reason":"fastapi.exceptions.HTTPException","status":401,"request_id":"028f8c3e03768e47f6f85152ba18cf48","trace_id":null,"method":"DELETE","route":"/accounts/{account_id}","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":3,"previous":"41ea75d99c58cd8618d1f3e5bad140e52f270929beb26cc811a53c9bee452aa6","signature":"be3d2ff3bb03a6642e81027d5ac0edc75356ab880f9434b2ba88a089ff91eda5"}

A sign-in with a wrong password records which account was tried, never the password:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sessions -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ada@example.com", "password": "hunter2"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-request-id: b544c2688f7bd5b8cc1c58784a44ca68

{"detail":"Wrong e-mail or password"}

{"id":"6c10e3d17e1d4e3d9442c181ebc6e525","time":"2026-10-26T15:44:27.185776+00:00","action":"session.create","outcome":"denied","actor":"u1","resource":null,"reason":"wrong password","status":null,"request_id":"b544c2688f7bd5b8cc1c58784a44ca68","trace_id":null,"method":"POST","route":"/sessions","client":"127.0.0.1","details":{},"stream":"1c33125463a71ecb","sequence":4,"previous":"be3d2ff3bb03a6642e81027d5ac0edc75356ab880f9434b2ba88a089ff91eda5","signature":"9124fbfed7d210bde4fe27842947404b9c711d86acd3b6e1469e0af09d97c7d0"}

Ada checks the trail (and that check is recorded too, as audit.read). An event altered, forged or removed would be listed in problems:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/audit/verify -H "Authorization: Bearer ada-token"
{"events":4,"problems":[]}

GET /audit/events lists the last events, for admins only.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The audit dependency comes first: declared before current_account, it's entered before the authentication runs, so the 401s that one answers are recorded too, with the account from the path (resource="account:{account_id}").
  • Who acts goes in before the check: require_admin sets entry.actor and then refuses, so Sam's 403 is recorded with Sam, and entry.reason says why.
  • How it ended: a 401 or a 403 is denied, any other exception a failure (a 404 for an account that doesn't exist), with its type and status but never its message.
  • No secrets: the sign-in records the account and the reason, not the e-mail address typed (it may be a password typed in the wrong field) nor the password. Had they gone in details, the password would have been [redacted], by its key.
  • A stream of its own: the events go to the logger fastapi_alcazaba.audit.events, which writes them to standard output without the app's log format, one line each, for the log pipeline to ship to storage that can't be rewritten (an S3 bucket with Object Lock, a SIEM).
  • Signed and chained: each event carries an HMAC of its content and the signature of the previous one of its process. verify_audit_trail finds an event altered, forged or missing in the middle; it can't tell that the newest were removed, nor stop whoever has the key.
  • Correlation: the x-request-id a user quotes leads to the event (request_id), and with OpenTelemetry the event's trace_id leads to the request's trace.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/audit/main.py
"""An admin API whose sensitive actions leave an audit trail: who did what to which account,
whether it was allowed, and the request it came from.

    uvicorn examples.audit.main:app

- Changing a role and deleting an account are recorded when they end: `success`, `denied` (a 401
  without a token, a 403 for someone who isn't an admin) or `failure` (a 404 for an account that
  doesn't exist). Reading the trail is recorded too.
- Each event is a line of JSON on standard output, apart from the app's other logs, for the log
  pipeline to ship to storage that can't be rewritten. The events are signed and chained:
  `GET /audit/verify` says whether any was altered or removed.
- A sign-in records its outcome with `audit.log`, never the password, and the response carries
  the request ID that the event holds.

The accounts are a dict in memory here, a table in your database; the last events are kept in
memory too, for `/audit/events` and `/audit/verify`.
"""

import hmac
import logging
import secrets
import sys
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAudit
from fastapi_alcazaba.audit import AuditEntry, LoggingAuditSink, MemoryAuditSink, verify_audit_trail
from fastapi_alcazaba.observability import RequestIDMiddleware


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    # Signs the events: AUDIT_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process,
    # kept from the people whose actions are recorded: with it, they could rewrite the trail.
    audit_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()

# The trail: one line of JSON per event on standard output, without the app's log format.
trail_log = logging.getLogger("fastapi_alcazaba.audit.events")
trail_log.addHandler(logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout))
trail_log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
trail_log.propagate = False

recent = MemoryAuditSink(maxlen=1000)
audit = FastAPIAudit([LoggingAuditSink(trail_log), recent], signing_key=settings.audit_signing_key)

Role = Literal["admin", "support", "viewer"]


class Account(BaseModel):
    id: str
    email: str
    role: Role


class RoleChange(BaseModel):
    role: Role


class SignIn(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str


# Stands in for your users table, its password hashes and your access tokens.
PASSWORDS = {"ada@example.com": "correct horse", "sam@example.com": "battery staple"}
TOKENS = {"ada-token": "u1", "sam-token": "u2"}


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    application.state.accounts = {
        "u1": Account(id="u1", email="ada@example.com", role="admin"),
        "u2": Account(id="u2", email="sam@example.com", role="support"),
        "u3": Account(id="u3", email="vic@example.com", role="viewer"),
    }
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
# The ID of each request goes in its events and in the response: support finds the event a
# user's complaint is about.
app.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware)


def accounts(request: Request) -> dict[str, Account]:
    return request.app.state.accounts  # type: ignore[no-any-return]


Accounts = Annotated[dict[str, Account], Depends(accounts)]


async def current_account(connection: HTTPConnection) -> Account:
    """Stands in for your authentication: the account whose bearer token the request carries."""
    scheme, _, token = connection.headers.get("authorization", "").partition(" ")
    account_id = TOKENS.get(token) if scheme.lower() == "bearer" else None
    account = connection.app.state.accounts.get(account_id)
    if account is None:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Not authenticated", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return account  # type: ignore[no-any-return]


Me = Annotated[Account, Depends(current_account)]


def require_admin(entry: AuditEntry, me: Account) -> None:
    """Who acts goes in the event before the check: a refusal is recorded with its actor."""
    entry.actor = me.id
    if me.role != "admin":
        entry.reason = f"{me.role}, not admin"
        raise HTTPException(403, "Only admins can do this")


def find(all_accounts: dict[str, Account], account_id: str) -> Account:
    account = all_accounts.get(account_id)
    if account is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such account")
    return account


# The audit dependency goes before the authentication (Me): it records what that one refuses,
# a 401, with the account from the path.
changing_role = audit.action("account.role.change", resource="account:{account_id}")
deleting = audit.action("account.delete", resource="account:{account_id}")
reading_trail = audit.action("audit.read")


@app.put("/accounts/{account_id}/role")
async def change_role(
    account_id: str,
    change: RoleChange,
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(changing_role)],
    me: Me,
    all_accounts: Accounts,
) -> Account:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    account = find(all_accounts, account_id)
    entry.details.update({"from": account.role, "to": change.role})
    account.role = change.role
    return account


@app.delete("/accounts/{account_id}", status_code=204)
async def delete_account(
    account_id: str,
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(deleting)],
    me: Me,
    all_accounts: Accounts,
) -> None:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    entry.details["email"] = find(all_accounts, account_id).email
    del all_accounts[account_id]


@app.post("/sessions")
async def sign_in(form: SignIn, request: Request, all_accounts: Accounts) -> dict[str, str]:
    account = next((a for a in all_accounts.values() if a.email == form.email), None)
    expected = PASSWORDS.get(form.email, "")
    # Compared in constant time, and the same answer whatever was wrong.
    if account is None or not hmac.compare_digest(form.password.encode(), expected.encode()):
        await audit.log(
            "session.create",
            outcome="denied",
            actor=account.id if account else None,
            reason="unknown e-mail" if account is None else "wrong password",
            request=request,
        )
        raise HTTPException(401, "Wrong e-mail or password")
    await audit.log("session.create", actor=account.id, request=request)
    token = next(token for token, owner in TOKENS.items() if owner == account.id)
    return {"access_token": token, "token_type": "bearer"}


@app.get("/audit/events")
async def audit_events(
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(reading_trail)],
    me: Me,
    limit: int = 20,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    return [event.to_dict() for event in list(recent.events)[-limit:]]


@app.get("/audit/verify")
async def audit_verify(
    entry: Annotated[AuditEntry, Depends(reading_trail)],
    me: Me,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_admin(entry, me)
    events = list(recent.events)
    return {
        "events": len(events),
        "problems": verify_audit_trail(events, settings.audit_signing_key),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: API keys, revoked tokens and one-time codes
docs.text:
API keys, tokens and codes Owner to Your app: POST /login/code, e-mail. Your app to Owner: a code, by e-mail. Owner to Your app: POST /login, the code. Your app to Owner: an access token. Owner to Your app: POST /api-keys, token. Your app to Owner: acme_…, shown once. Program to Your app: GET /orders, X-API-Key. Your app to Program: 200, its owner's orders. Codes for people, keys for programs, only digests stored. Owner Your app Program POST /login/code, e-mail a code, by e-mail POST /login, the code an access token POST /api-keys, token acme_…, shown once GET /orders, X-API-Key 200, its owner's orders Codes for people, keys for programs, only digests stored What it's for: people sign in with a one-time code and get a revocable token; their programs call the API with keys that are stored only as digests.

An orders API for machine clients. Their owners sign in with a code sent by e-mail (OneTimeCodes), rate-limited per address with a FastAPIRateLimiter, and get an access token that logging out revokes (TokenBlocklist). With it they create API keys for their programs (FastAPIAPIKeys): shown once, stored only as digests, with scopes and an expiry date.

No JWT library is involved: a small stand-in signs the same claims (sub, jti, iat, exp) with HMAC. A real app decodes its JWTs with its library and passes the blocklist the same claims.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.auth.main:app

Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, OTP_SECRET, API_KEY_PEPPER and TOKEN_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process. Without them each start makes up throwaway ones, and every token, code and key stops working when the app restarts.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Ask for a code. The answer is the same whether the address has an account or not:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login/code -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com"}'
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted

{"detail":"If the address has an account, a code is on its way."}

The code never travels in a response. The stand-in for the e-mail service prints it in the server's terminal:

E-mail to ana@example.com: Your login code is 531060. It expires in 5 minutes.

Trade it for an access token. It works once:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com", "code": "531060"}'
{"access_token":"eyJzdWIiOiJhbmFAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20i...","expires_in":900}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com", "code": "531060"}'
{"detail":"Invalid or expired code"}

Three codes per address every 15 minutes, wherever the requests come from. The fourth:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/login/code -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ben@example.com"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
retry-after: 558

{"detail":"Too Many Requests"}

With the token, create two API keys, one that can only read. Each key is shown this once:

$ TOKEN=eyJzdWIiOiJhbmFAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20i...
$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scopes": ["orders:read"]}'
{"id":"j2aelpaafvjfr6ry","key":"acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa","scopes":["orders:read"],"expires_at":"2027-01-24T10:55:42.303928Z"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scopes": ["orders:read", "orders:write"]}'
{"id":"mxkvocavyp6ek2dc","key":"acme_mxkvocavyp6ek2dc_hnkk5z2qld3qoc7wv5sq2aq4qrvblr7mc4bucwfvbzj5uzea6d5a","scopes":["orders:read","orders:write"],"expires_at":"2027-01-24T10:55:42.306965Z"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"scopes": ["admin"]}'
{"detail":[{"type":"enum","loc":["body","scopes",0],"msg":"Input should be 'orders:read' or 'orders:write'",...}]}

Each endpoint asks for the scope it needs:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_mxkvocavyp6ek2dc_hnkk5z2qld3qoc7wv5sq2aq4qrvblr7mc4bucwfvbzj5uzea6d5a" \
    -d '{"item": "Olive oil", "quantity": 2}'
{"item":"Olive oil","quantity":2}

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa" \
    -d '{"item": "Olive oil", "quantity": 2}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Insufficient scope"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa"
[{"item":"Olive oil","quantity":2}]

A missing, malformed, unknown, wrong or expired key gets the same 401:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders -H "X-API-Key: acme_nottherightkey"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: APIKey

{"detail":"Invalid API key"}

Revoking a key takes effect at once in the process that handles it:

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys/j2aelpaafvjfr6ry -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders \
    -H "X-API-Key: acme_j2aelpaafvjfr6ry_gqdbzjcgz6dwuwtbmltalhn7cern6vjogztxgthxqwofrt6z2aaa"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: APIKey

{"detail":"Invalid API key"}

Logging out revokes the access token, which would otherwise work for 15 minutes more:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Invalid or expired token"}

/logout/everywhere revokes every token of the user issued before the current second, and gives the session that asked a new one. With two tokens of Ana's, $LAPTOP and $PHONE, issued a second or more before:

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/logout/everywhere -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHONE"
{"access_token":"eyJzdWIiOiJhbmFAZXhhbXBsZS5jb20i...","expires_in":900}

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api-keys \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LAPTOP" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"scopes": ["orders:read"]}'
401

$PHONE gets a 401 as well, and the new token a 201.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Nothing that opens a door is stored in clear: the api_keys table holds an HMAC of each key with the pepper, which lives outside the database, so a copy of the database can't even test a guess. The cache's backend holds HMACs of the codes and digests of the revoked token ids.
  • The code only goes by e-mail, and /login/code answers the same for any address. The e-mail is sent after the response (BackgroundTasks), so the time it takes doesn't tell either.
  • The rate limit on codes is per address, wherever the requests come from (identifier returns the same for everybody; the address is the key of hit). Each new code replaces the previous one and its five guesses, so this limit is what bounds the guesses at an account: 3 codes × 5 guesses every 15 minutes.
  • The token check is one dependency, token_claims: it decodes the token and asks the blocklist with its jti, and with its sub and iat for /logout/everywhere. With a JWT library you only change the decoding; set the blocklist's leeway to the one your library tolerates after exp.
  • Revoking a key deletes its row and calls keys.forget(), because cache_ttl=30 keeps looked-up records in each process: the other processes stop accepting it within 30 seconds.
  • Scopes are an enum: users can only grant their keys scopes the API knows.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth/main.py
"""An orders API for machine clients, whose owners sign in with a code sent by e-mail.

    uvicorn examples.auth.main:app

People sign in with a one-time code (`OneTimeCodes`) and get an access token, which logging out
revokes (`TokenBlocklist`). With it they create API keys (`FastAPIAPIKeys`) for their programs:
shown once, stored as digests, with scopes and an expiry date. The programs call `/orders` with
the key in `X-API-Key`.

Revoked tokens, codes and rate-limit counters live in the cache's backend: in memory here, Redis
or Valkey in production, so that every process sees them at once. Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY,
OTP_SECRET, API_KEY_PEPPER and TOKEN_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every
process, in the environment or a .env file.
"""

import base64
import dataclasses
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, Body, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAPIKeys, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import OneTimeCodes, TokenBlocklist
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit import FastAPIRateLimiter, too_many_requests

TOKEN_LIFETIME = 15 * 60  # seconds


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file: secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    each, the same in every process."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    otp_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    api_key_pepper: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    token_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class Scope(StrEnum):
    # An enum: users can only grant scopes the API knows.
    ORDERS_READ = "orders:read"
    ORDERS_WRITE = "orders:write"


@dataclasses.dataclass
class APIKeyRow:
    """A row of the api_keys table: everything about a key but the key itself."""

    id: str
    owner: str
    digest: str
    scopes: frozenset[str]
    expires_at: datetime | None


class Order(BaseModel):
    item: str = Field(max_length=100)
    quantity: int = Field(ge=1, le=100)


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users = {"ana@example.com", "ben@example.com"}
        self.api_keys: dict[str, APIKeyRow] = {}
        self.orders: dict[str, list[Order]] = {}  # by owner


async def send_email(to: str, text: str) -> None:
    """Stands in for the e-mail service: prints the message, for you to read the code in the
    server's terminal, and keeps it for the tests."""
    outbox.append((to, text))
    print(f"E-mail to {to}: {text}", flush=True)


class Claims(BaseModel):
    sub: str
    jti: str
    iat: int
    exp: int


class AccessTokens:
    """Stands in for a JWT library, which this example doesn't depend on: a JWT's claims, signed
    with HMAC-SHA256. A real app issues and decodes its JWTs with PyJWT or joserfc, and gives the
    blocklist their `jti`, `sub`, `iat` and `exp` just like here."""

    def __init__(self, key: SecretStr) -> None:
        self.key = key.get_secret_value().encode()

    def sign(self, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        return hmac.digest(self.key, payload, "sha256").hex().encode()

    def issue(self, subject: str) -> str:
        now = int(time.time())
        jti = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
        claims = Claims(sub=subject, jti=jti, iat=now, exp=now + TOKEN_LIFETIME)
        payload = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(claims.model_dump_json().encode())
        return (payload + b"." + self.sign(payload)).decode()

    def decode(self, token: str) -> Claims | None:
        """The claims of a token signed here that hasn't expired; None otherwise."""
        payload, _, signature = token.encode().partition(b".")
        if not hmac.compare_digest(signature, self.sign(payload)):
            return None
        claims = Claims.model_validate_json(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload))
        return claims if claims.exp > time.time() else None


db = Database()
outbox: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
access_tokens = AccessTokens(settings.token_secret)
blocklist = TokenBlocklist()  # in FastAPICache's backend
codes = OneTimeCodes(secret=settings.otp_secret)  # 6 digits, 5 minutes, 5 guesses
# Per address, wherever the requests come from. Each code replaces the previous one and its
# guesses, so this is what bounds the guesses at an account: 3 codes x 5 guesses per 15 minutes.
code_requests = FastAPIRateLimiter(times=3, minutes=15, identifier=lambda _: "")


async def load_key(key_id: str) -> APIKeyRow | None:
    return db.api_keys.get(key_id)


# A distinctive prefix, for secret scanners to spot leaked keys. Each process keeps the records
# it looked up for 30 s: a revocation takes up to that long to reach the other processes.
keys = FastAPIAPIKeys(load_key, pepper=settings.api_key_pepper, prefix="acme", cache_ttl=30)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the state. Signed: revocations
    # planted in the backend are ignored.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="auth", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)


async def token_claims(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(bearer)],
) -> Claims:
    """The claims of the request's access token; a 401 if it's missing, expired or revoked."""
    claims = access_tokens.decode(credentials.credentials) if credentials else None
    if claims is None or await blocklist.is_revoked(
        claims.jti, subject=claims.sub, issued_at=claims.iat
    ):
        raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid or expired token", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return claims


TokenClaims = Annotated[Claims, Depends(token_claims)]


class CodeRequest(BaseModel):
    email: str = Field(max_length=254)


class Login(CodeRequest):
    code: str = Field(max_length=10)


class Token(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    expires_in: int = TOKEN_LIFETIME


@app.post("/login/code", status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED)
async def send_code(form: CodeRequest, request: Request, tasks: BackgroundTasks) -> dict[str, str]:
    """E-mail a login code. The answer doesn't tell whether the address has an account."""
    email = form.email.lower()
    if (wait := await code_requests.hit(request, key=email)) is not None:
        too_many_requests(request, wait)
    tasks.add_task(email_code, email)  # after the response: its timing doesn't tell either
    return {"detail": "If the address has an account, a code is on its way."}


async def email_code(email: str) -> None:
    if email in db.users:
        code = await codes.issue(email, purpose="login")
        await send_email(email, f"Your login code is {code}. It expires in 5 minutes.")


@app.post("/login")
async def login(form: Login) -> Token:
    email = form.email.lower()
    if not await codes.verify(email, form.code, purpose="login"):
        raise HTTPException(400, "Invalid or expired code")
    return Token(access_token=access_tokens.issue(email))


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def logout(claims: TokenClaims) -> None:
    """Refuse this token from now on, until it would have expired anyway."""
    await blocklist.revoke(claims.jti, expires_at=claims.exp)


@app.post("/logout/everywhere")
async def logout_everywhere(claims: TokenClaims) -> Token:
    """Refuse every token of the user issued before this second (a lost laptop, a new password),
    and give this session a new one, which stays valid."""
    await blocklist.revoke_subject(claims.sub, ttl=TOKEN_LIFETIME)
    return Token(access_token=access_tokens.issue(claims.sub))


class NewKey(BaseModel):
    id: str
    key: str
    scopes: list[str]
    expires_at: datetime | None


@app.post("/api-keys", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def create_key(
    claims: TokenClaims,
    scopes: Annotated[set[Scope], Body(embed=True, min_length=1)],
) -> NewKey:
    """A new key, shown this once: only a digest of it is stored."""
    expires_at = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=90)
    key, record = keys.generate(scopes=scopes, expires_at=expires_at)
    db.api_keys[record.id] = APIKeyRow(owner=claims.sub, **dataclasses.asdict(record))
    return NewKey(id=record.id, key=key, scopes=sorted(scopes), expires_at=expires_at)


@app.delete("/api-keys/{key_id}", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def revoke_key(key_id: str, claims: TokenClaims) -> None:
    row = db.api_keys.get(key_id)
    if row is None or row.owner != claims.sub:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such key")
    del db.api_keys[key_id]
    keys.forget(key_id)  # refused at once by this process, by the others within cache_ttl


@app.get("/orders")
async def list_orders(
    key: Annotated[APIKeyRow, Depends(keys.require(Scope.ORDERS_READ))],
) -> list[Order]:
    return db.orders.get(key.owner, [])


@app.post("/orders", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_order(
    order: Order,
    key: Annotated[APIKeyRow, Depends(keys.require(Scope.ORDERS_WRITE))],
) -> Order:
    db.orders.setdefault(key.owner, []).append(order)
    return order


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Background work
docs.text:
Background work Client to Your app: POST /users. Your app to Worker: queue: welcome e-mail. Your app to Client: 201, at once. Worker: mailer down: retries. Worker: then a dead letter. Client to Your app: admin: requeue it. Your app to Worker: the task, again. Worker: ✓ e-mail sent. Work after the response: retried, kept, never lost. Client Your app Worker POST /users queue: welcome e-mail 201, at once mailer down: retries then a dead letter admin: requeue it the task, again ✓ e-mail sent Work after the response: retried, kept, never lost What it's for: work that goes on after the response (e-mails, reports, relays), run in one of the processes, retried while it fails, and kept when it can't be done.

A sign-up service whose work goes on after the response. POST /users saves the user and hands the welcome e-mail to FastAPITaskQueue, which runs it in the background, in whichever process takes it, and retries it while the e-mail provider is down. Out of retries, it becomes a dead letter, which an admin endpoint lists and puts back in the queue once the provider is back. FastAPIScheduler ends the trials on the hour and sends the team a sign-up report on weekdays at 8:00 in Madrid, each run in one process only. And FastAPILeader has one process relay the outbox, the events saved with the users, to the message broker; if that process stops, another one takes over.

Unlike the other examples, it needs Redis or Valkey: the tasks live in Redis streams that every process shares. They're signed with the cache's signing_key, so a task planted or altered in Redis is refused and never runs.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository, with Redis or Valkey running (a throwaway one: docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:6379:6379 valkey/valkey:8):

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0
export CACHE_SIGNING_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
uvicorn examples.background.main:app

Every process needs the same CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, or the tasks that one seals are refused by the others. The admin routes take Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN; without ADMIN_TOKEN the token is random, and they stay closed. The database, the e-mail provider and the broker are stand-ins in the process's memory, so try it with one process. With a real database, run as many as you need.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
A sign-up answers at once, before the welcome e-mail goes out. A moment later the queue has sent it:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/users -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "ana@example.com", "name": "Ana"}'
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json

{"id":1,"email":"ana@example.com","name":"Ana","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:58.884780Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":false}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/1
{"id":1,"email":"ana@example.com","name":"Ana","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:58.884780Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":true}

What the process is doing: it's the leader, no task is pending, and the jobs run next (in UTC) on the hour and at 8:00 in Madrid, which is 7:00 UTC in winter time. Without the token, a 401:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/background -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
{"leader":true,"pending_tasks":0,"next_runs":{"end-trials":"2026-10-26T12:00:00Z","signup-report":"2026-10-27T07:00:00Z"}}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/background
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Now the e-mail provider goes down. A sign-up still answers at once, and its task waits for a retry:

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/mailer?down=true" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/users -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"email": "luis@example.com", "name": "Luis"}'
{"id":2,"email":"luis@example.com","name":"Luis","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:59.914617Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":false}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/background -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
{"leader":true,"pending_tasks":1,"next_runs":{"end-trials":"2026-10-26T12:00:00Z","signup-report":"2026-10-27T07:00:00Z"}}

The retries come 10 s, 20 s, 40 s… apart, with jitter. After the sixth attempt, here about four minutes later, the task is a dead letter. It says which task failed and the type of its error, never its arguments nor the error's message, which may hold personal data:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/dead-letters -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
[{"id":"1793014866323-0","reason":"failed","task":"send-welcome-email","task_id":"dd4b818df71444c0af26dcc01e59ce10","error":"examples.background.main.MailerUnavailable","attempts":6,"failed_at":"2026-10-26T11:41:06.323669Z"}]

Once the provider is back, the dead letter goes back in the queue, and the e-mail goes out:

$ curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/simulate/mailer?down=false" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/dead-letters/requeue \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
{"requeued":1}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/2
{"id":2,"email":"luis@example.com","name":"Luis","created_at":"2026-10-26T11:36:59.914617Z","plan":"trial","welcomed":true}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/dead-letters -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
[]

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• At least once, so safe to run twice: a worker that dies after sending the e-mail, before it can say so, has its task run again elsewhere. send_welcome_email checks first whether the e-mail already went out.
  • Only an ID goes through Redis: the task takes the user's ID and reads the address when it runs, so no personal data waits in Redis, and the log line names the user by ID too.
  • Sealed tasks: the cache's signing_key signs every task and binds it to its queue. Without it, whoever can write to Redis could run the tasks with arguments of their choosing.
  • Each run in one process: the scheduler's ticks are the same in every process (every(hours=1) is on the hour, UTC), and only one of them runs each tick. The cron job has a time zone, so the report is at 8:00 in Madrid in summer time and in winter time.
  • One relay, never two: two processes relaying the outbox would publish every event twice. The leader's loop is cancelled if its process stops leading, and starts in the next leader. An event leaves the outbox only once it's published: a crash in between publishes it again, and never loses it.
  • Started and stopped with the app: async with queue, leader, scheduler in the lifespan. They stop in the reverse order: the jobs first, the queue last, giving its running tasks 10 s.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/background/main.py
"""Background work for a sign-up service: a task queue, scheduled jobs and a leader, on Redis.

    export REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0
    export CACHE_SIGNING_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
    export ADMIN_TOKEN=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
    uvicorn examples.background.main:app

Every process runs the three tools, started and stopped with the app, and they share the work
through Redis: in production, run as many processes as you need (`--workers`, more machines).
Here the database is a stand-in in each process's memory, so try it with one.

- FastAPITaskQueue: POST /users hands the welcome e-mail to the queue, which retries it while the
  e-mail provider is down. After its last retry it's a dead letter, which the admin endpoints
  list and put back in the queue once the provider is back.
- FastAPIScheduler: trials end on the hour, and the team gets a sign-up report on weekdays at
  8:00 in Madrid; each run happens in one process only.
- FastAPILeader: one process relays the outbox (the events saved with the users) to the message
  broker; if it stops, another one takes over.

The e-mail provider is a stand-in too: `PUT /admin/simulate/mailer?down=true` makes it fail, to
watch retries and dead letters. The admin routes take `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`. The
variables above can go in a .env file instead.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from redis.asyncio import Redis

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache, FastAPILeader, FastAPIScheduler, FastAPITaskQueue
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.redis import RedisBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.background import DeadLetter

logger = logging.getLogger("signup")


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    redis_url: str = "redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0"  # rediss://, with a password, in production
    # Every process needs the same key, or the tasks one seals are refused by the others. The
    # random default only suits a single process that you try out locally.
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    # Unset: a random token nobody knows, so the admin endpoints stay closed.
    admin_token: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()
REPORT_TO = "team@example.com"
TRIAL = timedelta(days=14)
RELAY_INTERVAL = 1.0  # seconds between looks at the outbox


def redis_client() -> Redis:
    """The connection to Redis or Valkey."""
    return Redis.from_url(settings.redis_url)


class MailerUnavailable(Exception):
    """The e-mail provider didn't answer."""


class Mailer:
    """Stands in for the e-mail provider's client."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.available = True
        self.sent: list[tuple[str, str]] = []  # (to, subject)

    async def send(self, to: str, subject: str) -> None:
        if not self.available:
            raise MailerUnavailable("503 Service Unavailable")
        self.sent.append((to, subject))


@dataclass
class User:
    id: int
    email: str
    name: str
    created_at: datetime
    plan: str = "trial"
    welcomed: bool = False


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database, which every process shares in a real app."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[int, User] = {}
        self.outbox: list[dict[str, Any]] = []  # events, saved in the same transaction as the data

    def add_user(self, email: str, name: str, created_at: datetime | None = None) -> User:
        user = User(len(self.users) + 1, email, name, created_at or datetime.now(UTC))
        self.users[user.id] = user
        self.outbox.append({"type": "user.created", "user_id": user.id})
        return user


class Broker:
    """Stands in for the message broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ...)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.published: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    async def publish(self, event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.published.append(event)


db, mailer, broker = Database(), Mailer(), Broker()
# FastAPICache's backend, set in the lifespan.
queue = FastAPITaskQueue()
scheduler = FastAPIScheduler()
leader = FastAPILeader("outbox-relay")


# Six attempts over about five minutes (10 s, 20 s, 40 s... apart, with jitter), then a dead letter.
@queue.task(name="send-welcome-email", retries=5, backoff=10)
async def send_welcome_email(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Runs at least once, so it checks first whether the e-mail already went out."""
    user = db.users.get(user_id)
    if user is None or user.welcomed:  # deleted meanwhile, or a second run
        return
    await mailer.send(user.email, f"Welcome, {user.name}!")
    user.welcomed = True
    logger.info("Welcome e-mail sent to user %d", user_id)  # an ID, not the address


@scheduler.every(hours=1, name="end-trials")
async def end_trials() -> None:
    """On the hour (UTC): the users whose trial is over go to the free plan."""
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    for user in db.users.values():
        if user.plan == "trial" and user.created_at + TRIAL <= now:
            user.plan = "free"


@scheduler.cron("0 8 * * mon-fri", tz="Europe/Madrid", name="signup-report")
async def signup_report() -> None:
    """Weekdays at 8:00 in Madrid, in summer time and in winter time."""
    since = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1)
    count = sum(user.created_at >= since for user in db.users.values())
    await mailer.send(REPORT_TO, f"{count} sign-ups in the last 24 hours")


@leader.run
async def relay_outbox() -> None:
    """In the leader only: two processes would publish every event twice. It's cancelled if this
    process stops leading, and starts again in the next leader."""
    while True:
        while db.outbox:
            await broker.publish(db.outbox[0])
            db.outbox.pop(0)  # once it's out: a crash in between publishes it again, never loses it
        await asyncio.sleep(RELAY_INTERVAL)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    redis = redis_client()
    # Signed: a task planted or altered in Redis is refused and never runs.
    FastAPICache.init(RedisBackend(redis), prefix="signup", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    # Stopped in the reverse order: the jobs first, the queue last, giving its running tasks 10 s.
    async with queue, leader, scheduler:
        yield
    await redis.aclose()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class SignUp(BaseModel):
    email: str = Field(max_length=254, pattern=r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+$")
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)


@app.post("/users", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def sign_up(signup: SignUp) -> User:
    """The response doesn't wait for the e-mail provider, nor fails while it's down."""
    user = db.add_user(signup.email, signup.name)
    # Only the ID goes through Redis: no personal data there, and the task reads the address then.
    await queue.enqueue(send_welcome_email, user.id)
    return user


@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
async def get_user(user_id: int) -> User:
    if (user := db.users.get(user_id)) is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND)
    return user


def require_admin(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())],
) -> None:
    if not secrets.compare_digest(
        credentials.credentials.encode(), settings.admin_token.get_secret_value().encode()
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN)


admin = APIRouter(prefix="/admin", dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])


class Background(BaseModel):
    leader: bool
    pending_tasks: int
    next_runs: dict[str, datetime | None]


@admin.get("/background")
async def background() -> Background:
    """Whether this process leads, the tasks not done yet and when the jobs run next (UTC)."""
    return Background(
        leader=leader.is_leader,
        pending_tasks=await queue.pending(),
        next_runs={name: scheduler.next_run(name) for name in ("end-trials", "signup-report")},
    )


@admin.get("/dead-letters")
async def dead_letters() -> list[DeadLetter]:
    """The tasks out of retries, newest first: their name and error type, never their arguments."""
    return await queue.dead_letters()


@admin.post("/dead-letters/requeue")
async def requeue_dead_letters() -> dict[str, int]:
    """Once the cause is fixed: every dead letter back in the queue, with its attempts reset."""
    return {"requeued": await queue.requeue_dead_letters()}


@admin.put("/simulate/mailer", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def simulate_mailer(down: bool) -> None:
    """Only in this example: makes the e-mail provider fail, to watch retries and dead letters."""
    mailer.available = not down


app.include_router(admin)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: A browser app: sessions, CSRF and security headers
docs.text:
A browser app Browser to Your app: GET /. Your app to Browser: page, CSRF token, CSP. Browser to Your app: POST /cart, X-CSRF-Token. Your app to Sessions: the cart, in the session. Your app to Browser: 303 → /. Browser to Your app: another site's POST /logout. Your app to Browser: 403, cross-site. Sessions on the server; forms only from your own pages. Browser Your app Sessions GET / page, CSRF token, CSP POST /cart, X-CSRF-Token the cart, in the session 303 → / another site's POST /logout 403, cross-site Sessions on the server; forms only from your own pages What it's for: a server-rendered app whose sessions live on the server, whose forms only its own pages can send, and whose pages carry the security headers.

A small shop rendered on the server, with plain HTML and a few lines of JavaScript. Who signed in and the cart live in a server-side session (ServerSessionMiddleware): the cookie only carries a random id, which signing in replaces and signing out deletes, and 30 minutes without requests end it. CSRFMiddleware refuses what pages on other sites make the browser send, and with require_token=True also wants the page's token in a header. SecurityHeadersMiddleware and BodySizeLimitMiddleware add the security headers, with a Content-Security-Policy for the pages, and refuse large bodies. A FastAPIRateLimiter slows down password guessing.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.browser_app.main:app

Open http://localhost:8000 and sign in as ana, password correct horse battery staple.

The cookies are Secure: browsers only keep them from HTTPS sites and from http://localhost, which they treat as secure. Use localhost, not a LAN address, to try it over plain HTTP. In tests, give the client an https URL for the same reason: TestClient(app, base_url="https://testserver").

Set SESSION_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Without it each start makes up a throwaway one, and every session ends when the app restarts.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
curl keeps Secure cookies from localhost too, so a cookie jar plays the browser. The first page sets the CSRF token, in a cookie and in the page, and carries the security headers:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar http://localhost:8000/
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
vary: Cookie
set-cookie: __Host-csrftoken=QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=Lax
x-content-type-options: nosniff
x-frame-options: DENY
referrer-policy: no-referrer
cross-origin-opener-policy: same-origin
content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'

<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Shop</title><meta name="csrf-token" content="QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc"><script src="/app.js" defer></script></head><body><p><a href="/login">Sign in</a></p>...

No session yet: it's only created when there's something to keep. A form posted without the token is refused, even from the app's own page (Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin, as browsers send):

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/cart -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -d product=Figs
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Missing or invalid CSRF token"}

With the token in X-CSRF-Token, as app.js sends it, the cart gets a session:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/cart -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc" -d product=Figs
HTTP/1.1 303 See Other
location: /
set-cookie: __Host-session=ozlYn1TlYGLpFmUZlKT0eArPzN2hQZkbFLVVbPWV1II; Max-Age=28800; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
cache-control: no-store

Signing in gives the session a new id, with the same cart:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc" \
    -d username=ana --data-urlencode "password=correct horse battery staple"
HTTP/1.1 303 See Other
location: /
set-cookie: __Host-session=s4wi5n6b_DRAvO0aFKJ7gzK6lyPtWymwDfZ8Xqm8AJ0; Max-Age=28800; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

$ curl -b jar http://localhost:8000/
...<p>Signed in as ana.</p>...<h2>Cart</h2><ul><li>Figs: 1</li></ul></body></html>

The old id is worth nothing now, so one planted in the browser before signing in (session fixation) gives nothing away:

$ curl http://localhost:8000/ -H "Cookie: __Host-session=ozlYn1TlYGLpFmUZlKT0eArPzN2hQZkbFLVVbPWV1II"
...<p><a href="/login">Sign in</a></p>...

A page on another site can't sign the user out, even if it had the token:

$ curl -i -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/logout -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site" \
    -H "Origin: https://evil.example" -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'

{"detail":"Cross-site request refused"}

Signing out deletes the session from the backend: a copy of the cookie doesn't work either:

$ curl -i -c jar -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/logout -H "Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin" \
    -H "X-CSRF-Token: QkgoLDXsFG6SGZsxRY39XJJJWKwuVB1VQCAoC7HQIpc"
HTTP/1.1 303 See Other
location: /
set-cookie: __Host-session=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax

$ curl http://localhost:8000/ -H "Cookie: __Host-session=s4wi5n6b_DRAvO0aFKJ7gzK6lyPtWymwDfZ8Xqm8AJ0"
...<p><a href="/login">Sign in</a></p>...

Bodies over 64 KiB are refused before the app reads them:

$ head -c 100000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x > big.txt
$ curl -i -b jar -X POST http://localhost:8000/cart --data-binary @big.txt
HTTP/1.1 413 Content Too Large
x-content-type-options: nosniff

{"detail":"Request body too large"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The order of the middlewares: each one added wraps those before it. The session is the innermost; CSRF goes outside it, so a refused request never reads a session from the backend; the security headers are the outermost, so the 403s and 413s of the others get them too.
  • require_token=True needs JavaScript: the middleware reads the token from the X-CSRF-Token header, which a plain HTML form can't set, so app.js sends the forms with fetch, taking the token from the page's <meta> (request.state.csrf_token). An app whose forms must work without JavaScript leaves require_token off: the origin checks alone already stop CSRF in every current browser, login CSRF included.
  • A strict Content-Security-Policy for the pages: only the app's own script, no inline code (so the token goes in a <meta> and the script in its own file), no framing, forms only to the app. The JSON responses keep the default default-src 'none'. /docs is off: a site has no use for it, and its CDN scripts wouldn't pass the policy.
  • rotate_session at sign-in, clear_session at sign-out: the first defeats session fixation, the second makes a stolen cookie worthless at once. The __Host- prefix keeps a sibling subdomain from planting either cookie.
  • Small, escaped sessions: the cart only holds products of an enum, at most 10 of each, so a session can't outgrow max_size; everything that reaches the HTML goes through html.escape.
  • Passwords: a salted scrypt hash, computed in a thread (it's slow on purpose) and for unknown users too, so the time doesn't tell who has an account; five attempts a minute per address.

docs.title: The code
Response cache
docs.text:
Response cache Client to Your app: GET /products/1. Your app to Cache: miss: run it, store it. Your app to Client: 200, miss; stored. Client to Your app: GET /products/1. Cache to Your app: hit: the stored response. Your app to Client: 200, hit; ttl=600. Client to Your app: PUT /products/1. Your app to Cache: drop tag product:1. Computed once, served from the cache until it changes. Client Your app Cache GET /products/1 miss: run it, store it 200, miss; stored GET /products/1 hit: the stored response 200, hit; ttl=600 PUT /products/1 drop tag product:1 Computed once, served from the cache until it changes What it's for: an endpoint computed once and served from the cache, to everybody or to each user, until a change drops it.

A shop's catalogue and account pages behind @cache: product pages are the same for everybody and share one entry each, account pages depend on who asks and get entries of their own, an update drops the entries of a product by tag, and get_or_set caches what doesn't fit a decorator. Every entry is signed, so whoever can write to Redis can't plant one.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.cache.main:app

It keeps the entries in memory. To share them between processes, give it a Redis or Valkey and a signing key, the same in every process:

export REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0
export CACHE_SIGNING_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
uvicorn examples.cache.main:app --workers 4

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
