$ curl http://localhost:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
{"id":"1","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

When it expires, 15 minutes later, the refresh token gets a new pair, and is used up:

$ curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/token/refresh -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"refresh_token": "r1.HilC5JFTP0wGAQkfMyLpIw.0.TCpsBYBjfQlTsg2ZnfHjxFQx9sGDDPJ_-hdW9xR5PV4"}'
{"access_token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzNjYzMTQ2LCJleHAiOjE3OTM2NjQwNDYsImp0aSI6ImFUYzBKVHphOGl0dEFXYUxGU3h1blEiLCJpc3MiOiJodHRwOi8vbG9jYWxob3N0OjgwMDAiLCJhdWQiOiJodHRwOi8vbG9jYWxob3N0OjgwMDAvYXBpIiwic2lkIjoiSGlsQzVKRlRQMHdHQVFrZk15THBJdyJ9.9PvmHE-vAiYklyJi6prSek3qCgQ7x3KJqKiK5H8Ycj0","refresh_token":"r1.HilC5JFTP0wGAQkfMyLpIw.1.CcXRawc697P2f-imSUh3QVQ0EQmrbdttvw9VUoxvvj0","token_type":"bearer","expires_in":900,"refresh_expires_in":2591999,"session":"HilC5JFTP0wGAQkfMyLpIw"}

A refresh token that comes back after it was exchanged (10 seconds later, or older) was copied: the login ends, for whoever holds its tokens.

$ curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8000/token/refresh -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"refresh_token": "r1.HilC5JFTP0wGAQkfMyLpIw.0.TCpsBYBjfQlTsg2ZnfHjxFQx9sGDDPJ_-hdW9xR5PV4"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

{"detail":"Log in again"}

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/me -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzNjYzMTQ2LCJleHAiOjE3OTM2NjQwNDYsImp0aSI6ImFUYzBKVHphOGl0dEFXYUxGU3h1blEiLCJpc3MiOiJodHRwOi8vbG9jYWxob3N0OjgwMDAiLCJhdWQiOiJodHRwOi8vbG9jYWxob3N0OjgwMDAvYXBpIiwic2lkIjoiSGlsQzVKRlRQMHdHQVFrZk15THBJdyJ9.9PvmHE-vAiYklyJi6prSek3qCgQ7x3KJqKiK5H8Ycj0"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Logging out ends the login the same way: its access and refresh tokens are refused from then on.

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/token -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

Five tries a minute per address: the next one gets a 429, with the right password or not. After a few wrong ones:

$ curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8000/token -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"login": "octocat", "password": "guess"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
ratelimit: "5/60s";r=0;t=19
retry-after: 19

{"detail":"Too Many Requests"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Readable, not secret: the middle part of the token is its claims in base64, which anyone can read: {"sub":"1","iat":1793663146,"exp":1793664046,"jti":"n2ZBZetSbGurYMBbLAb1tg", "iss":"http://localhost:8000","aud":"http://localhost:8000/api","sid":"HilC5JFTP0wGAQkfMyLpIw"}. The signature only stops anyone from changing them: put nothing secret in a JWT.
  • Whose and for whom: issuer and audience go into each token and are checked on each request, so a token that another app signed with the same secret, or that the same identity provider issued for another app, is refused.
  • No lookup: the user's id is in sub, so verify loads the user without looking the token up. That's also why a token can't be taken back by deleting it: TokenBlocklist keeps the revoked ones, and the logins (sid) that ended, in the cache's backend, until they expire.
  • Short tokens, long logins: access tokens last 15 minutes; RefreshTokens keeps each login for 30 days (7 without a refresh), rotating its refresh token at each exchange. The backend keeps a record per login, never a refresh token: whoever reads it can't make one.
  • Passwords: kept as scrypt digests, compared in constant time, and unknown logins take as long as wrong passwords. FastAPIRateLimiter limits the tries per address.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/jwt_tokens.py
"""An API for scripts and apps: they log in with a password and get a JWT, which they send in
`Authorization: Bearer` for 15 minutes, and a refresh token, which gets them a new pair when it
expires, until they log out.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.jwt_tokens:app

`JWTStrategy` verifies the tokens the app issues: their signature, their expiry, who issued
them and for whom (`issuer`, `audience`), and that they weren't revoked (`TokenBlocklist`). The
token carries the user's id, so the app knows who sends it without looking the token up.
`RefreshTokens` rotates the refresh tokens: each one is used up when it's exchanged, and one used
twice (it was copied) ends the login.

Log in as octocat, with the password "correct horse battery staple". Set JWT_SECRET,
REFRESH_SECRET and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process,
in the environment or a .env file.
"""

import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuth, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import RefreshRefused, RefreshTokens, TokenBlocklist, TokenPair
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies.jwt import JWTStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit import FastAPIRateLimiter

TOKEN_LIFETIME = 900  # seconds: the refresh token gets a new one
DEMO_PASSWORD = "correct horse battery staple"  # noqa: S105  # octocat's, to try the example


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    base_url: str = "http://localhost:8000"
    jwt_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    refresh_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    login: str
    name: str | None = None


def password_digest(password: str, salt: bytes) -> bytes:
    """scrypt: slow on purpose, so that a stolen database gives the passwords away slowly."""
    return hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)


# What unknown logins are checked against, so that they take as long as wrong passwords.
UNKNOWN_SALT = secrets.token_bytes(16)
UNKNOWN_DIGEST = password_digest(secrets.token_urlsafe(), UNKNOWN_SALT)


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: one user, octocat, with the demo password."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users = {"1": User(id="1", login="octocat", name="The Octocat")}
        salt = secrets.token_bytes(16)
        self.passwords = {"octocat": ("1", salt, password_digest(DEMO_PASSWORD, salt))}

    def check_password(self, login: str, password: str) -> User | None:
        user_id, salt, digest = self.passwords.get(login, ("", UNKNOWN_SALT, UNKNOWN_DIGEST))
        if hmac.compare_digest(password_digest(password, salt), digest) and user_id:
            return self.users[user_id]
        return None


db = Database()

blocklist = TokenBlocklist()  # in FastAPICache's backend
auth = FastAPIAuth()
tokens = auth.use(
    JWTStrategy(
        settings.jwt_secret,
        issuer=settings.base_url,  # tokens of this app
        audience=f"{settings.base_url}/api",  # for this API: not another one's tokens
        blocklist=blocklist,  # revoked tokens are refused
        verify=lambda claims: db.users.get(claims["sub"]),
    )
)
# A login lasts 30 days, or 7 without a refresh; a refresh token used twice ends it.
refresh_tokens = RefreshTokens(tokens, secret=settings.refresh_secret, access_ttl=TOKEN_LIFETIME)
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("jwt"))]
# Five logins a minute per address: a script that guesses passwords soon gets 429s.
login_attempts = FastAPIRateLimiter(times=5, minutes=1)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process sees the logins and revoked tokens.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="jwt", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class Login(BaseModel):
    login: str = Field(max_length=100)
    password: str = Field(max_length=200)


class Refresh(BaseModel):
    refresh_token: str = Field(max_length=200)


@app.post("/token", dependencies=[Depends(login_attempts)])
async def log_in(form: Login) -> TokenPair:
    """Tokens for the user's scripts, for their login and password."""
    user = db.check_password(form.login, form.password)
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "Wrong login or password")
    return await refresh_tokens.issue(user.id)


@app.post("/token/refresh")
async def refresh(body: Refresh) -> TokenPair:
    """A new pair for the refresh token, which is used up."""
    try:
        return await refresh_tokens.exchange(body.refresh_token)
    except RefreshRefused:
        # Never say why: a thief would learn which of its tokens still work.
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "Log in again") from None


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    return user


@app.delete("/token", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def log_out(
    user: CurrentUser,
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(HTTPBearer())],
) -> None:
    """End the login of the request's token: its access and refresh tokens are refused."""
    del user  # checked by the JWT strategy: valid and not revoked
    claims = await tokens.decode(credentials.credentials)
    await refresh_tokens.revoke_session(claims["sid"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("jwt_tokens:app", reload=True)

docs.title: OAuth2Strategy
docs.text:
OAuth2Strategy Browser to Your app: GET /login/github. Your app to Browser: 302 → GitHub, state, PKCE. Browser to GitHub: log in at GitHub, allow the app. GitHub to Browser: 302 → callback ?code=…&state=… Browser to Your app: GET /auth/github/callback. Your app to GitHub: code + verifier → profile. Your app to Browser: session cookie, 303 /me. Logged in with GitHub: your app never sees the password. Browser Your app GitHub GET /login/github 302 → GitHub, state, PKCE log in at GitHub, allow the app 302 → callback ?code=…&state=… GET /auth/github/callback code + verifier → profile session cookie, 303 /me Logged in with GitHub: your app never sees the password What it's for: people log in with an account they already have (GitHub, Google…), and your app never sees their password.

People log in with their GitHub account: the authorization code flow with PKCE, then a session that remembers them. The strategy: OAuth2Strategy.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Create a GitHub OAuth app (GitHub's Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps) whose callback URL is http://localhost:8000/auth/github/callback. Then, from a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=... GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=...
uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.oauth2_login:app

Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY too (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Open the app at http://localhost:8000, not 127.0.0.1: GitHub only sends people back to the callback URL it knows.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
/login/github sends the browser to GitHub, with a random state and a PKCE challenge. The state and the PKCE verifier wait in a cookie, for the callback to check:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/login/github
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
location: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A8000%2Fauth%2Fgithub%2Fcallback&state=jXJcV-_O0q0_v9K2MfyEfeMjEah55SvgW9sSoO3rjmY&code_challenge=c19OME8_wXKNeiwWUU70d6uUfTS2mdbbKUgEioMybbI&code_challenge_method=S256&scope=read%3Auser
set-cookie: __Host-alcazaba-oauth2-github=jXJcV-_O0q0_v9K2MfyEfeMjEah55SvgW9sSoO3rjmY.iDVwXX46...; Max-Age=600; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
cache-control: no-store

Open http://localhost:8000/login/github in the browser. GitHub asks whether to let the app read your profile, then sends you back to the callback: the strategy checks the state, exchanges the code for a token and reads your profile, and the app starts a session and takes you to /me. For a GitHub user called octocat:

{"id":"github:583231","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Only on the callback: GitHubUser is the only dependency with the github strategy, and only the callback takes it. Elsewhere the strategy finds nobody, and the session tells who's there.
  • A login nobody can force on you: the callback is refused without the cookie that /login/github set, or with another state, so a link to the callback with someone else's code doesn't log you in as them.
  • The app owns its users: find_or_create_user turns GitHub's profile into a user of the app, created the first time. The session carries the app's user id, never GitHub's token.
  • CSRF: the session is a cookie, which browsers send by themselves; CSRFMiddleware refuses what other sites make them send, such as a form that posts to /logout.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/oauth2_login.py
"""Log in with GitHub: the authorization code flow with PKCE, then a session.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.oauth2_login:app

`/login/github` sends the browser to GitHub, which asks the user to let the app read their
profile and sends them back to the callback. There `OAuth2Strategy` checks the state, exchanges
the code for a token, reads the profile and calls `find_or_create_user`; the app keeps its own
user in a session (`SessionStrategy`), so GitHub isn't asked again on every request.

Create a GitHub OAuth app (Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps) whose callback URL is
http://localhost:8000/auth/github/callback, and set GITHUB_CLIENT_ID and GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET.
Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY too (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, in the
environment or a .env file. Open the app at http://localhost:8000: GitHub only sends people back
to the callback URL it knows.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuth, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import SessionStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies.oauth2 import OAuth2Strategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.security import CSRFMiddleware, ServerSessionMiddleware


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    base_url: str = "http://localhost:8000"
    github_client_id: str = "set GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"
    github_client_secret: SecretStr = SecretStr("set GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET")
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    login: str
    name: str | None = None


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, User] = {}


db = Database()


def find_or_create_user(tokens: dict[str, Any], profile: dict[str, Any] | None) -> User | None:
    """GitHub says who logged in: our user for that account, created the first time."""
    del tokens  # GitHub's access token: keep it to call GitHub on the user's behalf
    if profile is None:
        return None  # refuses the login
    user_id = f"github:{profile['id']}"
    if user_id not in db.users:
        db.users[user_id] = User(id=user_id, login=profile["login"], name=profile.get("name"))
    return db.users[user_id]


def load_user(user_id: str) -> User | None:
    return db.users.get(user_id)


auth = FastAPIAuth()
github = auth.use(
    OAuth2Strategy(
        name="github",
        authorization_url="https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize",
        token_url="https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token",  # noqa: S106  # a URL
        userinfo_url="https://api.github.com/user",
        client_id=settings.github_client_id,
        client_secret=settings.github_client_secret,
        redirect_uri=f"{settings.base_url}/auth/github/callback",
        scopes=["read:user"],
        verify=find_or_create_user,
    )
)
sessions = auth.use(SessionStrategy(load_user))
GitHubUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("github"))]
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("session"))]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the sessions.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="github", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware)
app.add_middleware(CSRFMiddleware)  # session cookies: refuse what other sites make browsers send


@app.get("/login/github")
async def log_in() -> RedirectResponse:
    """To GitHub's login page, which sends the user back to the callback."""
    return github.redirect()


@app.get("/auth/github/callback")
async def github_callback(request: Request, user: GitHubUser) -> RedirectResponse:
    """GitHub sends the user back here: the strategy checks the state, exchanges the code and
    reads the profile; the session remembers the user from now on."""
    sessions.login(request, user.id)
    return RedirectResponse("/me", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    return user


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def log_out(request: Request, user: CurrentUser) -> None:
    del user  # only to refuse requests without a session
    sessions.logout(request)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("oauth2_login:app", reload=True)

docs.title: OIDCStrategy
docs.text:
OIDCStrategy Browser to Your app: GET /login. Your app to Browser: 302, state, PKCE, nonce. Browser to Provider: log in at the provider. Provider to Browser: 302 → callback ?code=… Browser to Your app: GET /auth/callback. Your app to Provider: code + verifier → ID token. Your app: signature, iss, aud, nonce ✓. Your app to Browser: session cookie, 303 /me. The ID token verified: from the provider, for this app, this login. Browser Your app Provider GET /login 302, state, PKCE, nonce log in at the provider 302 → callback ?code=… GET /auth/callback code + verifier → ID token signature, iss, aud, nonce ✓ session cookie, 303 /me The ID token verified: from the provider, for this app, this login What it's for: logins with an OpenID Connect provider (Keycloak, Google, Entra ID…), whose ID token is verified before your code trusts its claims.

People log in with an OpenID Connect provider (Keycloak, Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta…): the authorization code flow with PKCE and a nonce, the ID token verified, then a session that remembers them. The strategy: OIDCStrategy.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Register the app at the provider, with the redirect URI http://localhost:8000/auth/callback. With Keycloak, in a realm: Clients → Create client, client authentication on, the standard flow, and that redirect URI. Then, from a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:8080/realms/example OIDC_CLIENT_ID=... OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=...
uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.oidc_login:app

Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY too (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. At start, the app reads the issuer's discovery document, for the provider's endpoints and keys: it doesn't start when the issuer doesn't answer, or its document is another issuer's.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:8000/login in the browser. /login sends it to the provider's login page, with a random state, a PKCE challenge and a nonce, which wait in a cookie for the callback (__Host-alcazaba-oauth2-oidc: the state, the PKCE verifier and the nonce). Against Keycloak 26.4, with a realm alcazaba at http://localhost:18090:

302 → http://localhost:18090/realms/alcazaba/protocol/openid-connect/auth
      ?response_type=code&client_id=alcazaba-example&redirect_uri=...%2Fauth%2Fcallback
      &state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256&scope=openid+email+profile&nonce=...

Log in at the provider. It sends you back to the callback, where the strategy checks the state, exchanges the code, verifies the ID token (Keycloak signs it with RS256, by a key of its JWKS) and calls find_or_create_user; the app starts a session and takes you to /me:

{"id":"http://localhost:18090/realms/alcazaba#165fb2e0-1057-4b2c-b927-2c0ca4369d08","email":"ana@example.com","name":"Ana Test"}

The same callback again (its code, from the browser's history) gets a 401: Keycloak refuses a code used once already.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The ID token is verified: its signature with the provider's keys, its issuer, its audience (this app), its expiry and the login's nonce, before find_or_create_user sees its claims. A token for another app, or from another login, is refused.
  • Users by issuer and subject: sub is unique and stable for each issuer; an e-mail address can change hands. An address the provider says nobody proved (email_verified: false) refuses the login.
  • Discovered at start: the endpoints and the keys come from the issuer, in the lifespan; the keys are fetched again when the provider rotates them.
  • Only on the callback: LoggedIn is the only dependency with the oidc strategy; the session tells who's there everywhere else, and CSRFMiddleware refuses what other sites make browsers send with its cookie.

docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/oidc_login.py

from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.security import CSRFMiddleware, ServerSessionMiddleware

    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    base_url: str = "http://localhost:8000"
    oidc_issuer: str = "http://localhost:8080/realms/example"
    oidc_client_id: str = "set OIDC_CLIENT_ID"

settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    email: str | None = None
    name: str | None = None


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, User] = {}


db = Database()


def find_or_create_user(claims: dict[str, Any], userinfo: dict[str, Any] | None) -> User | None:
    """The ID token says who logged in: our user for that account, created the first time. Its
    claims are verified: they come from the provider, for this app, for this login."""
    del userinfo  # userinfo=False: the ID token's claims are enough here
    if claims.get("email") and claims.get("email_verified") is False:
        return None  # an address nobody proved theirs: refuse the login
    # `sub` is unique and stable per issuer; the e-mail address may change hands.
    user_id = f"{claims['iss']}#{claims['sub']}"
    if user_id not in db.users:
        db.users[user_id] = User(id=user_id, email=claims.get("email"), name=claims.get("name"))
    return db.users[user_id]


def load_user(user_id: str) -> User | None:
    return db.users.get(user_id)


auth = FastAPIAuth()
provider = auth.use(
    OIDCStrategy(
        name="oidc",
        issuer=settings.oidc_issuer,
        client_id=settings.oidc_client_id,
        client_secret=settings.oidc_client_secret,
        redirect_uri=f"{settings.base_url}/auth/callback",
        verify=find_or_create_user,
    )
)
sessions = auth.use(SessionStrategy(load_user))
LoggedIn = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("oidc"))]
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("session"))]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # The provider's endpoints and keys, from its issuer: the app doesn't start without them.
    await provider.discover()
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the sessions.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="oidc", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware)
app.add_middleware(CSRFMiddleware)  # session cookies: refuse what other sites make browsers send


@app.get("/login")
async def log_in() -> RedirectResponse:
    """To the provider's login page, which sends the user back to the callback."""
    return provider.redirect()


@app.get("/auth/callback")
async def callback(request: Request, user: LoggedIn) -> RedirectResponse:
    """The provider sends the user back here: the strategy checks the state, exchanges the code
    and verifies the ID token; the session remembers the user from now on."""
    sessions.login(request, user.id)
    return RedirectResponse("/me", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    return user


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def log_out(request: Request, user: CurrentUser) -> None:
    del user  # only to refuse requests without a session
    sessions.logout(request)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("oidc_login:app", reload=True)

docs.text:
SAMLStrategy Browser to Your app: GET /saml/login. Your app to Browser: 302 → IdP, SAML request. Browser to Identity provider: log in at the IdP, once for every app. Identity provider to Browser: a signed assertion, in a form. Browser to Your app: POST /saml/acs, assertion. Your app: ✓ signature, audience, request, once. Your app to Browser: session cookie, 303 /me. One login at the identity provider opens every app. Browser Your app Identity provider GET /saml/login 302 → IdP, SAML request log in at the IdP, once for every app a signed assertion, in a form POST /saml/acs, assertion ✓ signature, audience, request, once session cookie, 303 /me One login at the identity provider opens every app What it's for: single sign-on with the company's identity provider: one login there opens every app.

Single sign-on with a SAML identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, ADFS, Keycloak…), then a session. The strategy: SAMLStrategy.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
The app needs an identity provider (an IdP). To try it without one of your own, Mock SAML takes any e-mail at example.com and any password. From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export IDP_ENTITY_ID=https://saml.example.com/entityid
export IDP_SSO_URL=https://mocksaml.com/api/saml/sso
export IDP_CERTIFICATE="$(curl -s https://mocksaml.com/api/saml/metadata | python -c 'import re, sys, textwrap; c = re.search(r"X509Certificate>([^<]+)<", sys.stdin.read())[1].strip(); print("-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----", *textwrap.wrap(c, 64), "-----END CERTIFICATE-----", sep="\n")')"
uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.saml_login:app

Mock SAML is for trying, never for an app

Its signing key is public, so anyone can sign its answers. With your IdP, set its entity id, single sign-on URL and signing certificate, and register the app there with the entity id http://localhost:8000/saml/metadata and the ACS http://localhost:8000/saml/acs (or give it /saml/metadata).

Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY too (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
/saml/login sends the browser to the IdP, with a SAML request. The request's id waits in a cookie, for the answer to carry:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/saml/login
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
location: https://mocksaml.com/api/saml/sso?SAMLRequest=fdFLT8MwDADgv1...
set-cookie: __Host-alcazaba-saml-saml=_b67fcee98db3916463789be0824bd27c7db1ad3a; Max-Age=600; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None
cache-control: no-store

Open http://localhost:8000/saml/login in the browser, and log in at Mock SAML as jackson@example.com with any password. Mock SAML posts its signed answer back to /saml/acs; the strategy checks it, and the app starts a session and takes you to /me:

{"id":"saml:jackson@example.com","email":"jackson@example.com"}

The IdP reads the app's metadata at http://localhost:8000/saml/metadata: its entity id and its ACS.

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Checked on what's signed: the strategy reads only the part that the IdP's signature covers, so an answer with a signed part and another one added (signature wrapping) gets nowhere. The issuer, the audience (this app), the recipient (the ACS), the request it answers and its validity are checked there.
  • Once: each assertion is kept in the cache's backend until it expires, so a copy posted again is refused, by every process.
  • No defaults for the IdP: without IDP_ENTITY_ID, IDP_SSO_URL and IDP_CERTIFICATE the app doesn't start: it never trusts an IdP it wasn't told about.
  • CSRF: the IdP posts the answer from its own site, so CSRFMiddleware lets /saml/acs through, and the strategy checks what CSRF would: that the answer is for the login this browser started.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/saml_login.py
"""Single sign-on with a SAML identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, ADFS, Keycloak…), then a session.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.saml_login:app

`/saml/login` sends the browser to the identity provider (the IdP) with a SAML request. The user
logs in there, and the IdP posts its signed answer back to `/saml/acs`, where `SAMLStrategy`
checks the signature with the IdP's certificate, and that the answer is for this app, for this
login and still valid. The app keeps its own user in a session (`SessionStrategy`), and gives
the IdP its metadata at `/saml/metadata`.

Set the IdP's IDP_ENTITY_ID, IDP_SSO_URL and IDP_CERTIFICATE (its signing certificate, in PEM),
and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, in the environment
or a .env file. At the IdP, register the app with the entity id
http://localhost:8000/saml/metadata and the ACS http://localhost:8000/saml/acs.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuth, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import SessionStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies.saml import SAMLProfile, SAMLStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.security import CSRFMiddleware, ServerSessionMiddleware


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file. The IdP's has no defaults:
    an app must never trust an IdP it wasn't told about."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    base_url: str = "http://localhost:8000"
    idp_entity_id: str
    idp_sso_url: str
    idp_certificate: str
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()  # type: ignore[call-arg]  # the IdP's settings come from the environment


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    email: str


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, User] = {}


db = Database()


def find_or_create_user(profile: SAMLProfile) -> User | None:
    """The IdP says who logged in: our user for that NameID (an e-mail here), created the first
    time."""
    user_id = f"saml:{profile.name_id}"
    if user_id not in db.users:
        db.users[user_id] = User(id=user_id, email=profile.name_id)
    return db.users[user_id]


def load_user(user_id: str) -> User | None:
    return db.users.get(user_id)


auth = FastAPIAuth()
saml = auth.use(
    SAMLStrategy(
        entity_id=f"{settings.base_url}/saml/metadata",  # this app, at the IdP
        acs_url=f"{settings.base_url}/saml/acs",
        idp_entity_id=settings.idp_entity_id,
        idp_sso_url=settings.idp_sso_url,
        idp_certificate=settings.idp_certificate,
        verify=find_or_create_user,
    )
)
sessions = auth.use(SessionStrategy(load_user))
SAMLUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("saml"))]
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("session"))]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the sessions, and refuses an
    # assertion that another one already accepted.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="sso", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware)
# The IdP posts to the ACS from its own site: SAMLStrategy checks what CSRF would.
app.add_middleware(CSRFMiddleware, exempt_paths=["/saml/acs"])


@app.get("/saml/login")
async def log_in() -> RedirectResponse:
    """To the IdP's login page, which posts the user back to the ACS."""
    return saml.redirect()


@app.post("/saml/acs")
async def acs(request: Request, user: SAMLUser) -> RedirectResponse:
    """The IdP posts its answer here: the strategy checks it; the session remembers the user from
    now on."""
    sessions.login(request, user.id)
    return RedirectResponse("/me", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)


@app.get("/saml/metadata")
async def metadata() -> Response:
    """This app's metadata, for the IdP."""
    return Response(saml.metadata(), media_type="application/samlmetadata+xml")


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    return user


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def log_out(request: Request, user: CurrentUser) -> None:
    del user  # only to refuse requests without a session
    sessions.logout(request)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("saml_login:app", reload=True)

SessionStrategy Browser to Your app: POST /login, password. Your app to Sessions: new session: user 1. Your app to Browser: Set-Cookie: session=<id>. Browser to Your app: GET /me, Cookie: session. Your app to Sessions: load session <id>. Sessions to Your app: user 1. Your app to Browser: 200 {"login": "octocat"}. The browser holds an id; the user stays on the server. Browser Your app Sessions POST /login, password new session: user 1 Set-Cookie: session=<id> GET /me, Cookie: session load session <id> user 1 200 {"login": "octocat"} The browser holds an id; the user stays on the server What it's for: a browser stays logged in after a login, holding only a random id; who the user is stays on the server.

A web app's login: a password, then a server-side session that remembers who logged in. The browser only holds a random id, in a cookie. The strategy: SessionStrategy.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.session_login:app

Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process. Without it each start makes up a throwaway one, and the sessions stop working when the app restarts.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Log in as octocat, whose password is correct horse battery staple. curl keeps the session's cookie in cookies.txt, as a browser would:

$ curl -i -c cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:8000/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"login": "octocat", "password": "correct horse battery staple"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
set-cookie: __Host-session=NZ4ZNmaZUVX7u7ZU4LB4AA4T8QDdE91BoXMzbXLKmJc; Max-Age=1209600; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
cache-control: no-store

{"id":"1","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

$ curl -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8000/me
{"id":"1","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

Logging out is refused without the app's Origin: CSRFMiddleware can't tell that the request comes from the app's own pages, as browsers say it with their Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site headers.

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:8000/logout
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Cross-site request refused"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X POST http://localhost:8000/logout -H "Origin: http://localhost:8000"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
set-cookie: __Host-session=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax
cache-control: no-store

The session is deleted from the backend, so the cookie that cookies.txt still holds is refused:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8000/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The user id, not the user: the session keeps the app's user id, and load_user loads the user on each request. A session whose user doesn't exist any more fails.
  • A new session at login: sessions.login() gives the session a new id, so one planted in the browser before (session fixation) doesn't get logged in too.
  • The cookie: HttpOnly (scripts in the page can't read it), Secure and SameSite=Lax, with Cache-Control: no-store on the responses that set it.
  • Passwords: kept as scrypt digests, compared in constant time, and unknown logins take as long as wrong passwords. FastAPIRateLimiter limits the tries per address.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/session_login.py
"""A web app's login: a password, then a server-side session that remembers who logged in.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.session_login:app

`sessions.login()` keeps the user's id in a session stored in the cache's backend, under a new
id (so that one planted in the browser before doesn't get logged in too); the browser only
holds that id, in a cookie. `SessionStrategy` loads the user from it on each request, and
`sessions.logout()` deletes the session from the backend.

Log in as octocat, with the password "correct horse battery staple". Set CACHE_SIGNING_KEY
(secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, in the environment or a .env file.
"""

import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuth, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import SessionStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit import FastAPIRateLimiter
from fastapi_alcazaba.security import CSRFMiddleware, ServerSessionMiddleware

DEMO_PASSWORD = "correct horse battery staple"  # noqa: S105  # octocat's, to try the example


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    login: str
    name: str | None = None


def password_digest(password: str, salt: bytes) -> bytes:
    """scrypt: slow on purpose, so that a stolen database gives the passwords away slowly."""
    return hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)


# What unknown logins are checked against, so that they take as long as wrong passwords.
UNKNOWN_SALT = secrets.token_bytes(16)
UNKNOWN_DIGEST = password_digest(secrets.token_urlsafe(), UNKNOWN_SALT)


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: one user, octocat, with the demo password."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users = {"1": User(id="1", login="octocat", name="The Octocat")}
        salt = secrets.token_bytes(16)
        self.passwords = {"octocat": ("1", salt, password_digest(DEMO_PASSWORD, salt))}

    def check_password(self, login: str, password: str) -> User | None:
        user_id, salt, digest = self.passwords.get(login, ("", UNKNOWN_SALT, UNKNOWN_DIGEST))
        if hmac.compare_digest(password_digest(password, salt), digest) and user_id:
            return self.users[user_id]
        return None


db = Database()


def load_user(user_id: str) -> User | None:
    return db.users.get(user_id)


auth = FastAPIAuth()
sessions = auth.use(SessionStrategy(load_user))
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("session"))]
# Five logins a minute per address: guessing passwords soon gets 429s.
login_attempts = FastAPIRateLimiter(times=5, minutes=1)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the sessions.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="web", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware)
app.add_middleware(CSRFMiddleware)  # session cookies: refuse what other sites make browsers send


class Login(BaseModel):
    login: str = Field(max_length=100)
    password: str = Field(max_length=200)


@app.post("/login", dependencies=[Depends(login_attempts)])
async def log_in(request: Request, form: Login) -> User:
    """Start a session for the user of that login and password."""
    user = db.check_password(form.login, form.password)
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "Wrong login or password")
    sessions.login(request, user.id)  # a new session id: no session fixation
    return user


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    return user


@app.post("/logout", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def log_out(request: Request, user: CurrentUser) -> None:
    del user  # only to refuse requests without a session
    sessions.logout(request)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("session_login:app", reload=True)

UnkeyStrategy Script to Your app: GET /documents, docs_… Your app to Unkey: verifyKey, documents.read. Unkey to Your app: VALID, 99 credits. Your app to Script: 200 [documents]. Script to Your app: POST /documents. Your app to Unkey: verifyKey, documents.write. Unkey to Your app: INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS. Your app to Script: 403 Forbidden. Unkey keeps the keys, and answers for each request. Script Your app Unkey GET /documents, docs_… verifyKey, documents.read VALID, 99 credits 200 [documents] POST /documents verifyKey, documents.write INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS 403 Forbidden Unkey keeps the keys, and answers for each request What it's for: API keys that Unkey keeps and checks on every request, with their permissions, credits and rate limits.

API keys that Unkey keeps: people sign up and get a key, their scripts send it, and Unkey checks it on every request, with its permissions, its credits and its rate limit. The strategy: UnkeyStrategy.

Each key reads documents (documents.read), has 100 credits a month and 10 requests a minute. Writing a document takes 5 credits and needs documents.write, which signing up doesn't give.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Create an API in Unkey's dashboard, and two root keys: one that may only verify its keys, one that may create and delete them. Then, from a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
export UNKEY_VERIFY_KEY=... UNKEY_ADMIN_KEY=... UNKEY_API_ID=api_...
uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.unkey_keys:app

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Sign up: the key is shown this once, Unkey keeps only its hash.

$ curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/signup -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"username": "ana"}'
{"key":"docs_...","key_id":"key_..."}

The key reads documents; each request takes a credit and one of the minute's 10:

$ curl http://localhost:8000/documents -H "Authorization: Bearer docs_..."
[{"title":"Style guide","owner":"unkey"}]

Writing needs documents.write, which Ana's key doesn't have: a 403. Give it the permission in Unkey's dashboard, and the same key writes, for 5 credits:

$ curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8000/documents -H "Authorization: Bearer docs_..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Draft"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Insufficient permissions"}

The eleventh request of a minute gets a 429 with Retry-After, and a key out of credits a 429 too ({"detail":"No credits left"}) until they're refilled on the 1st. Ana deletes her key, and Unkey refuses it from then on (within 30 seconds):

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://localhost:8000/keys/key_... -H "Authorization: Bearer docs_..."
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/documents -H "Authorization: Bearer docs_..."
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Two root keys: the strategy's may only verify keys, UnkeyKeys' may create and delete them: a leak of the first can't make keys.
  • The user from the key: each key is made with external_id=user.id, and load_user gets it back from every verification.
  • A strategy per permission: writing has a strategy of its own, unkey-write, with its permission and its cost, and the same client.
  • Only the owner deletes a key: a key ID that isn't the user's is a 404.
  • Unkey down: the requests get a 503, never let through.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/unkey_keys.py
"""API keys that Unkey keeps: people sign up and get a key, their scripts send it, and Unkey
checks it on every request, with its permissions, its credits and its rate limit.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.unkey_keys:app

Each key reads documents (`documents.read`), has 100 credits a month, of which writing a
document takes 5 and needs `documents.write`, which signing up doesn't give, and 10 requests a
minute. Its owner deletes it with `DELETE /keys/{key_id}`, and Unkey refuses it from then on.

Create an API in Unkey's dashboard, and two root keys: one that may only verify its keys, one
that may create and delete them. Set UNKEY_VERIFY_KEY, UNKEY_ADMIN_KEY and UNKEY_API_ID, in the
environment or a .env file.
"""

import uuid
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuth
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies import UnkeyStrategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth.strategies.unkey import (
    CreditRefill,
    KeyRatelimit,
    UnkeyClient,
    UnkeyKey,
    UnkeyKeys,
)


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    unkey_verify_key: SecretStr = SecretStr("set UNKEY_VERIFY_KEY")
    unkey_admin_key: SecretStr = SecretStr("set UNKEY_ADMIN_KEY")
    unkey_api_id: str = "set_UNKEY_API_ID"


settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    username: str


class SignUp(BaseModel):
    username: str = Field(pattern=r"^[a-z0-9_]{3,30}$")


class NewKey(BaseModel):
    key: str  # shown once: Unkey keeps only its hash
    key_id: str


class Document(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(max_length=200)
    owner: str = ""


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: the users, and the ids of their keys."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users: dict[str, User] = {}
        self.keys_of: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
        self.documents = [Document(title="Style guide", owner="unkey")]


db = Database()
# A root key for each use, with only the permissions it needs.
verifier = UnkeyClient(settings.unkey_verify_key)
admin = UnkeyClient(settings.unkey_admin_key)
keys = UnkeyKeys(admin, api_id=settings.unkey_api_id, prefix="docs")


def load_user(key: UnkeyKey) -> User | None:
    """The owner of a valid key: the user its external ID names."""
    return db.users.get(key.external_id) if key.external_id is not None else None


auth = FastAPIAuth(
    UnkeyStrategy(verifier, load_user, permissions="documents.read"),
    # Writing needs another permission and costs more: a strategy of its own, the same client.
    UnkeyStrategy(verifier, load_user, name="unkey-write", permissions="documents.write", cost=5),
)
Reader = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("unkey"))]
Writer = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("unkey-write"))]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    yield
    await verifier.aclose()
    await admin.aclose()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.post("/signup", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def sign_up(form: SignUp) -> NewKey:
    """A new user and its first key, which reads documents: shown once."""
    if any(user.username == form.username for user in db.users.values()):
        raise HTTPException(409, "That username is taken")
    user = User(id=f"user_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}", username=form.username)
    created = await keys.create(
        external_id=user.id,
        name=f"{user.username}'s first key",
        credits_left=100,
        refill=CreditRefill(100, day=1),
        ratelimits=[KeyRatelimit("requests", 10, timedelta(minutes=1))],
        permissions=["documents.read"],
    )
    db.users[user.id] = user
    db.keys_of[user.id] = {created.key_id}
    return NewKey(key=created.key.get_secret_value(), key_id=created.key_id)


@app.get("/documents")
async def list_documents(user: Reader) -> list[Document]:
    """One credit of the key, and one request of its rate limit."""
    del user  # authenticated: that's all it needs
    return db.documents


@app.post("/documents", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def write_document(document: Document, user: Writer) -> Document:
    """For keys with documents.write: five credits."""
    written = Document(title=document.title, owner=user.username)
    db.documents.append(written)
    return written


@app.delete("/keys/{key_id}", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def delete_key(key_id: str, user: Reader) -> None:
    """Deletes one of the user's keys, this one too: Unkey refuses it from then on."""
    if key_id not in db.keys_of.get(user.id, set()):
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such key")  # someone else's keys don't exist for them
    await keys.delete(key_id)
    db.keys_of[user.id].discard(key_id)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("unkey_keys:app", reload=True)

From a clone of the repository:

source .venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Without a key, nobody; the 401 says which credential the app takes:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: APIKey

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

Create a key as octocat, whose password is correct horse battery staple. It's shown this once:

$ curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api-keys -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"login": "octocat", "password": "correct horse battery staple"}'
{"id":"pij7glsba4npknkb","key":"demo_pij7glsba4npknkb_u5n6cue325sg5q5z4vlsu6pt275tu2xp6gajqsyxc6cdgu3gl2ca","expires_at":"2027-01-27T15:16:06.323588Z"}

A program sends it with each request:

$ KEY=demo_pij7glsba4npknkb_u5n6cue325sg5q5z4vlsu6pt275tu2xp6gajqsyxc6cdgu3gl2ca
$ curl http://localhost:8000/me -H "X-API-Key: $KEY"
{"id":"1","login":"octocat","name":"The Octocat"}

A wrong key gets the same 401 as no key, never telling which part was wrong:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8000/me -H "X-API-Key: demo_pij7glsba4npknkb_u5n6cue325sg5q5z4vlsu6pt275tu2xp6gajqsyxc6cdgu3gAAAA"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: APIKey

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Three answers: authenticate() returns the user; None when the request has no X-API-Key, so that the next strategy is tried; or raises AuthenticationFailed when the key is wrong, which is logged and never sent. challenge is the WWW-Authenticate of the 401s.
  • With the others: as a strategy, the key goes with sessions or JWTs on the same route: auth.authenticate("api-key", "jwt") takes either.
  • In the docs: openapi_scheme() puts the header in the OpenAPI schema, for the Authorize button of /docs.
  • Keys: FastAPIAPIKeys keeps their digests, bound to the server's pepper, and looks them up by their public id (pij7glsba4npknkb); the demo_ prefix lets secret scanners spot leaked ones.

docs.text:
examples/auth_strategies/api_key_strategy.py
"""A strategy of your own: API keys in `X-API-Key`, for the programs that call the API.

    uvicorn examples.auth_strategies.api_key_strategy:app

A strategy is a class whose `authenticate()` returns the user; None when the request doesn't
carry its credentials, so that the next strategy is tried; or raises AuthenticationFailed when
they're there but wrong. This one hands the key to FastAPIAPIKeys, which keeps keys as digests
bound to a server-side pepper, and gives FastAPIAuth the key's owner. As a strategy it goes
with the others: `auth.authenticate("api-key", "jwt")` would take a key or a JWT.

Create a key as octocat, with the password "correct horse battery staple". Set API_KEY_PEPPER
and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process, in the
environment or a .env file.
"""

import dataclasses
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import APIKeyHeader
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict
from starlette.requests import HTTPConnection

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAPIKeys, FastAPIAuth, FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.auth import AuthenticationFailed, Strategy
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit import FastAPIRateLimiter

DEMO_PASSWORD = "correct horse battery staple"  # noqa: S105  # octocat's, to try the example


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    api_key_pepper: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class User(BaseModel):
    id: str
    login: str
    name: str | None = None


@dataclasses.dataclass
class APIKeyRow:
    """A row of the api_keys table: everything about a key but the key itself."""

    id: str
    owner: str
    digest: str
    scopes: frozenset[str]
    expires_at: datetime | None


def password_digest(password: str, salt: bytes) -> bytes:
    """scrypt: slow on purpose, so that a stolen database gives the passwords away slowly."""
    return hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)


# What unknown logins are checked against, so that they take as long as wrong passwords.
UNKNOWN_SALT = secrets.token_bytes(16)
UNKNOWN_DIGEST = password_digest(secrets.token_urlsafe(), UNKNOWN_SALT)


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: one user, octocat, with the demo password, and their keys."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.users = {"1": User(id="1", login="octocat", name="The Octocat")}
        salt = secrets.token_bytes(16)
        self.passwords = {"octocat": ("1", salt, password_digest(DEMO_PASSWORD, salt))}
        self.api_keys: dict[str, APIKeyRow] = {}

    def check_password(self, login: str, password: str) -> User | None:
        user_id, salt, digest = self.passwords.get(login, ("", UNKNOWN_SALT, UNKNOWN_DIGEST))
        if hmac.compare_digest(password_digest(password, salt), digest) and user_id:
            return self.users[user_id]
        return None


db = Database()


async def load_key(key_id: str) -> APIKeyRow | None:
    return db.api_keys.get(key_id)


keys = FastAPIAPIKeys(load_key, pepper=settings.api_key_pepper, prefix="demo")


class APIKeyStrategy(Strategy):
    """The owner of the key in `X-API-Key`."""

    challenge = "APIKey"  # the WWW-Authenticate of the 401s

    def __init__(self, api_keys: FastAPIAPIKeys[APIKeyRow]) -> None:
        super().__init__("api-key")
        self.api_keys = api_keys

    def openapi_scheme(self) -> APIKeyHeader:
        """For the docs' Authorize button."""
        return APIKeyHeader(name="X-API-Key", scheme_name=self.name, auto_error=False)

    async def authenticate(self, connection: HTTPConnection) -> User | None:
        key = connection.headers.get("x-api-key")
        if key is None:
            return None  # not this strategy's: the next one is tried
        try:
            row = await self.api_keys.authenticate(key)
        except HTTPException as exc:  # FastAPIAPIKeys' 401: unknown, wrong or expired
            raise AuthenticationFailed("invalid API key") from exc
        owner = db.users.get(row.owner)
        if owner is None:
            raise AuthenticationFailed("the key's owner is gone")
        return owner


auth = FastAPIAuth()
auth.use(APIKeyStrategy(keys))
CurrentUser = Annotated[User, Depends(auth.authenticate("api-key"))]
# Five tries a minute per address: guessing passwords soon gets 429s.
login_attempts = FastAPIRateLimiter(times=5, minutes=1)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the limit's counters.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="keys", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class Login(BaseModel):
    login: str = Field(max_length=100)
    password: str = Field(max_length=200)


class NewKey(BaseModel):
    id: str
    key: str
    expires_at: datetime


@app.post("/api-keys", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED, dependencies=[Depends(login_attempts)])
async def create_key(form: Login) -> NewKey:
    """A new key, valid for 90 days and shown this once: only a digest of it is stored."""
    user = db.check_password(form.login, form.password)
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "Wrong login or password")
    expires_at = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(days=90)
    key, record = keys.generate(expires_at=expires_at)
    db.api_keys[record.id] = APIKeyRow(owner=user.id, **dataclasses.asdict(record))
    return NewKey(id=record.id, key=key, expires_at=expires_at)


@app.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentUser) -> User:
    return user


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("api_key_strategy:app", reload=True)

docs.text:
Authorization User to Your app: bob: PUT /articles/7. Your app to Policy engine: may bob PUT /articles/7? Policy engine to Your app: deny. Your app to User: 403 Forbidden. User to Your app: GET /users/%0A. Your app to User: 400, before asking. One dependency, whatever engine holds the policy. User Your app Policy engine bob: PUT /articles/7 may bob PUT /articles/7? deny 403 Forbidden GET /users/%0A 400, before asking One dependency, whatever engine holds the policy What it's for: a policy, not checks spread over the routes, decides who may do what, with the engine in the process (Casbin, Cedar) or as a service apart.

A policy decides who may do what, checked by FastAPIAuthz for each route or each action, and by AuthzMiddleware for every request, whatever engine holds the policy:

  • In process, with the policy in the app's memory:
    • Casbin: a newsroom whose roles write, edit, publish and grant roles.
    • Cedar: a team's documents, read and edited as their attributes allow, where contractors never see a confidential one.
  • As a separate service, one policy decision point that every service asks:
    • Open Policy Agent: a shop whose orders and refunds a Rego policy decides, by the user's roles and the order's total.

Each example runs with uvicorn and its own users, tokens and data; the commands in its page show what each user gets.

docs.text:
Casbin User to Your app: cris: POST …/3/publish. Your app to Casbin policy: (cris, articles, publish)? Casbin policy to Your app: deny: a writer. Your app to User: 403 Forbidden. User to Your app: ben: POST …/3/publish. Your app to Casbin policy: (ben, articles, publish)? Casbin policy to Your app: allow: an editor. Your app to User: 200, published by ben. Who may do what is in the policy, not in the routes. User Your app Casbin policy cris: POST …/3/publish (cris, articles, publish)? deny: a writer 403 Forbidden ben: POST …/3/publish (ben, articles, publish)? allow: an editor 200, published by ben Who may do what is in the policy, not in the routes What it's for: a Casbin policy (roles and their permissions) decides who may do what, for each route or each action, instead of checks spread over the code.

A newsroom API whose policy, not its routes, says who may do what. Anybody reads the published articles; writers write drafts, editors edit and publish them, and admins give people roles. The FastAPIAuthz dependencies check each request against Casbin's policy: on the path and method of the route, or on a named action such as (ben, articles, publish).

Users log in with a fixed token each, which stands in for your authentication (JWTs, sessions, API keys): ana-token (admin), ben-token (editor), cris-token (writer) and dan-token (no role yet).

docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.authz.main:app

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Visitors read the published articles. Cris, a writer, reads the drafts too:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles
[{"title":"Olive harvest starts","body":"...","id":1,"author":"cris","published_by":"ben"}]

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles -H "Authorization: Bearer cris-token"
[{"title":"Olive harvest starts",...,"published_by":"ben"},{"title":"Draft: new mill","body":"...","id":2,"author":"cris","published_by":null}]

Writing needs an account, and the writer role:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title": "Mill opens", "body": "On Monday."}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles -H "Authorization: Bearer cris-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Mill opens", "body": "On Monday."}'
{"title":"Mill opens","body":"On Monday.","id":3,"author":"cris","published_by":null}

Publishing is a named action, (user, articles, publish), which only editors may do:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles/3/publish -H "Authorization: Bearer cris-token"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Forbidden"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles/3/publish -H "Authorization: Bearer ben-token"
{"title":"Mill opens","body":"On Monday.","id":3,"author":"cris","published_by":"ben"}

Dan has an account but no role, and so reads what visitors read, and nothing more. Ana, an admin, makes Dan a writer, which takes effect at once:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles -H "Authorization: Bearer dan-token" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Hello", "body": "First post."}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden

{"detail":"Forbidden"}

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/dan/roles/writer -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer dan-token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"title": "Hello", "body": "First post."}'
201

Admins only grant the roles the policy knows:

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/dan/roles/root -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token"
{"detail":[{"type":"enum","loc":["path","role"],"msg":"Input should be 'writer', 'editor' or 'admin'",...}]}

A wrong token is refused, rather than taken for a visitor without one:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/articles -H "Authorization: Bearer nonsense"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer

{"detail":"Invalid token"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The policy is data: policy.csv has a p line per permission of a role and a g line per role of a user (or of another role: editors are writers too). Changing who may do what doesn't change the code; in production the policy comes from a database, through one of Casbin's async adapters.
  • Two ways to ask: Depends(authz) asks about the route, as (user, path, method): Casbin's keyMatch2 takes /articles/:id as a pattern. members.require("articles", "publish") asks about a named action, the same on whatever route it guards.
  • Visitors and members: authz has the policy check visitors without a token as *anonymous, a name no user can have, so that the policy opens the reading routes to them. members refuses them with a 401 before asking the policy, and so always returns a user name: the routes for members don't deal with None.
  • What visitors may do, everybody may: the matcher grants the rules of *anonymous to every subject (p.sub == "*anonymous" || g(r.sub, p.sub)), so Dan, without a role, isn't worse off than a visitor.
  • Checks that depend on the data go in the route, with await authz.enforce(): everybody may list the articles, but only those who may read the drafts see them. A draft is a 404 for the others, not a 403, which would tell that it exists.
  • Roles granted at runtime take effect at once in the process that grants them: an AsyncEnforcer changes its policy in the event loop, where the checks run. The file adapter of the example doesn't keep them; a database adapter does, and a Casbin watcher tells the other processes to load the policy again.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
main.pymodel.confpolicy.csv

examples/authz/main.py

"""A newsroom API whose policy, not its routes, says who may do what: Casbin's RBAC.

    uvicorn examples.authz.main:app

Anybody reads the published articles; writers write drafts, editors edit and publish them, and
admins give people roles. Who may do what is in policy.csv (`p` lines: what a role may do; `g`
lines: who has which role, and which roles include others), checked by FastAPIAuthz: on the path
and method of a route (`Depends(authz)`), or on a named action (`Depends(authz.require(...))`).

The policy is read from files here; in production, from a database through one of Casbin's
async adapters (casbin-async-sqlalchemy-adapter...), which also keeps the roles granted at runtime.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated

import casbin
import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPIAuthz

HERE = Path(__file__).parent


class Role(StrEnum):
    # An enum: admins can only grant the roles the policy knows.
    WRITER = "writer"
    EDITOR = "editor"
    ADMIN = "admin"


class Draft(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(max_length=200)
    body: str = Field(max_length=10_000)


class Article(Draft):
    id: int
    author: str
    published_by: str | None = None


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.articles = {
            1: Article(
                id=1, title="Olive harvest starts", body="...", author="cris", published_by="ben"
            ),
            2: Article(id=2, title="Draft: new mill", body="...", author="cris"),
        }


# Async: its changes to the policy (granting a role) run in the event loop, like the checks.
enforcer = casbin.AsyncEnforcer(str(HERE / "model.conf"), str(HERE / "policy.csv"))
db = Database()
bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
# Stands in for the app's authentication (JWTs, sessions, API keys): a token per user.
TOKENS = {"ana-token": "ana", "ben-token": "ben", "cris-token": "cris", "dan-token": "dan"}


async def current_user(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(bearer)],
) -> str | None:
    """Who makes the request; None for a visitor without a token."""
    if credentials is None:
        return None
    user = TOKENS.get(credentials.credentials)
    if user is None:  # a wrong token isn't a visitor without one
        raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid token", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return user


# Routes open to visitors when the policy says so: the policy knows them as "*anonymous", a name
# no user can have (the * isn't allowed in user names), so nobody signs up to get its rules.
authz = FastAPIAuthz(enforcer, subject=current_user, anonymous="*anonymous")
# Routes for people with an account: a 401 without one, before asking the policy.
members = FastAPIAuthz(enforcer, subject=current_user)
Visitor = Annotated[str | None, Depends(authz)]
Member = Annotated[str, Depends(members)]


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    await enforcer.load_policy()  # an AsyncEnforcer reads it when told
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


async def reads_drafts(user: str | None) -> bool:
    # A check inside the route: the route is open to everybody, the drafts aren't.
    return user is not None and await authz.enforce(user, "drafts", "read")


@app.get("/articles")
async def list_articles(user: Visitor) -> list[Article]:
    """The published articles; the drafts too for those who may read them."""
    drafts = await reads_drafts(user)
    return [article for article in db.articles.values() if article.published_by or drafts]


@app.get("/articles/{article_id}")
async def read_article(article_id: int, user: Visitor) -> Article:
    article = db.articles.get(article_id)
    if article is None or not (article.published_by or await reads_drafts(user)):
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such article")  # for readers, a draft doesn't exist
    return article


@app.post("/articles", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def write_article(draft: Draft, user: Member) -> Article:
    article = Article(id=max(db.articles) + 1, author=user, **draft.model_dump())
    db.articles[article.id] = article
    return article


@app.put("/articles/{article_id}")
async def edit_article(article_id: int, draft: Draft, user: Member) -> Article:
    article = db.articles.get(article_id)
    if article is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such article")
    if article.author != user and not await authz.enforce(user, "articles", "edit"):
        raise HTTPException(403, "Only its author or an editor edits an article")
    article.title, article.body = draft.title, draft.body
    return article


@app.post("/articles/{article_id}/publish")
async def publish_article(
    article_id: int,
    editor: Annotated[str, Depends(members.require("articles", "publish"))],
) -> Article:
    """A named action, not a path: (editor, articles, publish)."""
    article = db.articles.get(article_id)
    if article is None:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such article")
    article.published_by = editor
    return article


@app.put(
    "/users/{user}/roles/{role}",
    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
    dependencies=[Depends(members.require("roles", "grant"))],
)
async def grant_role(user: str, role: Role) -> None:
    """Takes effect at once in this process. The other processes see it when they load the policy
    again: a Casbin watcher (casbin-redis-watcher...) tells them."""
    await enforcer.add_role_for_user(user, role)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

# RBAC on paths and on named actions: a request is (who, what, how).
#   (ben, /articles/7, PUT): may Ben edit article 7?
#   (ben, articles, publish): may Ben publish articles?
# keyMatch2 takes /articles/:id as a pattern; "articles" matches itself. What visitors
# (*anonymous: no user name starts with *) may do, everybody may: a user without a role reads
# what visitors read.

[request_definition]
r = sub, obj, act

[policy_definition]
p = sub, obj, act

[role_definition]
g = _, _

[policy_effect]
e = some(where (p.eft == allow))

[matchers]
m = (p.sub == "*anonymous" || g(r.sub, p.sub)) && keyMatch2(r.obj, p.obj) && r.act == p.act

Cedar User to Your app: eva: GET /documents/2. Your app to Cedar policies: eva read Document 2? Your app: a forbid beats a permit. Cedar policies to Your app: deny: confidential. Your app to User: 404, as if missing. User to Your app: ben: GET /documents/2. Your app to User: 200, Budget 2027. Attributes decide, and a forbid beats every permit. User Your app Cedar policies eva: GET /documents/2 eva read Document 2? a forbid beats a permit deny: confidential 404, as if missing ben: GET /documents/2 200, Budget 2027 Attributes decide, and a forbid beats every permit What it's for: policies on attributes (a document's team and owner, who's a contractor) where a forbid beats every permit, validated against a schema.

A team's shared documents, whose Cedar policies decide who reads, edits and deletes each one by its attributes: its team, its owner, whether it's confidential, and who's asking. The members of a document's team read it, its owner edits it, admins delete documents, and contractors never see a confidential one, whatever else allows it.

Users log in with a fixed token each, which stands in for your authentication: ana-token (admin, editorial), ben-token (editorial), eva-token (a contractor in editorial) and dan-token (sales).

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Ben reads both documents of his team, and none of sales. Eva, in the same team, doesn't get the confidential budget:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents -H "Authorization: Bearer ben-token"
[{"id":1,"title":"Style guide","owner":"ana","team":"editorial","confidential":false},{"id":2,"title":"Budget 2027","owner":"ben","team":"editorial","confidential":true}]

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents -H "Authorization: Bearer eva-token"
[{"id":1,"title":"Style guide","owner":"ana","team":"editorial","confidential":false}]

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents/2 -H "Authorization: Bearer eva-token"
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"No such document"}

Only its owner edits a document, admins included:

$ curl -i -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents/2 -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Budget 2028"}'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Only its owner edits a document"}

$ curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents/2 -H "Authorization: Bearer ben-token" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title": "Budget 2027, second draft"}'
{"id":2,"title":"Budget 2027, second draft","owner":"ben","team":"editorial","confidential":true}

Deleting is for admins, asked as a named action, (user, documents, delete):

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents/3 -H "Authorization: Bearer dan-token"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Forbidden"}

$ curl -i -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents/3 -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
content-type: application/json

Without a token, a 401 before the policy is asked:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/documents
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Not authenticated"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Attributes, not roles alone: the user's team and whether it's a contractor, the document's team, owner and confidentiality. The user is the entity the authentication gives; each document, the entity the route builds from the row it read.
  • A forbid beats every permit: Eva is in the budget's team, which permits reading it, and the forbid on confidential documents for contractors wins.
  • Validated at start: the policies are checked against schema.cedarschema when the enforcer is made, so a misspelled attribute fails at start, not as a wrong answer.
  • 404 for what you may not read: a document a user may not read doesn't exist for them.

A shop whose Open Policy Agent policy decides who reads each order and who refunds it, asked over the network: everybody reads the catalogue, customers their own orders and the support staff every order. Support refunds up to 100 euros, and a manager above that. While OPA is down, every request gets a 503.

Users log in with a fixed token each, which stands in for your authentication: ana-token and leo-token (customers), sam-token (support) and max-token (support and manager).

From a clone of the repository, OPA in Docker with the policy, and the app:

docker run -p 8181:8181 -v "$PWD/examples/authz:/policies:ro" openpolicyagent/opa:1.21.4 \
    run --server --addr 0.0.0.0:8181 /policies/shop.rego
make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.authz.opa_service:app
