docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Everybody reads the catalogue, a token or not:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/products
[{"id":1,"name":"Olive oil","price":9.5}]

Ana reads her orders, not Leo's; Sam, in support, reads every order:

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token"
{"id":1,"customer":"ana","total":40.0,"refunded":false}

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/3 -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token"
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"No such order"}

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/3 -H "Authorization: Bearer sam-token"
{"id":3,"customer":"leo","total":15.0,"refunded":false}

The policy reads the order's total: Sam doesn't refund 250 euros, Max, a manager, does. Ana doesn't refund her own:

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/2/refund -H "Authorization: Bearer sam-token"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Refunds are for the support staff, and a manager above 100 euros"}

$ curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/2/refund -H "Authorization: Bearer max-token"
{"id":2,"customer":"ana","total":250.0,"refunded":true}

$ curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/orders/1/refund -H "Authorization: Bearer ana-token"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Refunds are for the support staff, and a manager above 100 euros"}

Stop OPA, and nothing is let through:

$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/products
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Authorization unavailable"}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The policy is elsewhere: the app sends who asks (the user with its roles), the order and the action, and OPA answers. Changing who refunds what is a change to shop.rego, which OPA loads, not a deploy of the app.
  • Attributes in the input: input.subject.roles and input.resource.total are what the route gives authz.enforce, the user the authentication loaded and the order it read.
  • default allow := false: without it, the rule would be undefined for what no body matches, which the enforcer refuses with a warning.
  • Fails closed: OPA down is a 503, never a request let through, and after 5 failures the circuit breaker refuses at once instead of waiting for OPA on every request.
  • 404 for what you may not read: an order a user may not read doesn't exist for them.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/authz/shop.rego
# Who may do what in the shop: the rule `allow` of `package shop`, which the app queries as
# shop.allow with the input {"subject": ..., "resource": ..., "action": ..., "context": ...}.
package shop

# Nothing is allowed unless a rule below says so: the rule is never undefined.
default allow := false

# Everybody reads the catalogue, signed in or not.
allow if {
    input.action == "GET"
    input.resource == "/products"
}

# Customers read their own orders, and the support staff every order.
allow if {
    input.action == "read"
    input.resource.customer == input.subject.name
}

allow if {
    input.action == "read"
    "support" in input.subject.roles
}

# The support staff refund up to 100 euros; above that, a manager does.
allow if {
    input.action == "refund"
    "support" in input.subject.roles
    input.resource.total <= 100
}

allow if {
    input.action == "refund"
    "manager" in input.subject.roles
}
examples/authz/opa_service.py
"""A shop whose orders and refunds Open Policy Agent decides, asked over the network: the policy
lives in its own service, shared by every app of the company.

    docker run -p 8181:8181 -v "$PWD/examples/authz:/policies:ro" openpolicyagent/opa:1.21.4 \\
        run --server --addr 0.0.0.0:8181 /policies/shop.rego
    uvicorn examples.authz.opa_service:app

Everybody reads the catalogue, customers their own orders and the support staff every order.
Support refunds up to 100 euros, and a manager above that. The policy is in shop.rego: the app
sends who asks (with the user's roles), the order and the action, and OPA answers. When OPA
doesn't answer, the requests get a 503: nothing is let through.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, Any

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from pydantic import BaseModel, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba.authz import FastAPIAuthz
from fastapi_alcazaba.authz.opa import OPAEnforcer


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    opa_url: str = "http://localhost:8181"
    opa_token: SecretStr | None = None  # when OPA runs with --authentication=token


class Product(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    price: float


class Order(BaseModel):
    id: int
    customer: str
    total: float
    refunded: bool = False


class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    roles: list[str] = []


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.products = [Product(id=1, name="Olive oil", price=9.5)]
        self.orders = {
            1: Order(id=1, customer="ana", total=40),
            2: Order(id=2, customer="ana", total=250),
            3: Order(id=3, customer="leo", total=15),
        }


settings = Settings()
db = Database()
bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
# Stands in for the app's authentication (JWTs, sessions, API keys): a token per user.
USERS = {
    "ana-token": User(name="ana"),
    "leo-token": User(name="leo"),
    "sam-token": User(name="sam", roles=["support"]),
    "max-token": User(name="max", roles=["support", "manager"]),
}


async def current_user(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(bearer)],
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Who makes the request, with what the policy reads of them; None without a token."""
    if credentials is None:
        return None
    user = USERS.get(credentials.credentials)
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Invalid token", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return user.model_dump()


enforcer = OPAEnforcer(settings.opa_url, rule="shop.allow", token=settings.opa_token)
authz = FastAPIAuthz(enforcer, subject=current_user, anonymous="*anonymous")


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    yield
    await enforcer.aclose()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/products", dependencies=[Depends(authz)])
async def list_products() -> list[Product]:
    """(subject, path, method): the policy opens it to everybody, anonymous visitors too."""
    return db.products


async def signed_in(
    user: Annotated[dict[str, Any] | None, Depends(current_user)],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The user, for routes that ask the policy about the order they read."""
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(401, "Not authenticated", headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
    return user


SignedIn = Annotated[dict[str, Any], Depends(signed_in)]


@app.get("/orders/{order_id}")
async def read_order(order_id: int, user: SignedIn) -> Order:
    """The order, as OPA reads it: a 404 for those who may not, as if it didn't exist."""
    order = db.orders.get(order_id)
    if order is None or not await authz.enforce(user, order.model_dump(), "read"):
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such order")
    return order


@app.post("/orders/{order_id}/refund")
async def refund_order(order_id: int, user: SignedIn) -> Order:
    """The policy reads the order's total: support refunds small orders, managers any."""
    order = db.orders.get(order_id)
    if order is None or not await authz.enforce(user, order.model_dump(), "read"):
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such order")
    if not await authz.enforce(user, order.model_dump(), "refund"):
        raise HTTPException(403, "Refunds are for the support staff, and a manager above 100 euros")
    order.refunded = True
    return order


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("opa_service:app", reload=True)

docs.text:
As a separate service Your app to Policy service: may ana PUT /articles/7? Policy service to Your app: allow. Other service to Policy service: may ana refund order 9? Policy service to Other service: deny. Other service: down: refuse, never allow. One policy for every service, asked over the network. Your app Other service Policy service may ana PUT /articles/7? allow may ana refund order 9? deny down: refuse, never allow One policy for every service, asked over the network What it's for: one policy decision point that every service asks over the network, deployed and audited in one place.

A policy decision point that runs apart from the app, which every service asks over the network: Open Policy Agent, OpenFGA, SpiceDB, Cerbos. The policies are deployed and audited in one place, for every service at once.

The guide tells what changes from an engine in the process: the latency of each check, a 503 when the service doesn't answer, and an enforcer that awaits the answer.

  • Open Policy Agent: a shop whose orders and refunds a Rego policy decides, by the user's roles and the order's total, and which refuses everything while OPA is down.

Without a network, the engines in the process: Casbin and Cedar.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Pagination Client to Your app: GET ?page=2&page_size=3. Your app to Cache: page 2: its own entry. Your app to Client: 200, 3 items, Link: next. Client to Your app: GET ?page_size=1000. Your app to Client: 422, page_size ≤ 100. Client to Your app: GET …/newest?cursor=NTk… Your app to Client: 200, the 2 after it. Pages checked, linked, and cached each under its own key. Client Your app Cache GET ?page=2&page_size=3 page 2: its own entry 200, 3 items, Link: next GET ?page_size=1000 422, page_size ≤ 100 GET …/newest?cursor=NTk… 200, the 2 after it Pages checked, linked, and cached each under its own key What it's for: lists served a page at a time, by page number or by cursor, with limits that clients can't go past, and each page cached apart.

Each pagination strategy has an example of its own, in the menu. This one is a product catalogue paginated with PaginationPageNumber and PaginationCursor, and cached three ways: one entry per page, one entry for a whole short list sliced into pages, and one entry per cursor. Every list is tagged, so adding a product drops every page at once.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.pagination.main:app

Cursors are signed: set CURSOR_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, or a cursor made by one process is refused by the others.

docs.text:
A page, computed once and then served from the cache, which links to the pages around it in the Link header:

$ curl -i "http://127.0.0.1:8000/products?page=2&page_size=3"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

{"items":[{"name":"Product 4","category":"vegetables","price":1.4,"id":4},{"name":"Product 5","category":"oil","price":1.5,"id":5},{"name":"Product 6","category":"fruit","price":1.6,"id":6}],"total":60,"page":2,"page_size":3,"pages":20}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The page parameters are arguments of the endpoint, so @cache keeps each page, size and category under its own key. The catalogue (the database session in a real app) is left out of the key with exclude_params, since it changes from one request to the next.
  • Categories are an enum, not any string: clients can't create cache entries without end.
  • Three strategies for three kinds of lists: a page per entry for big lists where most clients read the first pages; the whole list once (get_or_set) for short ones; a cursor for infinite scroll and clients that sync everything.
  • Tags: every list is tagged products, and a write drops them all without knowing their keys.
  • Public data: the cache is created with vary_headers=(), so pages are shared by everybody. Don't do that for anything that depends on who asks.
  • Links made for each request: a cached page gets the Link header of the request it answers, with that request's other query parameters; the links aren't stored with the entry, where one client's parameters would reach everybody else.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/main.py
"""A product catalogue paginated and cached by Alcazaba, with no other library.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.main:app

Three ways to cache paginated lists:

- `/products`: `@cache` on the endpoint, one entry per page. Each response is served straight from
  the cache. Best for big lists, where most clients only read the first pages.
- `/categories/{category}/products`: the whole list cached once with `get_or_set`, and every page
  sliced from it. One entry, whatever the page and page size. Best for short lists.
- `/products/newest`: by cursor, newest first, one entry per cursor. Products added meanwhile
  don't shift the pages, which suits infinite scroll and clients that sync everything.

They're tagged "products", so a write drops every page at once without knowing their keys.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import (
    Cache,
    FastAPICache,
    get_cache,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.cursor import CursorPage, CursorParams, PaginationCursor
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.page_number import (
    PageNumberPage,
    PageNumberParams,
    PaginationPageNumber,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class Category(StrEnum):
    # An enum, not any string: clients can't create cache entries without end.
    FRUIT = "fruit"
    VEGETABLES = "vegetables"
    OIL = "oil"


class NewProduct(BaseModel):
    name: str
    category: Category
    price: float


class Product(NewProduct):
    id: int


class Catalog:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        categories = list(Category)
        self.products = [
            Product(id=i, name=f"Product {i}", category=categories[i % 3], price=1 + i / 10)
            for i in range(1, 61)
        ]
        self.queries = 0

    def find(self, category: Category | None = None) -> list[Product]:
        self.queries += 1
        return [p for p in self.products if category is None or p.category == category]

    def page(
        self,
        params: PageNumberParams,
        category: Category | None = None,
    ) -> PageNumberPage[Product]:
        """What a database does: count, and fetch only the page (OFFSET/LIMIT)."""
        found = self.find(category)
        rows = found[params.offset : params.offset + params.limit]
        return pages.paginate(rows, params, total=len(found))

    def newest(self, params: CursorParams) -> CursorPage[Product]:
        """What a database does: WHERE id < :after ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT :fetch; for the page
        before, WHERE id > :before ORDER BY id LIMIT :fetch, nearest first."""
        self.queries += 1
        if isinstance(params.before, int):  # the id of the first product of the page after
            rows = sorted((p for p in self.products if p.id > params.before), key=lambda p: p.id)
        else:
            rows = sorted(self.products, key=lambda p: p.id, reverse=True)
            if isinstance(params.after, int):  # the id of the last product of the page before
                rows = [p for p in rows if p.id < params.after]
        page = rows[: params.fetch]
        return cursors.paginate(page, params, key=lambda p: p.id, descending=True, queried=True)

    def add(self, product: NewProduct) -> Product:
        saved = Product(id=len(self.products) + 1, **product.model_dump())
        self.products.append(saved)
        return saved


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the entries.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="catalog", vary_headers=())  # public data
    application.state.catalog = Catalog()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_catalog(request: Request) -> Catalog:
    catalog: Catalog = request.app.state.catalog
    return catalog


CatalogDep = Annotated[Catalog, Depends(get_catalog)]


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    cursor_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()
pages = PaginationPageNumber(default_page_size=20, max_page_size=100)
# Signed: clients can't make cursors up. Every process must have the same secret, or a cursor
# made by one is refused by the others: set CURSOR_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)).
cursors = PaginationCursor(settings.cursor_secret, default_limit=20)


@app.get("/products")
@cache(expire=300, tags=["products"], exclude_params=["catalog"])
async def products(
    params: Annotated[PageNumberParams, Depends(pages)],
    catalog: CatalogDep,
    category: Category | None = None,
) -> PageNumberPage[Product]:
    """One entry per page, page size and category: the page parameters are arguments, part of the
    key. The session is left out of it, since it changes from one request to the next."""
    return catalog.page(params, category)


@app.get("/categories/{category}/products")
async def category_products(
    category: Category,
    params: Annotated[PageNumberParams, Depends(pages)],
    catalog: CatalogDep,
    app_cache: Annotated[Cache, Depends(get_cache)],
) -> PageNumberPage[Product]:
    """One entry for the whole category: every page is sliced from it."""

    async def load() -> list[Product]:  # annotated: the entry comes back as products
        return catalog.find(category)

    found = await app_cache.get_or_set(f"category:{category}", load, expire=300, tags=["products"])
    return pages.paginate(found, params)


@app.get("/products/newest")
@cache(expire=300, tags=["products"], exclude_params=["catalog"])
async def newest_products(
    params: Annotated[CursorParams, Depends(cursors)],
    catalog: CatalogDep,
) -> CursorPage[Product]:
    """By cursor, newest first: each next_cursor gives the products right after the last one seen,
    however many were added since."""
    return catalog.newest(params)


@app.post("/products", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_product(product: NewProduct, catalog: CatalogDep) -> Product:
    """The new product may land on any page: drop them all."""
    saved = catalog.add(product)
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags("products")
    return saved


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("main:app", reload=True)

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• A unique sort key: (created_at, id), since two events may share a time.
  • Both ways: next_cursor holds the key of the page's last event, prev_cursor that of its first. For the page before, the database reads the index the other way (oldest first, past the key), and paginate puts the rows back newest first.
  • One row more: the database fetches params.fetch rows (the limit and one), which tells whether there's another page that way, and paginate(..., queried=True) keeps the page.
  • Readable, not changeable: the cursor is base64 JSON, so clients can read the sort key, and signed, so they can't change it nor use it with other query parameters.
  • Pages that don't move: a cursor's page is the same whatever is added later, so each one is cached under its own key; the first page is renewed every minute.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/cursor.py
"""An activity feed by cursor, newest first: each `next_cursor` gives the events right after the
last one seen, however many were added since, and `prev_cursor` the ones before the first.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.cursor:app

`PaginationCursor` hides the sort key of the event at each edge of a page, `(created_at, id)`, in
a signed cursor: clients can't make one up, change it or use it with other filters. The database
fetches one row more than the page, which tells whether there's another one that way. Set
CURSOR_SECRET (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process, in the environment or a
.env file.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.cursor import CursorPage, CursorParams, PaginationCursor
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache

START = datetime(2026, 10, 29, 9, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    cursor_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class Event(BaseModel):
    id: int
    created_at: datetime
    text: str


class NewEvent(BaseModel):
    text: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)


def sort_key(event: Event) -> tuple[datetime, int]:
    """Unique: two events can share a time, never an id."""
    return event.created_at, event.id


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: 30 events, a minute apart."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.events = [
            Event(id=n, created_at=START + timedelta(minutes=n), text=f"Event {n}")
            for n in range(1, 31)
        ]

    def page(self, params: CursorParams) -> list[Event]:
        """Newest first: SELECT * FROM events WHERE (created_at, id) < :after
        ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT :fetch. For the page before:
        WHERE (created_at, id) > :before ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT :fetch, nearest first."""
        if isinstance(params.before, tuple):  # the key of the first event of the page after
            found = sorted(self.events, key=sort_key)
            found = [event for event in found if sort_key(event) > params.before]
        else:
            found = sorted(self.events, key=sort_key, reverse=True)
            if isinstance(params.after, tuple):  # the key of the last event of the page before
                found = [event for event in found if sort_key(event) < params.after]
        return found[: params.fetch]

    def add(self, event: NewEvent) -> Event:
        saved = Event(id=len(self.events) + 1, created_at=datetime.now(UTC), text=event.text)
        self.events.append(saved)
        return saved


db = Database()
# Signed: clients can't make cursors up. Every process must have the same secret, or a cursor
# made by one is refused by the others.
cursors = PaginationCursor(settings.cursor_secret, default_limit=5, max_limit=20)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the pages.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="feed", vary_headers=())  # public data
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/events")
@cache(expire=60)
async def events(params: Annotated[CursorParams, Depends(cursors)]) -> CursorPage[Event]:
    """One entry per cursor: the first page is renewed every minute, the others never change."""
    return cursors.paginate(db.page(params), params, key=sort_key, descending=True, queried=True)


@app.post("/events", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_event(event: NewEvent) -> Event:
    """A new event goes on top: the next pages of every client stay as they were."""
    return db.add(event)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("cursor:app", reload=True)

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• The key, as it is: after is the id of the last message, as text; a key of several values, such as (created_at, id), would be a JSON array.
  • One row more: each query fetches params.fetch rows (the limit and one), which tells whether there's a next page.
  • Syncing: the last page still gives its after, so a client that has caught up asks for whatever came since with it.
  • Both orders: /messages/newest reads the index the other way, and after there means the messages before it.
  • Cached page by page: each key and limit is an entry of its own, and a new message drops them all (tag messages).

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/keyset.py
"""A chat's messages paginated by keyset, the key in plain sight: clients ask for what came after
the last message they have, or page back through the history, newest first.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.keyset:app

`/messages?after=42&limit=20` gives the messages after 42, in order: a client that keeps the
`after` of its last page gets only the new ones, however many arrive meanwhile. `/messages/newest`
pages back from the newest, `after` being the oldest message of the page before. The key is the
id, which clients read and may write; each page is cached under its own key, and a new message
drops them all.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.keyset import KeysetPage, KeysetParams, PaginationKeyset
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class NewMessage(BaseModel):
    author: str
    text: str


class Message(NewMessage):
    id: int


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        authors = ("ana", "leo", "eva")
        self.messages = [
            Message(id=i, author=authors[i % 3], text=f"Message {i}") for i in range(1, 61)
        ]
        self.queries = 0

    def after(self, params: KeysetParams) -> KeysetPage[Message]:
        """What a database does: WHERE id > :after ORDER BY id LIMIT :fetch."""
        self.queries += 1
        rows = self.messages
        if isinstance(params.after, int):
            rows = [message for message in rows if message.id > params.after]
        return keyset.paginate(rows[: params.fetch], params, key=lambda m: m.id, queried=True)

    def before(self, params: KeysetParams) -> KeysetPage[Message]:
        """What a database does: WHERE id < :after ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT :fetch."""
        self.queries += 1
        rows = self.messages[::-1]
        if isinstance(params.after, int):
            rows = [message for message in rows if message.id < params.after]
        return keyset.paginate(
            rows[: params.fetch],
            params,
            key=lambda m: m.id,
            descending=True,
            queried=True,
        )

    def add(self, message: NewMessage) -> Message:
        saved = Message(id=len(self.messages) + 1, **message.model_dump())
        self.messages.append(saved)
        return saved


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="chat", vary_headers=())
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_db(request: Request) -> Database:
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    return db


DatabaseDep = Annotated[Database, Depends(get_db)]

# Sorted by id, an int: ?after=42. Several values, such as (created_at, id), go as a JSON array.
keyset = PaginationKeyset(sort=int, default_limit=20, max_limit=100)


@app.get("/messages")
@cache(expire=300, tags=["messages"], exclude_params=["db"])
async def messages(
    params: Annotated[KeysetParams, Depends(keyset)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
) -> KeysetPage[Message]:
    """The messages after `after`, oldest first: for clients that sync."""
    return db.after(params)


@app.get("/messages/newest")
@cache(expire=300, tags=["messages"], exclude_params=["db"])
async def newest_messages(
    params: Annotated[KeysetParams, Depends(keyset)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
) -> KeysetPage[Message]:
    """The messages before `after`, newest first: for a history read backwards."""
    return db.before(params)


@app.post("/messages", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_message(message: NewMessage, db: DatabaseDep) -> Message:
    """The last pages change: drop them all."""
    saved = db.add(message)
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags("messages")
    return saved


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("keyset:app", reload=True)

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• One row more, no count: the database is asked for limit + 1 rows (params.fetch); the extra one isn't returned, it only says that there's a next page. Nothing counts the whole log, which on a big table takes longer than the page itself.
  • No total, no last page: total is null and the links are first, previous and, while has_more, next. An endpoint that counts passes total= instead of queried=True, and its pages have the total and a link to the last one.
  • Lines written meanwhile shift the pages: a line logged while page one is read pushes its last line into page two, which repeats it. To follow a list that grows at the top without that, page by key: PaginationKeyset or PaginationCursor.
  • A short expiry: the log changes all the time, so each page is cached for ten seconds, under its own key (offset, limit and level). The level is an enum: clients can't create cache entries without end.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/offset.py
"""An access log paginated by offset, without the total: a table too big to count at every
request, and that grows while it's read.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.offset:app

`/logs?offset=0&limit=20` reads one row more than the page, which says whether there's a next one
(`has_more`), instead of counting the whole log: the newest lines first, all of them or those of
one level. Each page is cached for a few seconds, under its own key.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.offset import OffsetPage, OffsetParams, PaginationOffset
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class Level(StrEnum):
    # An enum, not any string: clients can't create cache entries without end.
    INFO = "info"
    WARNING = "warning"
    ERROR = "error"


class Line(BaseModel):
    id: int
    level: Level
    message: str


def level_of(number: int) -> Level:
    if number % 50 == 0:
        return Level.ERROR
    return Level.WARNING if number % 10 == 0 else Level.INFO


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lines = [
            Line(id=i, level=level_of(i), message=f"GET /products/{i % 97}") for i in range(1, 1001)
        ]
        self.queries = 0

    def page(
        self,
        params: OffsetParams,
        level: Level | None = None,
    ) -> OffsetPage[Line]:
        """What a database does: WHERE level = :level ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT :fetch OFFSET
        :offset, one row more than the page and no count."""
        self.queries += 1
        newest = [line for line in reversed(self.lines) if level is None or line.level == level]
        rows = newest[params.offset : params.offset + params.fetch]
        return offsets.paginate(rows, params, queried=True)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="logs", vary_headers=())
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_db(request: Request) -> Database:
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    return db


DatabaseDep = Annotated[Database, Depends(get_db)]

offsets = PaginationOffset(default_limit=20, max_limit=100)


@app.get("/logs")
@cache(expire=10, exclude_params=["db"])
async def logs(
    params: Annotated[OffsetParams, Depends(offsets)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
    level: Level | None = None,
) -> OffsetPage[Line]:
    """The newest lines first, a page at a time: `has_more` says whether to ask for the next."""
    return db.page(params, level)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("offset:app", reload=True)

Asked again, it comes from the cache, without a query:

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Only the page, and the count: the database fetches the page with params.offset and params.limit, and counts the posts: pages.paginate(rows, params, total=count).
  • One entry per page and size: the page parameters are an argument of the endpoint, so @cache keeps each page apart.
  • The cost of numbers: each page counts every post, and a post published while someone reads shifts the pages after it. For feeds, see PaginationCursor.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/page_number.py
"""A blog's archive by page number: numbered pages of posts, newest first, with the total and the
number of pages.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.page_number:app

`PaginationPageNumber` reads `page` and `page_size` from the query (a 422 for a page size over
20), the database counts the posts and fetches only the page, and the response links to the
first, previous, next and last pages. Each page is cached under its own key; publishing a post
drops them all, by tag.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.page_number import (
    PageNumberPage,
    PageNumberParams,
    PaginationPageNumber,
)
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class Post(BaseModel):
    id: int
    title: str


class NewPost(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: 45 posts, and how many queries it ran."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.posts = [Post(id=n, title=f"Post {n}") for n in range(1, 46)]
        self.queries = 0

    def count(self) -> int:
        """SELECT count(*) FROM posts"""
        self.queries += 1
        return len(self.posts)

    def newest(self, offset: int, limit: int) -> list[Post]:
        """SELECT * FROM posts ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset"""
        self.queries += 1
        return sorted(self.posts, key=lambda post: post.id, reverse=True)[offset : offset + limit]

    def add(self, post: NewPost) -> Post:
        saved = Post(id=len(self.posts) + 1, title=post.title)
        self.posts.append(saved)
        return saved


db = Database()
pages = PaginationPageNumber(default_page_size=10, max_page_size=20)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process shares the pages.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="blog", vary_headers=())  # public data
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/posts")
@cache(expire=300, tags=["posts"])
async def posts(params: Annotated[PageNumberParams, Depends(pages)]) -> PageNumberPage[Post]:
    """Only the page, and the count: what a database does with OFFSET and LIMIT."""
    rows = db.newest(params.offset, params.limit)
    return pages.paginate(rows, params, total=db.count())


@app.post("/posts", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def publish(post: NewPost) -> Post:
    """The new post goes first and shifts every page: drop them all."""
    saved = db.add(post)
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags("posts")
    return saved


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("page_number:app", reload=True)

A range that starts past the last contact is a 416, which says how many there are:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/contacts?start=319"
HTTP/1.1 416 Range Not Satisfiable
content-range: items */319
content-type: application/json

{"detail":"Range Not Satisfiable"}

A range that ends before it starts, or holds more than 100 contacts, is a 400:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/contacts?start=10&end=5"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
content-type: application/json

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• Both ends included, from 0: start=0&end=24 is 25 contacts; without end, a range holds default_items (25 here). For the database, params.offset and params.limit.
  • The total twice: in the body (total) and in Content-Range: items 0-24/319, where a grid that reads headers finds it; items */319 when the range holds nothing.
  • 400 or 416: a range that can't be one (end before start, or too big) is the client's mistake, a 400 before anything is queried. One that starts past the end is a 416, after the count: the list may have shrunk since the client last read its total.
  • Cached with its headers: each range is an entry, and a hit gets its Content-Range and links back. A new contact (POST /contacts) changes the total, so it drops every range.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/ranges.py
"""A contact list for a data grid, paginated by range: the grid asks for the rows it shows by their
indexes, and reads which ones it got, and how many there are, from `Content-Range`.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.ranges:app

`/contacts?start=0&end=24` answers the first 25 contacts with `Content-Range: items 0-24/319`. A
range that starts past the last contact is a 416, with `Content-Range: items */319`. Each range
is cached under its own key, and a new contact drops them all.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.ranges import PaginationRange, RangePage, RangeParams
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


class NewContact(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: str


class Contact(NewContact):
    id: int


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.contacts = [
            Contact(id=i, name=f"Contact {i:03}", email=f"contact{i}@example.com")
            for i in range(1, 320)
        ]
        self.queries = 0

    def page(self, params: RangeParams) -> RangePage[Contact]:
        """What a database does: count, and fetch only the range (ORDER BY name LIMIT :limit
        OFFSET :offset)."""
        self.queries += 1
        by_name = sorted(self.contacts, key=lambda contact: contact.name)
        rows = by_name[params.offset : params.offset + params.limit]
        return ranges.paginate(rows, params, total=len(by_name))

    def add(self, contact: NewContact) -> Contact:
        saved = Contact(id=len(self.contacts) + 1, **contact.model_dump())
        self.contacts.append(saved)
        return saved


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="contacts", vary_headers=())
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_db(request: Request) -> Database:
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    return db


DatabaseDep = Annotated[Database, Depends(get_db)]

ranges = PaginationRange(default_items=25, max_items=100)


@app.get("/contacts")
@cache(expire=300, tags=["contacts"], exclude_params=["db"])
async def contacts(
    params: Annotated[RangeParams, Depends(ranges)],
    db: DatabaseDep,
) -> RangePage[Contact]:
    """A range of contacts, by name: the cache gives a hit its Content-Range too."""
    return db.page(params)


@app.post("/contacts", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_contact(contact: NewContact, db: DatabaseDep) -> Contact:
    """The total changes, and the new contact may land in any range: drop them all."""
    saved = db.add(contact)
    await FastAPICache.invalidate_tags("contacts")
    return saved


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("ranges:app", reload=True)

An export of orders: a script reads every order in batches while the shop keeps selling, and gets them as they were when it started. The query runs once; its results are kept in the cache's backend, and each scroll_id reads the next batch of them. The strategy: PaginationScroll.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.pagination.scroll:app

Set SCROLL_SECRET and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY (secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process. Without them each start makes up throwaway ones, and the scroll ids stop working when the app restarts.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
The export starts: the first four of the 12 orders, and the scroll_id of the next batch, in the body and in the Link header:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=4"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
link: </orders/export?batch_size=4&scroll_id=WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw0XQ.3VRVV5FF93szTc6nwQegzA>; rel="next"

{"items":[{"customer":"customer-1","amount":10.0,"id":1,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-2","amount":20.0,"id":2,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-3","amount":30.0,"id":3,"status":"shipped"},{"customer":"customer-4","amount":40.0,"id":4,"status":"paid"}],"scroll_id":"WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw0XQ.3VRVV5FF93szTc6nwQegzA","total":12}

An order is placed meanwhile:

$ curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/orders -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"customer": "late", "amount": 99.5}'
{"customer":"late","amount":99.5,"id":13,"status":"paid"}

The export goes on with the orders it found: still 12, nothing seen twice. The same request again, as a script does when the response is lost, gets the same batch:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=4&scroll_id=WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw0XQ.3VRVV5FF93szTc6nwQegzA"
{"items":[{"customer":"customer-5","amount":50.0,"id":5,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-6","amount":60.0,"id":6,"status":"shipped"},{"customer":"customer-7","amount":70.0,"id":7,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-8","amount":80.0,"id":8,"status":"paid"}],"scroll_id":"WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw4XQ.FvL2Kiaq0Y5sccGOjqoMZQ","total":12}

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=4&scroll_id=WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw0XQ.3VRVV5FF93szTc6nwQegzA"
{"items":[{"customer":"customer-5","amount":50.0,"id":5,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-6","amount":60.0,"id":6,"status":"shipped"},{"customer":"customer-7","amount":70.0,"id":7,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-8","amount":80.0,"id":8,"status":"paid"}],"scroll_id":"WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw4XQ.FvL2Kiaq0Y5sccGOjqoMZQ","total":12}

The last batch has no scroll_id, and no Link:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=4&scroll_id=WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw4XQ.FvL2Kiaq0Y5sccGOjqoMZQ"
{"items":[{"customer":"customer-9","amount":90.0,"id":9,"status":"shipped"},{"customer":"customer-10","amount":100.0,"id":10,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-11","amount":110.0,"id":11,"status":"paid"},{"customer":"customer-12","amount":120.0,"id":12,"status":"shipped"}],"scroll_id":null,"total":12}

A scroll_id holds the snapshot's id and where the next batch starts, signed. One changed by hand to skip a batch doesn't match its signature:

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?scroll_id=WyJsR3NqcG9ZNGo5QVZIMGFoU3ZJZDVRIiw4XQ.3VRVV5FF93szTc6nwQegzA"
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

{"detail":"Invalid scroll_id"}

A new export runs the query again, and finds the 13 orders. When the script is done with it, it deletes the snapshot rather than leave it until it expires (60 seconds after its last batch):

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=10"
{"items":[...],"scroll_id":"WyJwNXRWQU9uV0ZnS3VuM01iSTlNekp3IiwxMF0.9cQSX6b7Hpxm_wVvrAsyAg","total":13}

$ curl -i -X DELETE "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?scroll_id=WyJwNXRWQU9uV0ZnS3VuM01iSTlNekp3IiwxMF0.9cQSX6b7Hpxm_wVvrAsyAg"
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

$ curl -i "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=10&scroll_id=WyJwNXRWQU9uV0ZnS3VuM01iSTlNekp3IiwxMF0.9cQSX6b7Hpxm_wVvrAsyAg"
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found

{"detail":"Expired or unknown scroll_id"}

Batches have a maximum size, checked before anything is queried:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/orders/export?batch_size=500"
{"detail":[{"type":"less_than_equal","loc":["query","batch_size"],"msg":"Input should be less than or equal to 50","input":"500","ctx":{"le":50}}]}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• One query per export: without a scroll_id the endpoint queries the orders and start keeps them; with one, next reads the batch from what was kept, and the database isn't touched.
  • A snapshot: what was found when the export started, whatever is written meanwhile. Items added, changed or deleted don't shift the batches.
  • Retries are safe: the scroll_id says where the batch starts, so the same request gets the same batch; reading a batch doesn't move anything forward.
  • Kept alive while it's read: each batch gives the snapshot another 60 seconds. A script that stops for longer gets a 404 and starts again.
  • Bounded: the query asks for one row more than max_items, and start refuses more than that, rather than keep a million rows in the backend.
  • Sealed in the backend: the cache's signing key seals the snapshot, so whoever can write to the backend can't plant one; an encryption_key instead also hides it, for personal data.
  • Not cached: the endpoint has no @cache, since each start keeps a snapshot of its own.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/scroll.py
"""An export of orders by scroll: a script reads every order in batches while the shop keeps
selling, and gets what was there when it started.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.scroll:app

`PaginationScroll` keeps what the query found as a snapshot in the cache's backend, and each
`scroll_id` reads its next batch: orders placed meanwhile don't show, none is skipped or seen
twice, and a retried request gets the same batch. Set SCROLL_SECRET and CACHE_SIGNING_KEY
(secrets.token_urlsafe(32) each), the same in every process, in the environment or a .env file.
"""

import secrets
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Query, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, SecretStr
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.scroll import PaginationScroll, ScrollPage, ScrollParams


def throwaway_secret() -> SecretStr:
    """A random secret, for trying the example: it changes at every start and differs between
    processes."""
    return SecretStr(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """The configuration, from environment variables or a .env file."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", env_file_encoding="utf-8", extra="ignore")

    scroll_secret: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)
    cache_signing_key: SecretStr = Field(default_factory=throwaway_secret)


settings = Settings()


class Status(StrEnum):
    PAID = "paid"
    SHIPPED = "shipped"


class NewOrder(BaseModel):
    customer: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    amount: float = Field(gt=0)


class Order(NewOrder):
    id: int
    status: Status = Status.PAID


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database: 12 orders, every third one shipped."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.orders = [
            Order(
                id=n,
                customer=f"customer-{n}",
                amount=10.0 * n,
                status=Status.SHIPPED if n % 3 == 0 else Status.PAID,
            )
            for n in range(1, 13)
        ]

    def find(self, state: Status | None, limit: int) -> list[Order]:
        """SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = :state ORDER BY id LIMIT :limit"""
        return [order for order in self.orders if state is None or order.status == state][:limit]

    def add(self, order: NewOrder) -> Order:
        saved = Order(id=len(self.orders) + 1, **order.model_dump())
        self.orders.append(saved)
        return saved


db = Database()
# Signed: clients can't make scroll ids up. Every process must have the same secret, or a
# scroll_id made by one is refused by the others.
scroll = PaginationScroll(
    Order,
    settings.scroll_secret,
    default_batch_size=5,
    max_batch_size=50,
    keep_alive=60,
    max_items=1_000,
)


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # Redis or Valkey in production, so that every process reads the same snapshots. The
    # signing key seals them: whoever can write to the backend can't plant one.
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop", signing_key=settings.cache_signing_key)
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/orders/export")
async def export_orders(
    params: Annotated[ScrollParams, Depends(scroll)],
    state: Annotated[Status | None, Query(alias="status")] = None,
) -> ScrollPage[Order]:
    """Without a scroll_id, the query runs and its results are kept for the next batches; with
    one, the next batch comes from them and the query doesn't run again. Not cached: each start
    keeps a snapshot of its own."""
    if params.scroll_id is None:
        # One more than the scroll keeps: if they're all there, start() refuses them.
        return await scroll.start(db.find(state, scroll.max_items + 1), params)
    return await scroll.next(params)


@app.delete("/orders/export", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def stop_export(scroll_id: str) -> None:
    """The script is done (or gives up): the snapshot goes now, not when it expires."""
    await scroll.clear(scroll_id)


@app.post("/orders", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def add_order(order: NewOrder) -> Order:
    """A new order: the exports running don't see it, the next ones will."""
    return db.add(order)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("scroll:app", reload=True)

docs.title: PaginationStreaming
docs.text:
PaginationStreaming Client to Your app: GET /events. Your app to Database: ORDER BY id LIMIT 100. Your app to Client: 200, 100 lines of NDJSON. Your app to Database: id > 100 LIMIT 100. Your app to Client: 100 more lines. Your app to Database: id > 200 LIMIT 100. Database to Your app: 50 rows: the last batch. Your app to Client: 50 lines, end. Every item in one response, read and sent a batch at a time. Client Your app Database GET /events ORDER BY id LIMIT 100 200, 100 lines of NDJSON id > 100 LIMIT 100 100 more lines id > 200 LIMIT 100 50 rows: the last batch 50 lines, end Every item in one response, read and sent a batch at a time What it's for: every item in one response, as they come, without pages, read from a big table a batch at a time by key.

An activity log sent whole, without pages: one JSON object per line, read from the database a hundred events at a time by id, each batch sent as soon as it's read. A second endpoint sends the 25 newest events from a synchronous cursor, and closes it there. The strategy: PaginationStreaming.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
From a clone of the repository:

make deps                 # .venv, with every extra
source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn examples.pagination.streaming:app

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Every event, one per line, as they come (-N turns curl's buffering off):

$ curl -iN http://localhost:8000/events | head -10
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/x-ndjson
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

{"id":1,"kind":"upload","at":"2026-10-29T09:01:00Z"}
{"id":2,"kind":"logout","at":"2026-10-29T09:02:00Z"}
{"id":3,"kind":"login","at":"2026-10-29T09:03:00Z"}
{"id":4,"kind":"upload","at":"2026-10-29T09:04:00Z"}

All 250 of them, from three queries of up to 100 rows; and the logins alone, from one:

$ curl -s http://localhost:8000/events | wc -l
250

$ curl -s "http://localhost:8000/events?kind=login" | head -3
{"id":3,"kind":"login","at":"2026-10-29T09:03:00Z"}
{"id":6,"kind":"login","at":"2026-10-29T09:06:00Z"}
{"id":9,"kind":"login","at":"2026-10-29T09:09:00Z"}

$ curl -s "http://localhost:8000/events?kind=login" | wc -l
83

The newest events end at 25, however many there are:

$ curl -s http://localhost:8000/events/latest | head -3
{"id":250,"kind":"upload","at":"2026-10-29T13:10:00Z"}
{"id":249,"kind":"login","at":"2026-10-29T13:09:00Z"}
{"id":248,"kind":"logout","at":"2026-10-29T13:08:00Z"}

$ curl -s http://localhost:8000/events/latest | wc -l
25

The parameters are checked before anything is streamed:

$ curl "http://localhost:8000/events?kind=anything"
{"detail":[{"type":"enum","loc":["query","kind"],"msg":"Input should be 'login', 'upload' or 'logout'","input":"anything","ctx":{"expected":"'login', 'upload' or 'logout'"}}]}

docs.title: What to look at
docs.text:
• No pages: one request, one response, every event. The status and headers go out first, and the lines follow as they're read, in chunks of batch_size lines; curl -N shows them as they arrive.
  • Read by key: batches(fetch, key=...) asks the database for 100 events, then for the 100 after the last id it got, and stops at the first batch shorter than 100: three queries for 250 events, each one through the index on id, as fast as the first. The whole log is never in memory.
  • Sync or async: fetch here is async; the cursor of /events/latest is a synchronous generator, which the stream reads in the thread pool, ten events at a time, so a blocking driver doesn't stop the event loop.
  • max_items: /events/latest ends at 25, and the cursor is closed there (its finally runs) rather than read to the end.
  • A client that disconnects stops the stream: no more queries are made for it.
  • Not cached: @cache doesn't keep streams, and each request reads the database again. Lists that are read often, a page at a time, are better cached by page (PaginationCursor).

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
examples/pagination/streaming.py
"""An activity log streamed as NDJSON, one event per line, without pages and without loading it.

    uvicorn examples.pagination.streaming:app

- `/events`: every event (or every event of a kind), read from the database 100 at a time by
  id, each batch sent as soon as it's read. A client that stops reading stops the queries.
- `/events/latest`: the 25 newest, from a synchronous cursor that the stream reads in the thread
  pool and closes at the 25th.

Streams aren't cached: each request reads the database again.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Iterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Annotated

import uvicorn
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.streaming import PaginationStreaming


class Kind(StrEnum):
    LOGIN = "login"
    UPLOAD = "upload"
    LOGOUT = "logout"


class Event(BaseModel):
    id: int
    kind: Kind
    at: datetime


class Database:
    """Stands in for the database (a session per request in a real app)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        kinds, start = list(Kind), datetime(2026, 10, 29, 9, 0, tzinfo=UTC)
        self.events = [
            Event(id=i, kind=kinds[i % len(kinds)], at=start + timedelta(minutes=i))
            for i in range(1, 251)
        ]
        self.queries = 0
        self.open_cursors = 0

    async def events_after(
        self,
        after: int | None,
        limit: int,
        kind: Kind | None,
    ) -> list[Event]:
        """What a database does: WHERE id > :after AND kind = :kind ORDER BY id LIMIT :limit."""
        self.queries += 1
        found = [
            event
            for event in self.events
            if (after is None or event.id > after) and (kind is None or event.kind == kind)
        ]
        return found[:limit]

    def newest(self) -> Iterator[Event]:
        """A synchronous driver's cursor, newest first: the rows come as they're read."""
        self.queries += 1
        self.open_cursors += 1
        try:
            yield from reversed(self.events)
        finally:
            self.open_cursors -= 1


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    application.state.db = Database()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


def get_db(request: Request) -> Database:
    db: Database = request.app.state.db
    return db


DatabaseDep = Annotated[Database, Depends(get_db)]

# 100 lines a chunk, and 100 rows a query.
stream = PaginationStreaming(batch_size=100)
latest = PaginationStreaming(batch_size=10, max_items=25)


@app.get("/events")
async def events(
    db: DatabaseDep,
    kind: Kind | None = None,
) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Every event, by id: a query per batch, past the last id of the batch before."""

    async def fetch(
        after: int | None,
        limit: int,
    ) -> list[Event]:
        return await db.events_after(after, limit, kind)

    return stream.response(stream.batches(fetch, key=lambda event: event.id))


@app.get("/events/latest")
async def latest_events(db: DatabaseDep) -> StreamingResponse:
    """The 25 newest events: the stream stops reading the cursor there, and closes it."""
    return latest.response(db.newest())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("streaming:app", reload=True)

docs.title: Secure by default
docs.text:
What could serve one user's data to another, trust data from outside, or let a client get around a protection is off unless you turn it on, and the documentation says what it costs.

The response cache is safe by default:

  • Users never get each other's responses. Requests carrying Authorization or Cookie get their own cache entries and the response is sent as Cache-Control: private, also when the endpoint authenticates through a router dependency.
  • No Redis script injection. FastAPICache.clear(namespace=...) deletes with SCAN + UNLINK: a namespace from user input never reaches a Lua script, and the server isn't blocked by KEYS.
  • Signed or encrypted entries. With a signing_key, every entry carries an HMAC bound to its key: whoever can write to Redis can't plant data, move one user's entry under another user's key, or get a pickle executed. With an encryption_key they're also encrypted (AES-256-GCM): a dump or a backup of Redis doesn't reveal the cached responses.
  • Bounded memory. InMemoryBackend evicts the least recently used entries instead of growing forever with every new query string.
  • Clients can't bypass the cache with Cache-Control: no-cache unless you allow it.
  • Only successful responses are cached, never a 404 or a 500 replayed as a 200.
  • Cache stampede protection: concurrent misses for one key compute once, in each process and, with distributed_lock, across processes.
  • A broken backend doesn't take the app down: every backend call has a timeout, and a circuit breaker stops calling it while it fails.
  • Keys that never repeat are reported: an argument whose repr() changes on every call (a database session, a service) makes every request a miss; Alcazaba warns about it.

And more: early refresh of popular entries, Valkey through valkey-py or Valkey GLIDE, cache hits that return the annotated type (Pydantic models, not dicts), deterministic ETags, the Cache-Status header (Alcazaba; hit; ttl=42, Alcazaba; fwd=miss; stored), the response model in OpenAPI, exclude_params and stale-while-revalidate.

The other tools follow the same rules. Nothing that opens a door is stored in clear: API keys, one-time codes and revoked tokens are kept as digests or HMACs. Sessions keep only a random id in the cookie. Uploads are checked from their bytes, not from what the client says they are.

docs.title: Shared by every process
docs.text: An app runs in several processes, on several machines. Whatever must hold for all of them lives in the backend, Redis, Valkey, memcached or DynamoDB, and every process sees it at once: the rate limits and the locks, the sessions and the revoked tokens, maintenance mode and the feature flags. Scheduled jobs run once per tick whatever the number of processes, and the task queue runs each task at least once, retried when it fails.

docs.title: Resilient
docs.text: Every call to the backend has a timeout and goes through a circuit breaker: a backend that hangs or fails doesn't take the app down with it. What each tool does then is chosen for it and documented: the cache and the rate limiter let requests through, the token blocklist refuses them. The security model has the details.

docs.title: The FastAPI way
docs.text: The tools are what FastAPI already uses: dependencies (Depends(FastAPIRateLimiter(...)), Depends(authz)), decorators (@cache) and ASGI middlewares. What they need from the request shows in the OpenAPI schema, and the docs' Authorize button knows the API keys and tokens. Everything is typed: @cache keeps the signature and the return type of what it decorates, and your editor completes what you write.

docs.title: Based on standards
docs.text: Errors are problem details (RFC 9457), cache results are told in Cache-Status (RFC 9211), and rate limits in the IETF's RateLimit headers. Webhooks follow Standard Webhooks, pages link to each other with Link (RFC 8288), and the security headers are OWASP's. Authorization uses Casbin policies, and metrics and traces go through OpenTelemetry.

docs.title: Observable
docs.text: Alcazaba logs under fastapi_alcazaba.* and, with the otel extra, records metrics and traces through OpenTelemetry: cache hits and misses, backend calls, limited requests, refused authorizations, task runs. Never keys, tokens or identities. Every request can have an ID, in the logs, the responses and the errors. See metrics and traces.

docs.title: Tested hard
docs.text: Every change runs the tests on Python 3.11 to 3.14, against real Redis, Valkey, a Valkey cluster, memcached and DynamoDB Local, with at least 90 % coverage, and the examples run in uvicorn processes against a real Valkey. Fuzzing (ClusterFuzzLite) runs on whatever reads data from outside, mutation testing checks that the tests notice when the code changes, and a benchmark 50 % slower than main's fails the pull request.

docs.title: Signed releases
docs.text: Releases are built by GitHub Actions and signed with Sigstore, with an SBOM of what they contain: you can verify that what PyPI serves is what the repository built. The project's builds take no dependency released less than three days earlier.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
What the hot paths cost, measured by the benchmarks in tests/benchmarks, which CI runs on every push and fails when one gets more than 50 % slower than the others.

On an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, Python 3.13, pydantic 2.14 and the in-memory backend, the median of each (one call; the time of the event loop's own round trip is included):

What Median Per second A cache hit: 100 pydantic items, as their type 78 µs 12 400 The same, signed (HMAC-SHA256) 84 µs 11 700 The same, encrypted (AES-256-GCM) 84 µs 11 600 The same, compressed with zstd 81 µs 12 100 The same, encrypted and compressed 88 µs 11 200 The function without the cache, returning the items it holds 4 µs 238 000 Encoding the 100 items as JSON 62 µs 16 100 Decoding them back as list[Item] 48 µs 20 800 The default cache key of an endpoint 1 µs 990 000 Signing and verifying the 100 items 6 µs 155 000 Encrypting and decrypting them 8 µs 129 000 A rate limiter's check, within the limit 24 µs 41 000
  • Most of a hit is pydantic's: turning JSON back into 100 models takes 48 of the 78 µs. Signing adds 6 µs, encryption 6 more, compression 3: protecting the entries costs little next to decoding them.
  • When the cache pays: a function that answers in 4 µs from memory is faster without it. One that queries a database (a millisecond or more) or another service is a hundred times slower than a hit. Cache the second kind.
  • With Redis or Valkey, add a network round trip (a fraction of a millisecond on the same network) to each hit and each rate-limit check.

Run them on your machine:

make deps
.venv/bin/pytest tests/benchmarks --benchmark-only

docs.title: Scope and stability
docs.text: What Alcazaba is for, what it leaves to others, and which of its tools are settled.

docs.title: What's in it
docs.text:
Alcazaba gathers the pieces that cut across a FastAPI backend, which most apps end up writing themselves:

  • State that every process must share, in Redis, Valkey, memcached or DynamoDB: a cache, rate limits and quotas, sessions, revoked tokens, locks, feature flags, a task queue.
  • Security at the edges of a request: who makes it (authentication, a second factor, passkeys), what they may do (authorization), what they used (accounting), what they did (an audit trail), and what reaches the app (CSRF, headers, uploads, webhooks, outbound calls).
  • The operations around them: circuit breakers, maintenance mode, health checks, problem details, request IDs, metrics, traces and logs.
  • What leaves the app: e-mail, files in object storage, messages to its other processes, and those a change announces (an outbox).

A tool belongs here when it keeps that kind of state or guards that kind of edge, and is secure by default: nothing that opens a door stored in clear, a failure that refuses unless the tool says otherwise, a backend that fails without taking the app down.

docs.title: What isn't
docs.text: Not in Alcazaba Instead An ORM, migrations, a database layer The app's: SQLAlchemy, SQLModel… (the pagination builds their queries) CORS, compression, static files, trusted hosts Starlette's middlewares: CORSMiddleware, GZipMiddleware, StaticFiles, TrustedHostMiddleware Being an identity provider (issuing tokens to other apps, users and groups, federation, SCIM) An identity provider; Alcazaba logs in with it (OIDCStrategy, SAMLStrategy) A policy engine of its own Casbin, Cedar or Open Policy Agent, which FastAPIAuthz asks GraphQL, gRPC, server-side rendering Their libraries; Alcazaba's tools work under any route Billing (invoices, payments, plans) A billing system, fed by the usage records

docs.title: Stability
docs.text:
Until 1.0, any release may change any tool: the release notes say what changed, and what to change in an app. Beyond that, each tool is one of:

  • Stable: its API has been through releases, apps use it, and it should reach 1.0 as it is. A change to it is the exception, said first in the release notes.
  • Experimental: new, and may still change in any release, as its use shows what's missing or wrong. Its guide says so at the top.
Tool Stability Response cache, backends Stable Rate and concurrency limits Stable Idempotency keys Stable Authentication strategies: JWT, bearer, session, OAuth2, SAML, scopes Stable API keys, tokens and codes Stable Authorization with Casbin Stable Sessions, CSRF and security headers Stable Audit trail Stable Checking uploads Stable Webhooks and outbound calls Stable Pagination Stable Background work, operations, errors and observability Stable Cedar and Open Policy Agent Experimental OIDCStrategy, UnkeyStrategy Experimental Second factor (TOTP), passkeys (WebAuthn), step-up Experimental Each user's sessions (UserSessions) Experimental Accounting Experimental Passwords, object storage, e-mail Experimental Broadcast, the outbox, structured logs Experimental

docs.title: Towards 1.0
docs.text: 1.0 is when the stable tools stop changing: from then on, a change that breaks an app waits for a major version, and the release notes of the one before say it's coming. An experimental tool becomes stable once it has been through releases without changing, and apps use it.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Each tool has a page in the Tutorial - User Guide, an example app and its reference.

  • Response cache

    @cache for endpoints and functions: one entry for everybody or one per user, invalidation by tag, signed or encrypted entries.

  • Backends

    In memory, Redis, Valkey, GLIDE, memcached or DynamoDB, and a copy in each process in front of them.

  • Pagination

    Seven strategies: page numbers, offsets, ranges, signed cursors, keysets, scrolls and streams, each page cached under its own key.

  • Rate and concurrency limits

    Requests per window and requests at a time, per client or shared, across processes.

  • Idempotency keys

    A retried POST gets the first response instead of running twice.

  • Authentication strategies

    Who makes a request, by strategies: JWTs, bearer tokens, sessions, OAuth2 logins with GitHub or Google, SAML single sign-on, or your own.

  • API keys, tokens and codes

    API keys with scopes and expiry, a blocklist of tokens and one-time codes, nothing stored in clear.

  • Passwords

    Slow hashes with a pepper, leaked passwords refused, guesses limited per account, and resets by a link that works once.

  • Passkeys

    Logins without a password with Touch ID, Windows Hello, a phone or a security key (WebAuthn), which a phishing page can't relay.

  • Second factor

    Authenticator apps' codes (TOTP) after the password, each once, recovery codes, and a recent code for sensitive actions.

  • Authorization

    Who may do what, decided by a Casbin or Cedar policy in the process, or by Open Policy Agent over the network (ACL, RBAC, ABAC), per route or for every request.

  • Sessions, CSRF and security headers

    Sessions you can revoke, requests from other sites refused, the OWASP headers and a body size limit.

  • Accounting

    What each user, API key or tenant uses per period, held to its plan's quotas, with a usage record per charge for billing.

  • Audit trail

    Who did what to which resource, and whether it worked: no secrets, signed and chained.

  • Checking uploads

    The real type from the bytes, the size, image dimensions and safe file names.

  • Object storage

    Signed URLs and upload forms for S3, R2 or MinIO: files go straight from the browser, bounded in size and type.

  • E-mail

    Password resets, codes and receipts with their invoice, over SMTP with TLS or Amazon SES's API, in messages nothing can add a header or a recipient to.

  • Webhooks and outbound calls

    Standard Webhooks signing and verification, and calls out with a deadline, a breaker and SSRF protection.

  • Errors and observability

    RFC 9457 problem details, request IDs, timeouts, health checks, metrics, traces and logs as JSON.

  • Background work

    Scheduled jobs, a task queue, a leader and locks, shared by every process; messages to all of them, and an outbox for those a change announces.

  • Operations

    Circuit breakers, maintenance mode and feature flags that every process sees at once.

  • Security model and resilience

    What gets cached and for whom, what the backend is trusted with, and what happens when it fails.

docs.title: Tutorial - User Guide
docs.text:
This tutorial shows you how to use Alcazaba, step by step. It starts on this page with a quick start: a small shop API built in three steps, each adding one tool to the same main.py (a response cache, a rate limit and authorization with Casbin), each run and checked. The next pages take each tool in turn: read them in order, or go straight to the one you need.

Before you start

You need Python 3.11 or later, and to know FastAPI's basics: path operations, dependencies and the lifespan. If they're new to you, FastAPI's own tutorial explains them first.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Make a folder for the project, with a virtual environment, and install FastAPI and Alcazaba:

pipuv 
$ python -m venv .venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install "fastapi[standard]" "fastapi-alcazaba[casbin]"

$ uv venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ uv pip install "fastapi[standard]" "fastapi-alcazaba[casbin]"

fastapi[standard] brings the fastapi command and uvicorn, to run the app. Alcazaba itself only needs FastAPI; the casbin extra is for the third step.

docs.title: Create it
docs.text:
Create a file main.py with:

main.py
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

from fastapi_alcazaba import FastAPICache
from fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory import InMemoryBackend
from fastapi_alcazaba.response_cache import cache


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    FastAPICache.init(InMemoryBackend(), prefix="shop")
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)


class Product(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float


PRODUCTS = {1: Product(name="Olive oil", price=9.5)}


@app.get("/products/{product_id}")
@cache(expire=60)
async def read_product(product_id: int) -> Product:
    if product_id not in PRODUCTS:
        raise HTTPException(404, "No such product")
    return PRODUCTS[product_id]

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Run the development server:

$ fastapi dev main.py

 ⚡️ Starting FastAPI in development mode
