docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.authz.opa.OPAEnforcer
docs.text:
OPAEnforcer(url: str, *, rule: str = 'authz.allow', token: str | SecretStr | None = None, timeout: float = 1.0, client: AsyncClient | None = None)

An enforcer that asks Open Policy Agent, for FastAPIAuthz(enforcer) and AuthzMiddleware.

await enforce(subject, resource, action, context=None) queries rule with the input {"subject": subject, "resource": resource, "action": action, "context": context}: the subject your dependency gives (a name, or a dict with the user's attributes and roles), the path or the value of authz.require, and the method or the action. Only a result of true allows; false refuses, and so does a rule that is undefined for the input (with a warning: give it a default, default allow := false).

Fails closed: a service that doesn't answer within timeout, or answers with a 5xx, raises PolicyUnavailable, and the request gets a 503. Its own client gives each call a deadline and the service a circuit breaker (ResilientTransport): when it's down, requests are refused at once instead of each waiting for it. A query OPA refuses (a 4xx: a wrong token, an input that isn't JSON) and a result that isn't a boolean (a rule that names a package, or a rule that gives an object) raise RuntimeError, a 500: they're mistakes to fix, not refusals.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default url str

where OPA listens, http://localhost:8181 for a sidecar.

required rule str

the rule to query, as Rego references it after data.: authz.allow is the rule allow of package authz.

'authz.allow' token str | SecretStr | None

the bearer token OPA asks for, when it runs with --authentication=token.

None timeout float

seconds for each query, the answer included.

1.0 client AsyncClient | None

the httpx2 client to ask OPA with (for its TLS, its proxy, a transport of your own); one of its own by default, with a ResilientTransport. aclose() closes only its own.

None

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.backends.inmemory.InMemoryBackend
docs.text:
InMemoryBackend(max_size: int | None = 10000)

Bases: Backend

Cache in the memory of the process: for development, tests and single-process apps.

Each instance has its own store, bounded to max_size entries (the least recently used are evicted): a store that never evicted would grow with every new query string until the process ran out of memory.

State (rate-limit counters, revoked tokens, one-time codes, sessions, idempotency records: Cache.state_key) is never evicted while it lives: forgetting a revocation would accept the token again. Each kind of state has a store of its own, bounded to max_size live entries; a write to a full one raises BackendUnavailable, like Redis with noeviction, and each tool fails closed. So a flood of idempotency keys fills the idempotency records, never the revocations or the sessions.

MemcachedBackend(mcache: Client, *, max_value_size: int = 1024 * 1024 - 512)

Bases: Backend

Cached responses are stored with a stamp: their expiry, so hits know their remaining lifetime, and the generations of their namespaces and tags (see _generations), so that clear(namespace=...) and invalidate_tags hide them without listing keys. memcached can't count them: both return 0. docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.backends.dynamodb.DynamoBackend
docs.text:
DynamoBackend(table_name: str, region: str | None = None, *, endpoint_url: str | None = None)

Bases: Backend

Amazon DynamoDB backend provider

This backend requires an existing table within your AWS environment to be passed during backend init. If ttl is going to be used, this needs to be manually enabled on the table using the ttl key. Dynamo will take care of deleting outdated objects, but this is not instant so don't be alarmed when they linger around for a bit.

As with all AWS clients, credentials will be taken from the environment. Check the AWS SDK for more information.

clear(namespace=...) and invalidate_tags work without a scan: each namespace or tag that was cleared has a generation, an item of its own, and cached responses record the generations they were stored under (see _generations); a clear writes a new one, so the entries stored before it are no longer served. They can't be counted: both return 0. Reads are eventually consistent, so a clear may take a moment to be seen.

Usage: >> dynamodb = DynamoBackend(table_name="your-cache", region="eu-west-1") >> await dynamodb.init() >> FastAPICache.init(dynamodb)

endpoint_url points to DynamoDB Local, LocalStack or a VPC endpoint.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.backends.tiered.TieredBackend
docs.text:
TieredBackend(remote: Backend, *, local_ttl: int = 5, local_max_size: int = 1000, invalidation_channel: str | None = 'fastapi_alcazaba:invalidations')

Bases: Backend

Two levels: a small cache in the memory of each process in front of a shared backend.

A hit in the process skips the network. Each local copy lives at most local_ttl seconds and never longer than the shared entry, which bounds how stale it can get when another process changes the value.

With a Redis or Valkey shared backend whose client supports pub/sub (RedisBackend, ValkeyBackend; not a valkey-py cluster), writes, clears and tag invalidations are announced on invalidation_channel, and every process drops its copy right away (a tag invalidation names the keys it deleted; beyond 1000, every process drops all its copies). Local copies are only kept while the process is subscribed: when the subscription drops (and messages may have been missed), the local level is emptied and bypassed until it's back. A value read from the shared backend while an invalidation arrives isn't kept: it may be the old one.

Values are kept locally as the shared backend stores them, so signed or encrypted entries stay signed or encrypted in memory too.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.background.FastAPITaskQueue
docs.text:
FastAPITaskQueue(cache: Cache | None = None, *, name: str = 'default', concurrency: int = 10, grace: float = 10.0, poll_interval: float = 1.0, visibility_timeout: float = 60.0, max_deliveries: int = 5, max_payload_size: int = 65536, max_length: int = 100000, max_dead_letters: int = 10000, replay_window: float = 7 * 24 * 3600, status_ttl: float = 24 * 3600)

Tasks that run in the background, in any process sharing the cache's backend.

Every process enqueues; those that call start() (or use lifespan or async with) also run tasks. A worker-only process: async with queue: await asyncio.Event().wait().

Needs Redis 6.2+ or Valkey through RedisBackend or ValkeyBackend (or a TieredBackend in front of one). Its keys are state keys (Cache.state_key), which clear() never deletes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cache Cache | None

whose backend holds the queue; FastAPICache's by default, resolved when first needed.

None name str

queues with different names are independent.

'default' concurrency int

tasks run at a time by start() in this process.

10 grace float

seconds stop() waits for the tasks that are running; those still running then are cancelled and go back to the queue (a sync task's thread can't be stopped: it runs to its end, so that task may run twice).

10.0 poll_interval float

seconds between looks at the backend when there's nothing to do. A task enqueued in this process wakes its workers at once.

1.0 visibility_timeout float

seconds after which the tasks of a worker that stopped answering (its process died) are taken over by another. Running tasks are kept from it every third of it, however long they run.

60.0 max_deliveries int

times a task is handed to a worker (once, plus each time it's taken over from a worker that died) before it goes to the dead letters instead: it may be what kills them.

5 max_payload_size int

largest arguments, in bytes of JSON; anything larger is refused.

65536 max_length int

most tasks the queue holds (waiting, running or delayed); enqueue raises QueueFull beyond, instead of dropping tasks.

100000 max_dead_letters int

dead letters kept, about: the oldest go first.

10000 replay_window float

seconds a task may wait in the queue after it's due; later, it's refused as stale and goes to the dead letters (requeue_dead_letters() sends it again). Its run id is kept that long, so that a copy of it is refused.

7 * 24 * 3600 status_ttl float

seconds the status record of a task (status()) is kept after it ends; never less than its payload stays valid (replay_window): the record is what tells a dead letter from a copy of a task that ran (requeue_dead_letters).

24 * 3600

docs.text:
task(name: str | None = None, *, retries: int = 3, backoff: float = 1.0, max_backoff: float = 600.0, timeout: float | None = None, retry_on: type[BaseException] | tuple[type[BaseException], ...] | None = None, give_up_on: type[BaseException] | tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = ()) -> Callable[[F], F]

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str | None

the task's name in the queue, which travels with every task (keep it when the function moves); the function's module and name by default.

None retries int

times a task that raised is tried again: backoff seconds after the first failure, twice that after the second... up to max_backoff, each with jitter. Then it goes to the dead letters. 0: at the first failure.

3 timeout float | None

seconds a run may take; past them it's cancelled and fails with TimeoutError (retried, or to the dead letters), and its worker takes other tasks. A sync task's thread can't be stopped: it runs on, outside the count of concurrency.

None retry_on type[BaseException] | tuple[type[BaseException], ...] | None

the exceptions that are retried (all by default); any other sends the task to the dead letters at once.

docs.title: enqueue async
docs.text:
enqueue(task: Callable[..., Any] | str, /, *args: Any, delay: float | timedelta | None = None, unique_key: str | None = None, **kwargs: Any) -> str

Queue a run of task (a registered function, or its name) with these arguments, to start in delay seconds or as soon as a worker is free; returns the task's ID.

With a unique_key, while a task enqueued with it waits, runs or waits for a retry, this returns that task's ID and adds nothing: a message delivered twice, a request retried, runs once. Once it succeeds, goes to the dead letters or is cancelled, the key is free.

The arguments must fit the function and be JSON-serialisable (checked here, raising TypeError); they arrive as JSON gives them back: tuples as lists, dict keys as strings. A task can't take arguments named delay or unique_key by keyword. Raises QueueFull when the queue holds max_length tasks, and BackendUnavailable when the backend fails.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.background.FastAPIBroadcast
docs.text:
FastAPIBroadcast(client: Any = None, *, signing_key: Secrets | None = None, prefix: str = 'fastapi_alcazaba:broadcast:', queue_size: int = 1000)

Publishes messages to channels, which every process's subscribers of the channel get.

  • At most once: a message is for those subscribed when it's published; one that a subscriber's connection missed doesn't come back, it gets a gap instead. For work that must happen, a task queue or an outbox.
  • Signed: with signing_key, each message carries an HMAC of its channel and data, and those without it (planted by whoever can write to Redis) are dropped.
  • Bounded: a message has MAX_MESSAGE bytes of JSON at most, and each subscriber queue_size messages waiting: past it, it loses the oldest and gets a gap.
  • Reconnects by itself, with a backoff, and tells every subscriber of the gap.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default client Any

a redis-py or valkey-py asyncio client (the one of your RedisBackend); None to keep messages in this process.

None signing_key Secrets | None

a secret of 32 bytes or more, the same in every process (a list rotates it: the first signs, all of them verify).

None prefix str

what the channels are under in Redis.

'fastapi_alcazaba:broadcast:' queue_size int

messages a subscriber may have waiting.

1000

OutboxRelay(outbox: SQLAlchemyOutbox, deliver: Callable[[OutboxMessage], Awaitable[Any]], *, batch: int = 100, interval: float = 1.0, max_attempts: int = 10, max_delay: float = 3600, retention: float | None = 7 * 24 * 3600, purge_interval: float = 3600, purge_batch: int = 1000)

Delivers the outbox's messages, the oldest first, at least once: deliver(message) is awaited, and the message marked as sent when it returns. When it raises, the message is tried again later (1, 2, 4… seconds, up to max_delay), and given up on after max_attempts: kept with its error, never sent, until requeue or discard. Run it in one process (FastAPILeader).

Each delivery is a span (fastapi_alcazaba.outbox <topic>), the root of a trace of its own linked to the span that wrote the message; counted in fastapi_alcazaba.outbox (delivered, retried, given_up). Metrics and traces go to FastAPICache's providers when it's set up, to the global ones otherwise.

seconds the messages sent are kept; run() deletes them afterwards. None keeps them all.

docs.title: Sessions, CSRF and security headers
docs.text:
What a cookie-based app needs: server-side sessions, CSRF protection, headers and body limits. In fastapi_alcazaba.security.

In the guide: Server-side sessions, CSRF protection, Security headers and body size. In an app: the example.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.security.ServerSessionMiddleware
docs.text:
ServerSessionMiddleware(app: ASGIApp, *, cache: Cache | None = None, cookie_name: str = '__Host-session', max_age: int = 14 * 24 * 3600, idle_timeout: int | None = None, secure: bool = True, same_site: SameSite = 'lax', path: str = '/', domain: str | None = None, max_size: int = 16384, namespace: str = 'session', users: UserSessions | None = None)

ASGI middleware that keeps each browser's session in the cache's backend, under a random id carried by a cookie (HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite by default).

app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware)
  • Saved only when it changed, when the response starts; an empty session isn't stored and gets no cookie. A session emptied by the app is deleted and its cookie expired.
  • New ids are always the server's: a cookie whose session doesn't exist (expired, made up) never becomes the id of a new one. rotate_session at login, clear_session at logout.
  • Expiry: max_age seconds after the session was created (or rotated), and after idle_timeout seconds without requests. Both are checked when it's read, and the backend drops it then too.
  • Backend failures: if the session can't be read, the request goes on with an empty one (anonymous: fail closed) and a warning; a change to it, or any failure to save, rotate or clear, replaces the response with a 503 and leaves the cookie alone, since what the response says (logged in, logged out) wouldn't be true. Several requests of the same session at once: the last one to save wins, but never against a logout or a rotation: the old id leaves a mark for the rest of its life, and a request still running with it can't bring it back.
  • Sealed with the cache's signing_key or encryption_key (use the latter when sessions hold personal data). Without either, whoever can write to the backend can forge sessions: a warning is logged.
  • WebSockets get websocket.session too, read-only.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cache Cache | None

where sessions are kept; the app's (Cache.install) or FastAPICache's by default. With a TieredBackend, only its shared (remote) tier is used.

None cookie_name str

the cookie. __Host- keeps sibling subdomains from setting one (cookie tossing); it needs secure, path / and no domain: name it otherwise for plain HTTP in development.

'__Host-session' max_age int

seconds a session lasts from its creation; also the cookie's Max-Age.

14 * 24 * 3600 idle_timeout int | None

seconds without requests after which it's over; None for no limit.

None secure bool

only send the cookie over HTTPS.

True same_site SameSite

the cookie's SameSite: "lax", "strict" or "none" (needs secure).

'lax' path str

the cookie's path.

'/' domain str | None

the cookie's domain; None keeps it to the host that set it.

None max_size int

bytes of JSON a session may take; more raises ValueError when it's saved.

16384 namespace str

part of the backend keys, after the cache's prefix (Cache.state_key).

'session' users UserSessions | None

keeps each user's sessions (see UserSessions), to list them and end them, all of them at once too: sessions whose data has its user_key.

None

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.security.UserSessions
docs.text:
UserSessions(*, user_key: str = 'user_id', sid_key: str = 'oidc_sid', max_sessions: int = 50, record_client: bool = True, cache: Cache | None = None)

Each user's server sessions, to list them ("your devices") and end them: one, or all of them ("log out everywhere", a new password). Give it to the middleware:

user_sessions = UserSessions()
app.add_middleware(ServerSessionMiddleware, users=user_sessions)

await user_sessions.end_all(user.id, request=request, keep_current=True)

A session is the user's whose data has user_key (what SessionStrategy.login sets): the middleware keeps an index of each user's sessions in the backend, sealed like them, when they start, rotate and end.

  • Ending all of them also refuses, from then on, every session of the user that started before: those the index didn't hold too (two logins at once on a backend without locks, an index the backend lost). It costs one more read for each request with a user.
  • At most max_sessions per user: a login past it ends the oldest session.

  • The index holds each session's backend key (a digest: not a cookie), and its User-Agent and address when it started (record_client=False for neither).

  • Logins at an OpenID Connect provider: a session whose data has sid_key (the provider's sid of the login) can be ended by it, end_sid, which the provider's back-channel logout calls (OIDCStrategy.backchannel_logout_endpoint).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default user_key str

the key of the session's data that holds its user's ID.

'user_id' sid_key str

the key of the session's data that holds the provider's session id.

'oidc_sid' max_sessions int

sessions a user may have at once.

50 record_client bool

keep the User-Agent and the address of each session.

True cache Cache | None

where the sessions are; the request's (get_cache) by default.

None

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.security.CSRFMiddleware
docs.text:
CSRFMiddleware(app: ASGIApp, *, trusted_origins: Iterable[str] = (), exempt_paths: Iterable[str] = (), require_token: bool = False, check_all: bool = False, cookie_name: str = '__Host-csrftoken', header_name: str = 'X-CSRF-Token', cookie_secure: bool = True, cookie_domain: str | None = None)

ASGI middleware that refuses, with a 403, unsafe requests that a page on another site made the user's browser send. See the module's documentation for the rules.

app.add_middleware(CSRFMiddleware)

The app's own origin is the scheme and the Host header as the server sees them. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, let the server trust it (uvicorn --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=<proxy address>) so that the scheme is https, and have the proxy pass the Host header on; otherwise list the public origin in trusted_origins.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default trusted_origins Iterable[str]

other origins (https://admin.example.com) whose pages may send requests: sibling subdomains count as other origins, and so do identity providers and payment pages that post a form back to the app.

() exempt_paths Iterable[str]

path prefixes that aren't checked (webhooks signed in their own way). They're matched like the app's routes: without the root_path a proxy or a mount adds.

() require_token bool

also require, on requests with cookies, a header (header_name) equal to the token cookie (cookie_name) set on every response that lacks a valid one. The token is in request.state.csrf_token too. A request whose browser sends neither Origin nor Referer passes with a valid token.

False check_all bool

also check requests without cookies or HTTP authentication: for apps that trust TLS client certificates or the network (an intranet), which the browser sends too.

False cookie_name str

the token cookie. The __Host- prefix keeps sibling subdomains from setting one (cookie tossing); it needs cookie_secure and no cookie_domain.

'__Host-csrftoken' header_name str

the header that carries the token.

'X-CSRF-Token' cookie_secure bool

only send the token cookie over HTTPS.

True cookie_domain str | None

the token cookie's domain, for pages on another subdomain that need to read it (then pick a name without the __Host- prefix).

None

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.security.SecurityHeadersMiddleware
docs.text:
SecurityHeadersMiddleware(app: ASGIApp, *, headers: Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None, hsts: str | None = 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains', csp: str | None = "default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'", html_csp: str | None = None)

Adds the security headers of the OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet to every response, without overwriting the ones the app sets itself.

app.add_middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)
  • X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and a Permissions-Policy that turns off the camera, the microphone, geolocation, payments and the other powerful features on every response.
  • Strict-Transport-Security only on HTTPS requests: on plain HTTP browsers ignore it, and on a development localhost it would stick. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS, tell the server to trust it (uvicorn --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips=<proxy address>) so that the request's scheme is https.
  • Content-Security-Policy: csp for responses that aren't HTML (nothing in a JSON response should load anything), html_csp for HTML ones, None by default, so that FastAPI's Swagger UI and ReDoc, which load scripts from a CDN, keep working.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default headers Mapping[str, str | None] | None

more headers, or other values for the defaults; None removes a default.

None hsts str | None

the Strict-Transport-Security value; None leaves it out.

'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains' csp str | None

the Content-Security-Policy of responses that aren't HTML; None leaves it out.

"default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'" html_csp str | None

the Content-Security-Policy of HTML responses.

None

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.security.BodySizeLimitMiddleware
docs.text:
BodySizeLimitMiddleware(app: ASGIApp, *, max_size: int = 1048576, paths: Mapping[str, int | None] | None = None)

Refuses request bodies larger than max_size bytes with a 413. FastAPI has no limit of its own: a client could send an endless body that the app reads into memory.

app.add_middleware(BodySizeLimitMiddleware, max_size=1_048_576, paths={"/uploads": None})

A Content-Length over the limit is refused before the app runs. Bodies without one (chunked) are counted while the app reads them, and refused as soon as they pass the limit.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_size int

the limit, in bytes.

1048576 paths Mapping[str, int | None] | None

other limits for the paths starting with these prefixes (the longest matching prefix wins; None for no limit). They're matched like the app's routes: without the root_path a proxy or a mount adds in front.

None

docs.text:
Cache(backend: Backend, prefix: str = '', expire: int | None = None, coder: type[Coder] = JsonCoder, key_builder: KeyBuilder = default_key_builder, cache_status: str | None = 'Alcazaba', enable: bool = True, *, signing_key: Secrets | None = None, encryption_key: Secrets | None = None, vary_headers: Iterable[str] = DEFAULT_VARY_HEADERS, respect_cache_control: bool = False, single_flight: bool = True, backend_timeout: float | None = 1.0, circuit_breaker_failures: int | None = 5, circuit_breaker_reset: float = 30.0, max_value_size: int | None = None, distributed_lock: bool = False, lock_timeout: float = 10.0, lock_wait: float = 5.0, early_refresh: float | None = None, compression: Codec | None = None, compression_min_size: int = 1024, compression_level: int | None = None, metrics: bool = True, meter_provider: Any = None, tracing: bool = True, tracer_provider: Any = None)

A cache: a backend and its settings. Create one per app, or several (e.g. a public one and an encrypted one for personal data), and decorate with cached(); or use the global FastAPICache with @cache.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default backend Backend

where entries are stored.

required prefix str

prefix of every key.

'' expire int | None

default time to live, in seconds.

None coder type[Coder]

how values are stored (JsonCoder by default).

JsonCoder key_builder KeyBuilder

builds keys from the function and its arguments.

default_key_builder cache_status str | None

this cache's name in the responses' Cache-Status header (RFC 9211): Alcazaba; hit; ttl=42 for a hit, else why the request reached the endpoint (fwd=miss, stale, request, method, bypass) and whether the result was stored. A token (letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_|~:/`, starting with a letter); None for no header.

'Alcazaba' enable bool

False turns the cache off.

True signing_key Secrets | None

secret (at least 32 bytes; text, bytes, or pydantic's SecretStr or SecretBytes) used to sign every entry with HMAC-SHA256; entries without a valid signature are ignored. Strongly recommended when the backend is shared or reachable by others, and needed for PickleCoder (UnsignedEntriesError without it). A list of keys rotates them: the first one signs, all of them are accepted.

None encryption_key Secrets | None

like signing_key, but the entries are also encrypted (AES-256-GCM): a dump or a backup of the backend doesn't reveal the cached responses. Needs the crypto extra. Use one or the other, not both.

None vary_headers Iterable[str]

request headers that give each value its own cache entry and make the response private (see DEFAULT_VARY_HEADERS). Pass () for endpoints whose response is the same for everybody.

DEFAULT_VARY_HEADERS respect_cache_control bool

let clients skip the cache with Cache-Control: no-cache or no-store. Off by default: anyone could otherwise make every request reach the endpoint, which defeats the cache as a shield against load.

False single_flight bool

concurrent misses for the same key wait for the first one instead of all computing the value (cache stampede protection), within each process.

True backend_timeout float | None

seconds each backend call may take before the cache is skipped for that request; None waits as long as the client does.

1.0 circuit_breaker_failures int | None

consecutive backend failures after which the backend is not called for circuit_breaker_reset seconds (requests run uncached and don't wait for it); None disables the breaker.

5 max_value_size int | None

values larger than this many bytes (once encoded) aren't stored.

None distributed_lock bool

on a miss, take a lock in the backend so that a single process computes the value while the others wait for it (up to lock_wait seconds, then they compute it themselves). The lock expires after lock_timeout seconds.

False early_refresh float | None

fraction of the lifetime at its end in which a hit may recompute the value (more likely as the expiry nears), so that popular entries are refreshed before they expire instead of all callers missing at once. E.g. 0.1.

None compression Codec | None

"zstd" (Python 3.14, or the zstd extra) or "zlib": entries of at least compression_min_size bytes are stored compressed when that makes them smaller, with compression_level (the codec's default if None). Compressed entries are read back whatever this setting, so it can be turned on and off freely.

None metrics bool

record OpenTelemetry metrics (needs the otel extra).

True meter_provider Any

OpenTelemetry meter provider; the global one by default.

None tracing bool

record OpenTelemetry spans of cached calls and backend calls (otel extra).

True tracer_provider Any

OpenTelemetry tracer provider; the global one by default.

None

docs.text:
default_key_builder(func: Callable[..., Any], namespace: str = '', *, request: Request | None = None, response: Response | None = None, args: tuple[Any, ...], kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> str

namespace plus the SHA-256 of the function's module, qualified name and the repr() of its arguments.

SHA-256, not MD5, and __qualname__, not __name__, so that two methods with the same name in one module don't share their entries. Request headers that change the response, such as Authorization, are added by the decorator (vary_headers), whatever the key builder.

docs.title: Idempotency keys
docs.text:
The middleware that replays the first response to a retried request. In fastapi_alcazaba.idempotency.

In the guide: Idempotency keys. In an app: the example.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.idempotency.IdempotencyMiddleware
docs.text:
IdempotencyMiddleware(app: ASGIApp, *, cache: Cache | None = None, methods: Collection[str] = ('POST', 'PATCH'), expire: int = 86400, identifier: Identifier | None = None, max_body_size: int = 1048576, max_response_size: int = 1048576, lock_ttl: float = 60.0, fail_open: bool = False)

ASGI middleware that makes requests with an Idempotency-Key header run once.

app.add_middleware(IdempotencyMiddleware)

Requests without the header go through untouched (require_idempotency_key makes it mandatory on a route). The stored responses go through the cache's signing or encryption: use an encryption_key when they carry personal data. They're kept without Set-Cookie.

A retry gets the stored response before the route's dependencies run: authentication included. With the default identifier, whoever has a copy of the request (its token, its key) gets the response again until it expires, even after the token is revoked; an identifier that checks the credentials (async, returning the user's id, raising a 401 otherwise) closes that.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cache Cache | None

where responses and locks are kept; the app's (Cache.install) or FastAPICache's by default. Its backend must support locks.

None methods Collection[str]

the methods it applies to; PUT and DELETE are idempotent already.

('POST', 'PATCH') expire int

seconds a response is kept for retries.

86400 identifier Identifier | None

who the client is (credentials by default: the Authorization header, or the cookies). Return the user's id with tokens that get refreshed, and with cookies that change between requests: a retry sent with others would run again. Requests without credentials share one space of keys, unguessable as long as clients make them random (UUIDs).

None max_body_size int

larger request bodies get a 413: they're read whole to fingerprint them.

1048576 max_response_size int

larger responses aren't kept (a retry would run again).

1048576 lock_ttl float

seconds the lock outlives a process that dies while running the request.

60.0 fail_open bool

when the backend fails, run requests without idempotency instead of answering 503. Off by default: running a payment twice is worse than refusing it.

False

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.idempotency.credentials
docs.text:
credentials(connection: HTTPConnection) -> str

The default identifier: the request's credentials, hashed before they're stored, so that one user never gets another's response, whatever key they send: the Authorization header, or the cookies without one (a cookie session; any cookie that changes between a request and its retry makes the retry run again). Nothing for requests that carry neither.

docs.title: Integrity, resilience and errors
docs.text:
What signs and encrypts entries, RFC 8785 canonical JSON, the backends' circuit breaker, and the exceptions. In fastapi_alcazaba.core.

In the guide: Security model, Encrypted entries, Resilience.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.core.Signer
docs.text:
Signer(keys: Secrets)

Signs what the cache stores and only accepts what it signed itself.

Whoever can write to the backend (a shared Redis, a leaked password) can't plant data, nor a pickle that runs code when it's read, nor copy one user's entry under another user's key: the tag covers the key too. The first key signs; the others are only checked, so a key can be rotated without losing the cache: put the new one first and drop the old one later.

docs.title: unsign
docs.text:
unsign(cache_key: str, data: bytes) -> bytes | None

The payload, or None when data wasn't signed by us for this key.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.core.canonical_json
docs.text:
canonical_json(value: Any) -> bytes

value (dicts with string keys, lists, tuples, strings, integers, floats, booleans and None) in its canonical form, as UTF-8. Raises ValueError for what I-JSON leaves out (integers a double can't hold exactly, NaN, infinities, lone surrogates) and TypeError for what isn't JSON.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.core.Encrypter
docs.text:
Encrypter(keys: Secrets)

Encrypts what the cache stores and only accepts what it encrypted itself.

On top of what signing gives (whoever can write to the backend can't plant data, run a pickle or move one user's entry under another user's key), a dump or a backup of Redis doesn't reveal the cached responses. The cache key is the associated data, so an entry only decrypts under its own key. Each entry is encrypted with its own AES-256 key, derived with HKDF-SHA256 from the secret and a random salt, so random 96-bit nonces never get near the limits of AES-GCM however many entries are written.

The first secret encrypts; all of them decrypt, so a secret can be rotated without losing the cache: put the new one first and drop the old one later.

Layout: b"fastapi_alcazaba/e1" | key id (4) | salt (16) | nonce (12) | ciphertext and GCM tag (16).

docs.title: open
docs.text:
open(cache_key: str, data: bytes) -> bytes | None

The payload, or None when data wasn't encrypted by us for cache_key.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.core.CircuitBreaker
docs.text:
CircuitBreaker(failure_threshold: int = 5, reset_timeout: float = 30.0)

Stops calling a failing backend for a while.

Closed: calls go through, and failure_threshold consecutive failures open it. Open: calls are refused for reset_timeout seconds. Then a single trial call goes through (half open): a success closes it, a failure opens it again. One breaker per process.

docs.title: retry_after property
docs.text:
retry_after: float

Seconds until a trial call may go through; 0 unless it's open.

docs.title: allow
docs.text:
allow() -> str | None

The state the call goes through in: "closed", or "half-open" when it's the single trial; None when it's refused.

docs.title: reset
docs.text:
reset() -> None

Close it, whatever its state: the failures counted so far are forgotten.

docs.title: abandon_trial
docs.text:
abandon_trial() -> None

The trial call ended without a verdict (cancelled): let the next call try. Only for the call allow() let through "half-open": another one would let a second trial through.

docs.text: Warnings and exceptions of Alcazaba.

docs.title: UnsignedEntriesError

Bases: ValueError

A coder whose decoding can run code (PickleCoder) without a signing or encryption key: whoever can write to the backend could run code in the app.

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: Rate and concurrency limits
docs.text:
Requests per window and requests at a time, per client or shared, across processes. In fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit.

In the guide: Rate limiting, Concurrency limits. In an app: the example.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit.FastAPIRateLimiter
docs.text:
FastAPIRateLimiter(times: Limit = 1, milliseconds: int = 0, seconds: int = 0, minutes: int = 0, hours: int = 0, identifier: Identifier | None = None, callback: OnLimit | None = None, *, name: str | None = None, cache: Cache | None = None, fail_open: bool = True, cost: int = 1, headers: bool = True, exempt: Exemption | None = None)

FastAPI dependency that lets each client make times requests per window to a route; the next ones get a 429 with Retry-After until the window slides past enough of them.

@app.get("/search", dependencies=[Depends(FastAPIRateLimiter(times=10, minutes=1))])

The counters live in the cache's backend (the cache given, else the one get_cache returns), so every process shares them, and go through its timeout and circuit breaker. Their keys are SHA-256 digests: identities never reach the backend in clear.

It's a sliding window: the count of the previous window is added in proportion to how much of it is still less than a window ago, so no client doubles its rate around the boundary between two windows. That assumes the previous window's requests were spread evenly; when they came at its end, it's a little stricter than times per window. Requests over the limit don't count: checking and counting is one atomic operation where the backend allows it. Each process then refuses a client with nothing left without asking the backend, until something fits again, so a flood doesn't reach the backend.

Responses carry the RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers of the IETF draft (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers), for clients to slow down before they get a 429.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default times Limit

requests allowed per window; or a function of the request (sync or async) that says how many, e.g. by the user's plan. The count is kept whatever it says: a client whose plan changes keeps what it spent.

1 milliseconds int

the window is the sum of milliseconds, seconds, minutes and hours.

0 identifier Identifier | None

who the client is; its address by default (client_ip). E.g. a user id.

None callback OnLimit | None

called with the request and the seconds to wait when a request is over the limit; too_many_requests by default. If it returns, the request goes on.

None name str | None

the routes using limiters with this name and the same rate share one budget; by default each route (its methods and path template) has its own. Also the policy's name in the headers.

None cache Cache | None

the Cache whose backend keeps the counters.

None fail_open bool

when the backend fails, let requests through (the default, as the cache does) or refuse them with a 503.

True cost int

how much of the budget each request takes: an expensive route can take more of a budget it shares with others (name).

1 headers bool

send the RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers.

True exempt Exemption | None

who isn't limited: identities (as identifier returns them: an internal service's address, an admin's id), or a predicate of the request (sync or async). Their requests aren't counted nor get the headers; each is counted as exempt in the metrics, and logged the first time this process sees the identity.

None

docs.title: forget
docs.text:
forget() -> None

Forget the clients this process refuses without asking the backend (those with nothing left): their next requests ask it again. The counters in the backend stay. It's done by itself when the cache changes, as each test's lifespan sets one up.

docs.title: hit async
docs.text:
hit(connection: HTTPConnection, key: str = '', cost: int | None = None) -> float | None

Count a request: None if it's within the limit, else the seconds until it would be (and it isn't counted). Call it yourself to limit something else than whole requests: each message of a WebSocket, or the login attempts to an account (key=username). cost is how much of the budget it takes (the limiter's cost by default).

docs.title: reset async
docs.text:
reset(connection: HTTPConnection | None = None, *, identity: str | None = None, key: str = '', cache: Cache | None = None) -> None

Forget what a client spent: after a successful login, the failed attempts (key=account). The client is the request's (identifier), or identity; without a request, the limiter needs a name (its budget is the route's otherwise), and a cache. Other processes that refuse the client without asking the backend (it had nothing left) go on doing so until that budget would have refilled.

docs.title: status async
docs.text:
status(connection: HTTPConnection | None = None, *, identity: str | None = None, key: str = '', cache: Cache | None = None) -> RateLimitStatus

A client's budget without spending any: its limit, what fits now, and for how long no more is sure to fit. The client as for reset. Raises BackendUnavailable when the backend fails.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit.client_ip
docs.text:
client_ip(connection: HTTPConnection) -> str

The client's address as the ASGI server reports it, IPv6 addresses by their /64 network: that's what an ISP gives a single customer, who can use any of its 2⁶⁴ addresses. docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.rate_limit.FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter
docs.text:
FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter(limit: int, *, name: str | None = None, identifier: Identifier | None = None, wait: float = 0.0, ttl: float = 60.0, cache: Cache | None = None, fail_open: bool = True, retry_after: int = 1)

FastAPI dependency (with yield) that lets at most limit requests run at the same time; the slot is released when the request is done (see the module's docstring for streaming).

@app.post("/summaries", dependencies=[Depends(FastAPIConcurrencyLimiter(8, wait=5))])

The slots live in the cache's backend (the cache given, else the one get_cache returns), so every process shares them. Their keys are SHA-256 digests: identities never reach the backend in clear.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default limit int

requests that may run at the same time, 1 to MAX_LIMIT.

required name str | None

routes whose limiters have this name and the same limit share the slots; by default each route (its methods and path template) has its own. Needed by slot() outside requests.

None identifier Identifier | None

who the client is (e.g. client_ip, or a user id): each one gets limit slots of its own, and is refused with a 429 instead of a 503. None: every client shares them.

None wait float

seconds to wait for a slot when they're all taken; 0 tries once.

0.0 ttl float

seconds after which the slot of a process that died is freed; renewed every ttl / 3 seconds while the request runs.

60.0 cache Cache | None

the Cache whose backend keeps the slots.

None fail_open bool

when the backend fails, count the slots in each process instead (so at most limit per process run; the default), or refuse requests with a 503.

True retry_after int

the Retry-After of refused requests, in seconds.

1

docs.text:
slot(key: str = '', *, connection: HTTPConnection | None = None) -> AsyncIterator[None]

Hold a slot around a block, outside a dependency:

    await render(report)

key gives each value its own limit slots. With a connection, the route and the identifier apply as in the dependency; without one, the limiter needs a name. Raises ConcurrencyLimitExceeded when no slot frees within wait seconds, and BackendUnavailable when the backend fails and fail_open is False.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.observability.FastAPIProblemDetails
docs.text:
FastAPIProblemDetails(*, expose_detail: bool = True, max_errors: int = 100)

Answers errors with RFC 9457 problem details. install(app) handles:

  • HTTPException (FastAPI's and Starlette's, and subclasses such as BreakerOpen and Problem), keeping its headers (Retry-After, WWW-Authenticate...). A 4xx's detail is sent, since it's written for clients (expose_detail=False keeps it); a 5xx's never is, except a Problem's. Codes under 400 (redirects raised as exceptions) keep FastAPI's answer.
  • RequestValidationError: a 422 whose errors list each error's loc, msg and type, never its input (which echoes what was sent, passwords included) nor its ctx.

  • any other exception: a 500 that says nothing about it. Starlette raises the exception again after the response, so that the server logs it with its traceback (uvicorn's "Exception in ASGI application") and TestClient raises it in tests (raise_server_exceptions=False to see the response). With debug=True, Starlette answers with its traceback page instead.

    FastAPIProblemDetails().install(app)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default expose_detail bool

send the detail of 4xx HTTPExceptions.

True max_errors int

validation errors listed at most, so that a huge invalid body doesn't get a huge answer.

100

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.observability.request_id
docs.text:
A request ID for every request, to find all the log lines of one request and to let a client quote it when it reports an error.

app.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware)  # last: the outermost

handler.addFilter(RequestIDLogFilter())  # then "%(request_id)s" in the format

RequestIDMiddleware takes the ID from the request's X-Request-ID (set by a proxy or the client) when it's safe to log, else makes a random one; request_id() returns it anywhere while the request is handled, and the response carries it in the same header. An incoming ID is reused only if it matches [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}: anything else (line breaks that would forge log lines, an endless value) gets a new one.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.observability.RequestTimeoutMiddleware
docs.text:
RequestTimeoutMiddleware(app: ASGIApp, *, timeout: float | None = 30.0, paths: Mapping[str, float | None] | None = None)

Gives every HTTP request timeout seconds, from its arrival until its response has been sent; WebSockets and lifespan events go through untouched.

app.add_middleware(RequestTimeoutMiddleware, timeout=30, paths={"/exports": None})
  • Out of time before the response starts: the app is cancelled and the client gets a 504 with a small JSON body.
  • Out of time while a response streams: too late for a 504. The app is cancelled and the exception (a TimeoutError) raised again, so that the server closes the connection: the client sees an incomplete body, never a short one that looks complete. Give streaming endpoints (Server-Sent Events, big exports) their own limit in paths, or None.
  • Once the response has been sent, background tasks have no deadline.
  • Sync endpoints run in a thread that can't be interrupted: the client gets its 504 on time, but the thread runs to its end, after the exit of its yield dependencies has run. Endpoints that may hit the deadline are better async.

Both cases are logged as warnings.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default timeout float | None

the deadline, in seconds; None for none.

30.0 paths Mapping[str, float | None] | None

other deadlines for the paths starting with these prefixes (the longest matching prefix wins; None for none), matched like the app's routes: without the root_path a proxy or a mount adds in front.

None

offsets = PaginationOffset()

@app.get("/products")
@cache(expire=60)
async def products(params: Annotated[OffsetParams, Depends(offsets)]) -> OffsetPage[Item]:
    rows = ...  # ORDER BY id LIMIT params.limit OFFSET params.offset
    return offsets.paginate(rows, params, total=...)  # SELECT count(*)

docs.text:
PaginationRange(*, default_items: int = 50, max_items: int = 100)

Pagination by range: ?start=0&end=24, both included.

ranges = PaginationRange()

@app.get("/contacts")
@cache(expire=60)
async def contacts(params: Annotated[RangeParams, Depends(ranges)]) -> RangePage[Contact]:
    count = ...  # SELECT count(*)
    rows = ...  # ORDER BY name LIMIT params.limit OFFSET params.offset
    return ranges.paginate(rows, params, total=count)

The response says which items it holds in Content-Range: items 0-24/319 (items */319 when it holds none), on top of the page's start, end and total. A range that ends before it starts, or holds more than max_items items, is a 400; one that starts past the last item a 416, with Content-Range: items */<total>.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.cursor.PaginationCursor
docs.text:
PaginationCursor(secret: Secrets, *, ttl: int | None = None, default_limit: int = 50, max_limit: int = 100)

Pagination by cursor, in both directions: ?limit=20, then ?cursor=<next_cursor> for the next page or ?cursor=<prev_cursor> for the one before.

cursors = PaginationCursor(settings.cursor_secret)

@app.get("/events")
@cache(expire=60)
async def events(params: Annotated[CursorParams, Depends(cursors)]) -> CursorPage[Event]:
    rows = ...  # WHERE (created_at, id) > params.after ORDER BY ... LIMIT params.fetch,
    # or WHERE (created_at, id) < params.before ORDER BY ... DESC LIMIT params.fetch
    return cursors.paginate(rows, params, key=lambda e: (e.created_at, e.id), queried=True)

A cursor holds the sort key of the first or last item of a page, a digest of the request's other query parameters and when it was issued, signed with HMAC-SHA256. A cursor that a client made or changed, that comes with other query parameters than the ones it was issued for (the next page of genre=poetry asked with genre=novel), or that is older than ttl, is a 400 before the endpoint runs. limit may change from one page to the next. Cursors are base64, not encrypted: a client can read the sort key in them, so sort by what it may see.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default secret Secrets

at least 32 bytes (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process; a list rotates them, the first one signing and all of them accepted.

required ttl int | None

seconds a cursor is accepted for, from when its page was made; None for ever.

None default_limit int

items per page when the request doesn't say.

50 max_limit int

the most a request may ask for (a 422 beyond).

100

The page of items that params asks for, in the list's order whichever the direction, with the cursors of the pages around it, bound to the same query parameters.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default key Callable[[T], Position]

an item's sort key: a unique value or tuple ((e.created_at, e.id), not e.created_at alone, which two items may share).

False queried bool

The extra row tells whether there's another page that way; the other way, a page reached by a cursor takes there to be one, the page it came from. Otherwise items is the whole list, sorted by key, and the page is found in it.

docs.text:
PaginationKeyset(sort: type[CursorValue] | Sequence[type[CursorValue]], *, default_limit: int = 50, max_limit: int = 100)

Pagination by keyset, with the keys in plain sight: ?limit=20, then ?after=<after>&limit=20.

messages = PaginationKeyset(sort=int)  # by id: ?after=42

@app.get("/messages")
@cache(expire=60)
async def list_messages(
    params: Annotated[KeysetParams, Depends(messages)],
) -> KeysetPage[Message]:
    rows = ...  # WHERE id > params.after ORDER BY id LIMIT params.fetch
    return messages.paginate(rows, params, key=lambda m: m.id, queried=True)

events = PaginationKeyset(sort=(datetime, int))  # ?after=["2026-10-29T10:00:00Z",42]

The page gives the last item's key as after, and a client can as well start after a key of its own (the events after a date). Keys are neither encoded nor signed, so sort by what clients may see. Each value is converted to the type sort declares, and a value of another type, another number of them or JSON that doesn't parse is a 400, before the endpoint runs.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default sort type[CursorValue] | Sequence[type[CursorValue]]

Types: int, float, str, bool, datetime (with a time zone), date, UUID or Decimal; in JSON, datetimes and dates in ISO 8601, UUIDs and decimals as strings (which keep every digit of a decimal), the rest as themselves.

items per page when the request doesn't say.

50 max_limit int

the most a request may ask for (a 422 beyond).

100

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.scroll.PaginationScroll
docs.text:
PaginationScroll(item_type: type[T], secret: Secrets, *, default_batch_size: int = 100, max_batch_size: int = 1000, keep_alive: int = 60, max_items: int = 10000, cache: Cache | None = None, namespace: str = 'scroll')

Bases: Generic[T]

Pagination by scroll: ?batch_size=100 keeps what the query found as a snapshot in the cache's backend and answers its first batch, then ?scroll_id=<scroll_id> the next one.

scroll = PaginationScroll(Order, secret=settings.scroll_secret)

@app.get("/orders/export")
async def export(params: Annotated[ScrollParams, Depends(scroll)]) -> ScrollPage[Order]:
    if params.scroll_id is None:
        return await scroll.start(await find_orders(), params)
    return await scroll.next(params)

The batches are what was found when the scroll started, whatever is written meanwhile. The snapshot lasts keep_alive seconds after each batch; once it has expired, its scroll_id is a 404 and the client starts again. A scroll_id is signed (HMAC-SHA256) and holds the snapshot's id and where the next batch starts, so a retried request gets the same batch.

The snapshot is one entry under Cache.state_key, which the cache's clear() leaves alone, in the shared tier of a TieredBackend, and sealed with the cache's signing_key or encryption_key (the latter when it holds personal data). Whoever has a scroll_id reads the rest of the snapshot without the endpoint's query running again: when the results depend on who asks, pass owner (the user's id) to start and next, and a scroll_id is only good for them. Each batch reads the whole snapshot from the backend and writes it back to renew it: keep max_items modest.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default item_type type[T]

the type of the items, which writes them into the snapshot as JSON and reads them back (a pydantic model, a dataclass...).

required secret Secrets

at least 32 bytes (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)), the same in every process; a list rotates them, the first one signing and all of them accepted.

required default_batch_size int

items per batch when the request doesn't say.

100 max_batch_size int

the most a request may ask for (a 422 beyond).

1000 keep_alive int

seconds the snapshot lasts after its last batch.

60 max_items int

the most a snapshot holds: more is a ValueError at start.

10000 cache Cache | None

the Cache whose backend keeps the snapshots; FastAPICache's by default, resolved at each call.

None namespace str

part of the keys, after the cache's prefix (see Cache.state_key).

'scroll'

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.pagination.streaming.PaginationStreaming
docs.text:
PaginationStreaming(*, batch_size: int = 100, max_items: int | None = None)

Every item, as they come, without pages: not a dependency, but a response.

stream = PaginationStreaming(batch_size=100)

@app.get("/events")
async def events() -> StreamingResponse:
    async def fetch(after: int | None, limit: int) -> list[Event]:
        ...  # WHERE id > :after ORDER BY id LIMIT :limit
    return stream.response(stream.batches(fetch, key=lambda e: e.id))

The response is NDJSON (application/x-ndjson): one JSON value per line, sent in chunks of batch_size lines, so that a client starts reading while the rest is being queried. A client that disconnects stops it. Nothing is cached: @cache doesn't keep streams.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default batch_size int

lines in each chunk of the response, and rows in each query of batches().

100 max_items int | None

the most items a response sends: it ends there, whatever is left. None for no end.

None

A response that sends items as NDJSON, models serialised with pydantic.

a list, a generator, or an async iterable (an async generator, batches()). A synchronous one is read in the thread pool, batch_size items at a time. The response closes it when it's done, or at max_items.

docs.title: batches async
docs.text:
batches(fetch: Callable[[K | None, int], Iterable[T] | Awaitable[Iterable[T]]], *, key: Callable[[T], K]) -> AsyncIterator[T]

Every row of a big table, read batch_size rows at a time by key, without loading it whole: fetch(None, batch_size) first, then fetch(key(last row), batch_size), until a batch comes back shorter than batch_size. Each query finds its batch through an index, as fast as the first, and rows written meanwhile don't shift the batches.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fetch Callable[[K | None, int], Iterable[T] | Awaitable[Iterable[T]]]

fetch(after, limit), synchronous (run in the thread pool) or async: up to limit rows whose key is past after (all of them when None), in key order (WHERE id > :after ORDER BY id LIMIT :limit).

required key Callable[[T], K]

a row's sort key, unique ((r.created_at, r.id), not r.created_at alone).

Raises ValueError if fetch returns a batch whose last key is the one it was given: it isn't reading past it, and the same rows would come back for ever.

docs.text:
page_query(statement: SelectT, params: OffsetParams | PageNumberParams | RangeParams | CursorParams | KeysetParams, *, by: Sequence[Column] = (), descending: bool = False) -> SelectT

statement limited to the page of params.

By position (OffsetParams, PageNumberParams, RangeParams): OFFSET and LIMIT, in the order statement already has, or the one by gives. OffsetParams fetch one row more, which PaginationOffset.paginate(..., queried=True) takes to tell whether there's a next page; with total= it leaves the extra row out.

By key (CursorParams, KeysetParams): by is the sort key, unique as a whole ((Event. created_at, Event.id)), and the statement must have no ORDER BY of its own. The rows past params.after, in the order of by (descending for newest first), or for a previous page those before params.before in the reverse order, nearest first, as paginate(..., queried=True) expects them; one more than the limit in either case.

docs.title: Checking uploads
docs.text:
The type of a file from its bytes, its size and pixels, safe file names, and signed URLs and upload forms for object storage. In fastapi_alcazaba.uploads.

In the guide: Checking uploads, Object storage. In an app: the example.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.uploads.FastAPIUploads
docs.text:
FastAPIUploads(types: str | Collection[str], *, max_size: int = 10 * 1024 * 1024, max_pixels: int | None = 40000000, metrics: Metrics | None = None, scanner: Scanner | None = None, scan_timeout: float = 30.0, scan_fail_open: bool = False, on_infected: Callable[[UploadFile, ScanResult], Awaitable[None] | None] | None = None)

Checks uploaded files: their type from their bytes, their size and, for images, their dimensions. Use it as a dependency for a form field named file, or call check():

uploads = FastAPIUploads(types={"application/pdf"}, max_size=20 * 1024 * 1024)

@app.post("/invoices")
async def invoice(upload: Annotated[CheckedFile, Depends(uploads)]) -> Invoice: ...

@app.post("/albums")
async def album(photos: list[UploadFile]) -> Album:
    checked = [await photo_uploads.check(photo) for photo in photos]

The upload is read in chunks and counted, whatever UploadFile.size says. By the time an endpoint runs, the multipart parser has already stored the whole request, so keep its size down with BodySizeLimitMiddleware on the route as well.

It doesn't look inside the files, but a scanner does (ClamAV, ClamAVScanner): it runs on each file that passed the other checks. One it finds infected gets a 422 ("File rejected", never the threat's name, which is logged); when it can't scan (down, too slow), the upload gets a 503, unless scan_fail_open. A scanner only knows the malware it has signatures for: a PDF can still carry scripts, an Office document macros (the macro-enabled types are told apart from the others), ZIP and GZIP archives may expand to far more than their size, and the frames of a GIF aren't counted. HTML, SVG and XML run scripts in a browser: allow them only to serve them from another domain, as attachments.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default types str | Collection[str]

the types accepted, from KNOWN_TYPES (IMAGES, OFFICE_DOCUMENTS...).

required max_size int

the largest file accepted, in bytes; larger ones get a 413.

10 * 1024 * 1024 max_pixels int | None

the most pixels (width × height) an image may have; more gets a 413. None for no limit. Images whose dimensions can't be read get a 415 either way.

40000000 metrics Metrics | None

where to count the outcomes (fastapi_alcazaba.uploads); FastAPICache's by default.

None scanner Scanner | None

scans each file that passed the other checks (ClamAVScanner, or anything with async scan(file) -> ScanResult).

None scan_timeout float

seconds the scanner may take; past them, it couldn't scan.

30.0 scan_fail_open bool

when the scanner can't scan, accept the file (counted as unscanned, logged) instead of a 503.

False on_infected Callable[[UploadFile, ScanResult], Awaitable[None] | None] | None

on_infected(file, result), sync or async, before the 422: to keep the file in quarantine, alert someone. What it raises is logged; the file is refused anyway.

None

safe_filename(name: str | None, *, default: str = 'file', max_length: int = 255) -> str

check_uploaded(uploads: FastAPIUploads, presigner: S3Presigner, key: str, *, move_to: str, filename: str | None = None, client: AsyncClient | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0) -> CheckedFile

The object key, read back from the bucket, checked by uploads (type, size, pixels, scanner) and moved to move_to: copied only while it's still the object read (its ETag), with the type found in its bytes as its Content-Type, and deleted from key. Give clients URLs for key only, and serve move_to: what's there was checked.

When it fails the checks, it's deleted and the HTTPException goes on (413, 415, 422); when it was replaced while it was checked, deleted too, with a 409. When it couldn't be scanned (503), it stays at key: check it again later. A 404 when there's no such object, a 502 when the service doesn't answer as it should.

Up to uploads.max_size + 1 bytes are read: more is "too large" without reading the rest. The returned CheckedFile's file holds the bytes read (in memory up to 1 MiB, then on disk): close it (await checked.file.close()) when done.

the name to check and show (safe_filename); the key's last part by default.

docs.title: Webhooks and outbound calls
docs.text:
Webhooks in (Standard Webhooks, GitHub, Stripe, Slack) and out, and httpx transports with deadlines, breakers and SSRF checks. In fastapi_alcazaba.webhooks and fastapi_alcazaba.outbound.

In the guide: Signed webhooks, Outbound calls. In an app: the example.

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.webhooks.FastAPIWebhooks
docs.text:
FastAPIWebhooks(secret: WebhookSecrets, *, scheme: Scheme = 'standard', tolerance: int = 300, cache: Cache | None = None, max_body_size: int = 1048576, namespace: str = 'webhook', fail_open: bool = False)

FastAPI dependency that accepts only webhooks signed with secret, and each delivery once.

webhooks = FastAPIWebhooks(settings.webhook_secret)

@app.post("/webhooks")
async def receive(message: Annotated[WebhookMessage, Depends(webhooks)]) -> None: ...

It reads the raw body (up to max_body_size bytes, a 413 beyond) and leaves it in the request, for message.json() or await request.json(). Validate it there, not with a pydantic body parameter: FastAPI reads and validates those before any dependency, without the size limit and before the signature is checked. It can't read a body the endpoint takes as a form, which consumes it first (Slack's slash commands come as a form: read await request.form() after the dependency, from the body it kept).

Missing or malformed headers get a 400; a wrong signature, a timestamp more than tolerance seconds away from the server's clock (either way) and a delivery accepted before all get the same 401, which doesn't say which check failed.

Replays: each delivery accepted (its id and timestamp, hashed) is counted in the cache's backend until its timestamp can't be accepted anymore, so every process refuses it again. A retry of the sender has a new timestamp and signature and goes through: senders keep the id of a message for all its attempts, and a retry after a failed (5xx) attempt must get through. So make the endpoint idempotent on message.id (a unique constraint), if a message must not be processed twice. GitHub signs no time: its deliveries are refused again only for the same window, and a capture sent later goes through. Whoever can write to the backend can delete the marks (and allow a replay within tolerance): keep it out of reach.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default secret WebhookSecrets

what the sender signs with. Standard Webhooks: whsec_<base64>, the base64 alone or raw bytes (at least 24 bytes once decoded), or whpk_<base64>, the sender's Ed25519 public key (v1a). GitHub, Stripe (whsec_..., used as it is), Slack: the string they give, at least 16 characters. A list rotates them: any of them verifies.

required scheme Scheme

the sender's: "standard" (Standard Webhooks: Svix, Supabase, Clerk, Resend, OpenAI...), "github" (X-Hub-Signature-256), "stripe" (Stripe-Signature), "slack" (X-Slack-Signature).

'standard' tolerance int

seconds a timestamp may be away from the server's clock, either way.

300 cache Cache | None

the Cache whose backend counts the deliveries (it must support counters); the app's (Cache.install) or FastAPICache's by default.

None max_body_size int

larger bodies get a 413 without being read to the end.

1048576 namespace str

part of the keys, after the cache's prefix (see Cache.state_key).

'webhook' fail_open bool

when the backend fails, accept the (correctly signed) webhook without the replay check instead of answering 503. Off by default: senders retry a 503 later, while a replay would run its effects again.

False

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.outbound.ResilientTransport
docs.text:
ResilientTransport(transport: AsyncBaseTransport | None = None, *, timeout: float | None = 10.0, failure_threshold: int | None = 5, reset_timeout: float = 30.0, failure_statuses: Collection[int] = (500, 502, 503, 504), max_response_size: int | None = None, metrics: Metrics | None = None)

Bases: AsyncBaseTransport

An httpx transport that gives every call a deadline and every origin a circuit breaker.

client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=ResilientTransport(timeout=5), base_url=...)

Responses are read whole within the deadline before they're returned, so don't stream large downloads through it; max_response_size bounds what it reads.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default transport AsyncBaseTransport | None

the transport that sends the requests; httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport() by default (pass your own for its verify, limits, proxy...).

None timeout float | None

seconds for the whole call, from sending the request to the last byte of the response; httpx.TimeoutException beyond. It applies to each request the transport sends: with follow_redirects, every hop gets a deadline of its own. None for no deadline (httpx's own timeouts still apply).

10.0 failure_threshold int | None

consecutive failures of an origin (scheme, host and port) after which it isn't called for reset_timeout seconds; then a single trial call decides whether it's back. Transport errors and timeouts count; errors of the caller's own (an illegal header value, an unsupported URL scheme, a request body that raises) don't. None disables the breaker.

5 reset_timeout float

seconds an open breaker refuses calls.

30.0 failure_statuses Collection[int]

response statuses that count as failures, besides errors and timeouts. The response is still returned.

(500, 502, 503, 504) max_response_size int | None

bytes of response body read at most, as they come (before Content-Encoding is decoded); ResponseTooLargeError beyond, which isn't a failure of the origin. None for no limit.

None metrics Metrics | None

where to count breakers opening and refusing calls (fastapi_alcazaba.outbound.breaker); FastAPICache's by default.

None

docs.title: fastapi_alcazaba.outbound.SSRFGuardTransport
docs.text:
SSRFGuardTransport(transport: InnerTransport | None = None, *, allow: Iterable[AllowedDestination] = (), ports: Collection[int] | None = None, max_hosts: int = 100, metrics: Metrics | None = None)

Bases: AsyncBaseTransport

An httpx transport that only calls the public internet: no private, loopback, link-local (cloud metadata), multicast or reserved addresses, whatever the URL says.

client = httpx.AsyncClient(transport=ResilientTransport(SSRFGuardTransport()))

It resolves the host itself and refuses the request (BlockedDestinationError) if any of its addresses isn't public, IPv6 forms of IPv4 addresses (::ffff:127.0.0.1, NAT64, 6to4) and numeric spellings (2130706433, 0x7f.1) included. Then it connects to the address it checked: the URL is rewritten to it, the Host header keeps the name, and TLS gets the name for SNI and the certificate check. A DNS server that answers a public address to the check and a private one to the connection (DNS rebinding) gets nowhere. Each hop of a redirect comes through the transport again and is checked like the first.

Wrap it in ResilientTransport rather than the other way round: the deadline then covers the DNS lookup, and each breaker is per host name. Give the transport to the client, not as one of its mounts, and give the client no proxy: those requests wouldn't go through it. A proxy in the inner transport is refused: it would connect on its own (an egress proxy that filters destinations, such as Smokescreen, is the alternative to this transport, not its companion).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default transport InnerTransport | None

what sends the requests. By default each host name gets an httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport of its own, sharing one SSL context: connections are pooled by address, and two names on the same address (a CDN, a shared host) must not share one, whose certificate was checked for the other name. Pass a function returning a transport (e.g. lambda: httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(http2=True)) to make them yourself, or a transport (a mock in tests), to send everything through it.

None allow Iterable[AllowedDestination]

host names (exact, or *.example.com for its subdomains), networks and addresses that may be reached although they aren't public, e.g. an internal service: allow=["billing.internal", "10.1.2.0/24"]. Requests to them are still pinned to the address checked.

() ports Collection[int] | None

the only ports allowed (ports=(443,)); None for any.

None max_hosts int

host names with a transport of their own kept open at most (the least recently used ones without an open response are closed).

100 metrics Metrics | None

where to count refused requests (fastapi_alcazaba.outbound.ssrf.blocked); FastAPICache's by default.

None

docs.title: check async
docs.text:
check(url: URL | str, *, timeout: float | None = 5.0) -> None

Check url as a request to it would be, without sending anything: its scheme, its port and every address its host resolves to (within timeout seconds). Raises BlockedDestinationError when a request would be refused, and httpx.ConnectError when the host doesn't resolve. For a URL that users give (a webhook's endpoint), when they give it; every request is checked again all the same, as DNS answers change.

SSRFGuardTransport didn't send the request: its scheme, port or address isn't allowed. A limit of the client, like ResponseTooLargeError: it isn't counted against the origin.

docs.title: Get help
docs.text:
Questions, bugs and ideas go to the repository's issues, each with its own form:

  • A bug: what happened and what you expected, a minimal example to reproduce it, the versions of fastapi-alcazaba, Python, FastAPI and Pydantic, and the backend.
  • A feature: the problem it would solve before what you propose, and whether it could serve one user's data to another or trust data from the backend.

Search the open and closed issues first: somebody may have asked already.

Vulnerabilities

Don't open an issue for a vulnerability: report it privately, through a security advisory. The security policy says what to include and what happens next.

docs.title: Help Alcazaba
docs.text:
• Star the repository, so that others find it.
  • Tell what went wrong: a bug report with a way to reproduce it is already half the fix.
  • Improve the documentation: a page that didn't answer your question, an example that could be clearer.
  • Send a pull request: Development - Contributing tells how to set up the repository and run the checks.
